- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

`chain.ts` gains the two unknown cases of `RelayResult` on top of Task 1's re-export; the relayer's
lookup returns the final height it read once that height is above the delegate's `maxBlockHeight`,
and null while it is not or cannot be read (the lookup then goes on); `InFlight` keeps, for each
held buyer, the last height at which its payment may take effect; and `answerRelay` always holds the
buyer until `max_block_height + EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS`, then lets the lookup's final height lift the
hold if it is already above.

`apps/gateway/src/chain.ts`:

```typescript
import type { BuyerView, DecodedSignedDelegate, PoolView, TxOutcome } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';

export type { ReceiptOutcome, TxOutcome } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';

/** An access key as the gateway needs it. */
export interface AccessKeyInfo {
  nonce: bigint;
  fullAccess: boolean;
}

/** The latest final block. */
export interface BlockInfo {
  height: bigint;
  timestampMs: number;
}

/** Everything the gateway reads from the chain. */
export interface ChainReader {
  getPool(poolId: number): Promise<PoolView | null>;
  listPools(from: number, limit: number): Promise<PoolView[]>;
  getBuyer(poolId: number, accountId: string): Promise<BuyerView | null>;
  ftBalanceOf(accountId: string): Promise<bigint>;
  /** null when the account has no such key. */
  accessKey(accountId: string, publicKey: string): Promise<AccessKeyInfo | null>;
  finalBlock(): Promise<BlockInfo>;
  getToken(): Promise<string>;
}

/**
 * The result of submitting a transaction.
 * - `executed`: the RPC returned the outcome once every non-refund receipt had run (some may have
 *   failed).
 * - `unknown`: the transaction was sent but its result was not known in time. `expired` is true when
 *   the lookup stopped on a final block above the delegate's `maxBlockHeight`, whose height is
 *   `finalHeight`: the delegate can no longer be included, but one included by its `maxBlockHeight`
 *   may still have receipts to run. False when the lookup's time ran out first, and for a call that
 *   relays no delegate.
 * - `rejected`: the RPC refused the transaction, so nothing ran.
 */
export type RelayResult =
  | { kind: 'executed'; outcome: TxOutcome }
  | { kind: 'unknown'; txHash: string; expired: false }
  | { kind: 'unknown'; txHash: string; expired: true; finalHeight: bigint }
  | { kind: 'rejected'; txHash: string; error: string };

/**
 * A payment is `expired` unless its `maxBlockHeight` is more than this many blocks past the final
 * height, so that the relayed transaction can land before the delegate expires. The upper bound,
 * the offer's timeout in blocks, allows the same margin.
 */
export const EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS = 5n;

/**
 * Thrown by `relayDelegate` when the chain's final height is already too close to the delegate's
 * `maxBlockHeight` for a relayed transaction to land in time. Nothing was sent.
 */
export class DelegateExpiredError extends Error {
  override name = 'DelegateExpiredError';
}

/** Everything the gateway submits, all signed by the relayer account. */
export interface ChainWriter {
  /**
   * Wraps a signed delegate action in a transaction to its sender and submits it. Resolves with the
   * result once it is known, or with `unknown` once the lookup's deadline passes without one. Throws
   * only before anything is sent: DelegateExpiredError when the final height is within EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS of
   * `maxBlockHeight`, or the error of a failed read or key wait.
   */
  relayDelegate(signed: DecodedSignedDelegate, maxBlockHeight: bigint): Promise<RelayResult>;
  /** Calls `settle` or `refund` on the pools contract with no deposit. Throws only before anything is sent. */
  callPools(method: 'settle' | 'refund', args: Record<string, unknown>, gas: bigint): Promise<RelayResult>;
}
```

`apps/gateway/src/relayer.ts`:

```typescript
import { setTimeout as delay } from 'node:timers/promises';
import type { DecodedSignedDelegate } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { Account, KeyPairSigner, actions, baseEncode, type Action, type KeyPair, type Provider } from 'near-api-js';
import {
  ActionExecutionError,
  InvalidTransactionError,
  RequestValidationError,
  TransactionExecutionError,
} from 'near-api-js/rpc-errors';
import { DelegateExpiredError, EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS, type ChainWriter, type RelayResult, type TxOutcome } from './chain.ts';
import { toTxOutcome } from './outcome.ts';

/** A key on loan from the pool. Release it exactly once. */
export interface KeyLease {
  keyPair: KeyPair;
  release(): void;
}

/** The relayer's access keys. Each key signs one transaction at a time, so nonces never clash. */
export class KeyPool {
  readonly #size: number;
  readonly #free: KeyPair[];
  readonly #waiters: Array<(lease: KeyLease) => void> = [];

  constructor(keys: KeyPair[]) {
    if (keys.length === 0) throw new Error('KeyPool needs at least one key');
    this.#size = keys.length;
    this.#free = [...keys];
  }

  get size(): number {
    return this.#size;
  }

  /** Waits for a free key, first come first served. Rejects after `timeoutMs` (default 30 s). */
  acquire(timeoutMs = 30_000): Promise<KeyLease> {
    const keyPair = this.#free.shift();
    if (keyPair) return Promise.resolve(this.#lease(keyPair));
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const waiter = (lease: KeyLease): void => {
        clearTimeout(timer);
        resolve(lease);
      };
      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
        const index = this.#waiters.indexOf(waiter);
        if (index !== -1) this.#waiters.splice(index, 1);
        reject(new Error(`no relayer key was free within ${timeoutMs} ms`));
      }, timeoutMs);
      this.#waiters.push(waiter);
    });
  }

  #lease(keyPair: KeyPair): KeyLease {
    let released = false;
    return {
      keyPair,
      release: () => {
        if (released) return;
        released = true;
        const next = this.#waiters.shift();
        if (next) next(this.#lease(keyPair));
        else this.#free.push(keyPair);
      },
    };
  }
}

/**
 * Build both providers with `retries: 1`. near-api-js counts attempts (with `retries: 0` it posts
 * nothing), so a transaction is posted at most once, and each lookup posts once and leaves the
 * deadline to be checked between posts.
 */
export interface RpcRelayerOptions {
  relayer: string;
  poolsContract: string;
  keys: KeyPool;
  /** Reads: nonces, blocks, transaction lookups. Construct it with `retries: 1`. */
  readProvider: Provider;
  /** Sends only. Construct it with `retries: 1`, so a transaction is posted at most once. */
  sendProvider: Provider;
  /** How often a lookup by hash is retried. Default 2000 ms. */
  lookupIntervalMs?: number;
  /**
   * How long a delegate is looked up, at most, after a send whose result is not known. The lookup
   * ends sooner once the final height passes the delegate's `maxBlockHeight`. Default 240 000 ms.
   */
  delegateLookupMs?: number;
  /** How long a keeper call is looked up after a send whose result is not known. Default 60 000 ms. */
  callLookupMs?: number;
  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;
  now?: () => number;
}

/**
 * When a lookup by hash gives up: after `lookupMs`, or, for a delegate, once the final height passes
 * its `maxBlockHeight` (the result is then `unknown` and `expired`, with that height), whichever comes
 * first.
 */
interface Deadline {
  lookupMs: number;
  maxBlockHeight?: bigint;
}

type SignedDelegateParts = Parameters<typeof actions.signedDelegate>[0];

/**
 * True when the RPC refused the transaction while validating it (a bad nonce, an expired block hash,
 * a congested or stuck shard, a malformed request), or turned the request away unread with HTTP 429
 * (too many requests), so it never ran. A timeout, a routed request, a server error (any other HTTP
 * error status included), an error it does not recognise or a network failure leaves its fate open.
 */
function refused(error: unknown): boolean {
  // near-api-js throws its own error class, which it does not export, for an HTTP error status, with
  // the status as the error's cause.
  if (error instanceof Error && error.cause === 429) return true;
  // An action error is what a transaction that ran raises. near-api-js also gives one to a transaction
  // refused for an invalid action; that one is looked up too, which only delays its answer.
  if (error instanceof ActionExecutionError) return false;
  return (
    error instanceof TransactionExecutionError ||
    error instanceof InvalidTransactionError ||
    error instanceof RequestValidationError
  );
}

/**
 * The outcome in a transaction response, or null when the response cannot be read as one, including a
 * response from before every non-refund receipt had run.
 */
function readOutcome(response: unknown): TxOutcome | null {
  try {
    return toTxOutcome(response);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * ChainWriter that signs with the relayer account. It builds and signs each transaction with a leased
 * key, sends it once and waits for `EXECUTED_OPTIMISTIC`. A delegate is first checked against the
 * final height and refused with DelegateExpiredError, before anything is built or signed, when it is
 * about to expire. If the send times out, the network fails, the RPC cannot say whether it took the
 * transaction (a routed request, a server error) or its response cannot be read (or comes back below
 * `EXECUTED_OPTIMISTIC`), it looks the transaction up by hash (never re-signing or re-sending) until a
 * readable outcome is found or the deadline passes. An RPC error that refuses the transaction, or an
 * HTTP 429 that turns the request away, is a rejection: nothing ran, and the key's cached nonce is
 * dropped. Nothing throws once a transaction has been sent.
 *
 * The key goes back to the pool once a result is returned, even an `unknown` one whose transaction
 * may still be pending. Nonces are ordered, so the key's next transaction cannot clash with it: if
 * the next one lands first, the pending one can no longer land.
 */
export class RpcRelayer implements ChainWriter {
  readonly #relayer: string;
  readonly #poolsContract: string;
  readonly #keys: KeyPool;
  readonly #read: Provider;
  readonly #send: Provider;
  readonly #lookupIntervalMs: number;
  readonly #delegateLookupMs: number;
  readonly #callLookupMs: number;
  readonly #sleep: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;
  readonly #now: () => number;
  /** One Account per key, each holding near-api-js's nonce cache for that key alone. */
  readonly #accounts = new Map<string, Account>();

  constructor(opts: RpcRelayerOptions) {
    this.#relayer = opts.relayer;
    this.#poolsContract = opts.poolsContract;
    this.#keys = opts.keys;
    this.#read = opts.readProvider;
    this.#send = opts.sendProvider;
    this.#lookupIntervalMs = opts.lookupIntervalMs ?? 2_000;
    this.#delegateLookupMs = opts.delegateLookupMs ?? 240_000;
    this.#callLookupMs = opts.callLookupMs ?? 60_000;
    this.#sleep = opts.sleep ?? ((ms) => delay(ms));
    this.#now = opts.now ?? Date.now;
  }

  relayDelegate(signed: DecodedSignedDelegate, maxBlockHeight: bigint): Promise<RelayResult> {
    // Borsh encodes by field name, so the decoded plain objects serialize like near-api-js's classes.
    const action = actions.signedDelegate(signed as unknown as SignedDelegateParts);
    return this.#submit(signed.delegateAction.senderId, action, { lookupMs: this.#delegateLookupMs, maxBlockHeight });
  }

  callPools(method: 'settle' | 'refund', args: Record<string, unknown>, gas: bigint): Promise<RelayResult> {
    const action = actions.functionCall(method, args, gas, 0n);
    return this.#submit(this.#poolsContract, action, { lookupMs: this.#callLookupMs });
  }

  async #submit(receiverId: string, action: Action, deadline: Deadline): Promise<RelayResult> {
    const lease = await this.#keys.acquire();
    try {
      // After the lease, since waiting for a key takes blocks; before the transaction is built, since
      // building it reserves a nonce.
      if (deadline.maxBlockHeight !== undefined) await this.#refuseExpired(deadline.maxBlockHeight);
      const publicKey = lease.keyPair.getPublicKey().toString();
      const transaction = await this.#account(publicKey).createTransaction({ receiverId, actions: [action], publicKey });
      const signer = new KeyPairSigner(lease.keyPair);
      const { txHash: hashBytes, signedTransaction } = await signer.signTransaction(transaction);
      const txHash = baseEncode(hashBytes);
      let response: unknown;
      try {
        response = await this.#send.sendTransactionUntil(signedTransaction, 'EXECUTED_OPTIMISTIC');
      } catch (error) {
        if (!refused(error)) return await this.#lookUp(txHash, deadline);
        this.#accounts.delete(publicKey);
        return { kind: 'rejected', txHash, error: String(error) };
      }
      const outcome = readOutcome(response);
      if (outcome === null) return await this.#lookUp(txHash, deadline);
      return { kind: 'executed', outcome };
    } finally {
      lease.release();
    }
  }

  #account(publicKey: string): Account {
    let account = this.#accounts.get(publicKey);
    if (!account) {
      account = new Account(this.#relayer, this.#read);
      this.#accounts.set(publicKey, account);
    }
    return account;
  }

  /** Throws DelegateExpiredError when the final height is within EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS of `maxBlockHeight`. */
  async #refuseExpired(maxBlockHeight: bigint): Promise<void> {
    const block = await this.#read.viewBlock({ finality: 'final' });
    const height = BigInt(block.header.height);
    if (height + EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS >= maxBlockHeight) {
      throw new DelegateExpiredError(`the delegate expires at block ${maxBlockHeight} and the final height is ${height}`);
    }
  }

  /**
   * Looks the transaction up every `lookupIntervalMs` until an outcome is found or the deadline passes.
   * The clock is checked first, so no block is read once the time is up.
   */
  async #lookUp(txHash: string, { lookupMs, maxBlockHeight }: Deadline): Promise<RelayResult> {
    const end = this.#now() + lookupMs;
    for (;;) {
      // Read the deadline before looking, so the last lookup is made after the deadline has passed.
      const timeUp = this.#now() >= end;
      const passed = !timeUp && maxBlockHeight !== undefined ? await this.#finalHeightAbove(maxBlockHeight) : null;
      const outcome = readOutcome(await this.#find(txHash));
      if (outcome !== null) return { kind: 'executed', outcome };
      if (passed !== null) return { kind: 'unknown', txHash, expired: true, finalHeight: passed };
      if (timeUp) return { kind: 'unknown', txHash, expired: false };
      await this.#sleep(this.#lookupIntervalMs);
    }
  }

  /**
   * The final height when it is above `height`; null when it is not, or while it cannot be read (the
   * lookup goes on).
   */
  async #finalHeightAbove(height: bigint): Promise<bigint | null> {
    try {
      const block = await this.#read.viewBlock({ finality: 'final' });
      const finalHeight = BigInt(block.header.height);
      return finalHeight > height ? finalHeight : null;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  /** The transaction's response, or null while the RPC does not have it. */
  async #find(txHash: string): Promise<unknown> {
    try {
      return await this.#read.viewTransactionStatus({
        txHash,
        accountId: this.#relayer,
        waitUntil: 'EXECUTED_OPTIMISTIC',
      });
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }
}
```

```typescript
import { REDEEM_MAX_AGE_MS, REDEEM_MAX_SKEW_MS } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';

/**
 * Buyers with a payment in flight: at most one each (spec section 6.4). A buyer is busy from `begin`
 * to `end`, and held after `end` while a payment whose result is unknown may still execute or still
 * have receipts to run.
 */
export class InFlight {
  readonly #busy = new Set<string>();
  /** Held buyers, each with the last height at which its payment may still take effect. */
  readonly #held = new Map<string, bigint>();

  /** Marks the buyer busy. Returns false, changing nothing, if it already was busy or is held. */
  begin(buyer: string): boolean {
    if (this.#busy.has(buyer) || this.#held.has(buyer)) return false;
    this.#busy.add(buyer);
    return true;
  }

  /** Ends the buyer's busy time. A hold outlasts it. */
  end(buyer: string): void {
    this.#busy.delete(buyer);
  }

  /**
   * Keeps the buyer in flight until `passed` is given a final height above `untilHeight`: the last
   * height at which its payment may still take effect, its `max_block_height` plus the blocks its
   * receipts take.
   */
  hold(buyer: string, untilHeight: bigint): void {
    this.#held.set(buyer, untilHeight);
  }

  held(buyer: string): boolean {
    return this.#held.has(buyer);
  }

  /** Lifts every hold whose height is below `finalHeight`: those payments can no longer take effect. */
  passed(finalHeight: bigint): void {
    for (const [buyer, untilHeight] of this.#held) {
      if (finalHeight > untilHeight) this.#held.delete(buyer);
    }
  }

  /** True while the buyer is busy or held. */
  has(buyer: string): boolean {
    return this.#busy.has(buyer) || this.#held.has(buyer);
  }
}

/** Redemption nonces seen in the last `ttlMs`. In memory only, so it restarts empty. */
export class NonceCache {
  readonly #ttlMs: number;
  readonly #seenAt = new Map<string, number>();

  constructor(ttlMs: number) {
    this.#ttlMs = ttlMs;
  }

  /** Returns true if `key` was seen within the TTL; otherwise records it and returns false. */
  seen(key: string, nowMs: number): boolean {
    for (const [k, at] of this.#seenAt) {
      if (nowMs - at >= this.#ttlMs) this.#seenAt.delete(k);
    }
    if (this.#seenAt.has(key)) return true;
    this.#seenAt.set(key, nowMs);
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * The cache of redemption nonces (spec section 6.5). A proof signed up to REDEEM_MAX_SKEW_MS ahead
 * stays fresh until REDEEM_MAX_AGE_MS after its signing time, so a nonce is kept for their sum.
 */
export function proofNonceCache(): NonceCache {
  return new NonceCache(REDEEM_MAX_AGE_MS + REDEEM_MAX_SKEW_MS);
}
```

```typescript
import { PAYMENT_RESPONSE_HEADER, checkPaymentHeader, encodeHeader, paymentRequired } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import type {
  CheckedPayment,
  GatewayErrorCode,
  PaymentErrorCode,
  PaymentResponse,
  PoolView,
} from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import type { ActivityRecord } from './activity.ts';
import { DelegateExpiredError, EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS, type BlockInfo, type RelayResult, type TxOutcome } from './chain.ts';
import type { Deps } from './deps.ts';
import { currentAccepts, parseSeats } from './handle-offer.ts';
import { readCommit } from './outcome.ts';
import { servedPool } from './pools.ts';
import { reply, type Reply } from './reply.ts';


/**
 * NEAR refuses a delegate whose nonce is at or above the block height times this without storing
 * the nonce, so the same payment could otherwise be relayed again and again.
 */
const NONCE_RANGE_MULTIPLIER = 1_000_000n;

/** A refusal carries the buyer's seats once they are known, so that its offer can respect the buyer's limit. */
type ChainCheck = { ok: true; held: number } | { ok: false; code: GatewayErrorCode; held?: number };

/** Checks 4 and 5 passed, with the final block they were judged against. */
type FreshCheck = { ok: true; block: BlockInfo } | { ok: false; code: GatewayErrorCode };

/**
 * `GET /pools/:id/access?seats=N` with an `X-PAYMENT` header (spec sections 6.3 and 6.4): the
 * checks in order, then the relay, then the response table. The payment may commit to fewer seats
 * than `seats` (a reduced offer paid at the URL first requested), never to more.
 * - 400 `{error: "invalid_seats"}` and 404 `{error: "unknown_pool"}` as for the offer.
 * - 402 paymentRequired(current offer, code) for a failed check, a payment already in flight for
 *   the buyer, or a delegate the relayer finds too close to its expiry to send (`expired`). Nothing
 *   is relayed. The `over_buyer_cap` offer is for the seats the buyer may still take, if any.
 *   A payment takes its buyer's in-flight slot only once it has passed checks 4 and 5 (its key is a
 *   full-access key of the buyer's account, its nonce is above that key's, and its max_block_height
 *   is within the accepted window), so neither a payment signed with another key nor a replay of a
 *   used or expired payment can hold the slot.
 *   A payment whose result is unknown keeps its buyer in flight, while its delegate may still land,
 *   until a final block above its `max_block_height` plus EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS is read: a delegate
 *   included by its `max_block_height` still has its token and pools receipts to run after it. This
 *   holds also when the relayer's lookup saw the delegate expire; the buyer is then free at once only
 *   if the final height the lookup read is already above that.
 * - 202 `{status: "pending", receipt, pool}` or, when the commit filled the pool, 200 `{status:
 *   "filled", credential, poolId, seats, terms}`; both carry `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`.
 * - When no seats were taken: 410 `{error: "pool_expired", poolId, txHash}` if the pool is past its
 *   deadline (its view says Expired or Refunded, or says Open while the latest final block's time is
 *   at or past the deadline); 502 `{error: "relay_failed", txHash}` if the transfer never reached the
 *   pools contract or the pool is still Open with a seat left; otherwise (the pool filled) 409
 *   `{x402Version: 1, error: "no_seats_taken", accepts: []}`.
 * - 502 `{error: "relay_failed" | "result_unknown", txHash}` when the relay was refused, the delegate
 *   failed, or the result is unknown or cannot be read.
 * - 503 `{error: "chain_unavailable"}` when the chain cannot be read before the relay.
 *
 * A failure to append to the activity feed, and the error behind a 503 or a `result_unknown` reply
 * that follows a relay, are logged; none changes the reply.
 */
export async function handlePayment(
  deps: Deps,
  poolId: number,
  seatsParam: string | undefined,
  header: string,
): Promise<Reply> {
  const seats = parseSeats(seatsParam);
  if (seats === null) return reply(400, { error: 'invalid_seats' });
  try {
    return await checkAndRelay(deps, poolId, seats, header);
  } catch (error) {
    // A chain read failed, or relayDelegate threw before sending anything.
    console.error('could not check or relay a payment:', error);
    return reply(503, { error: 'chain_unavailable' });
  }
}

async function checkAndRelay(deps: Deps, poolId: number, seats: number, header: string): Promise<Reply> {
  const { config, chain, inFlight } = deps;
  const pool = await servedPool(chain, config.provider, poolId);
  if (pool === null) return reply(404, { error: 'unknown_pool' });
  // Every refused payment gets the offer as it stands.
  const refuse = (code: PaymentErrorCode, held?: number): Reply =>
    reply(402, paymentRequired(currentAccepts(pool, seats, config, held), code));

  const checked = checkPaymentHeader(header, {
    network: config.network,
    token: config.token,
    poolsContract: config.poolsContract,
    poolId,
    maxSeats: seats,
    seatPrice: BigInt(pool.seat_price),
    minGas: config.minGas,
    maxGas: config.maxGas,
  });
  if (!checked.ok) return refuse(checked.code);
  const { payment } = checked;

  const fresh = await checkFresh(deps, payment);
  if (!fresh.ok) return refuse(fresh.code);
  if (!inFlight.begin(payment.senderId)) return refuse('payment_in_flight');
  try {
    const check = await checkOnChain(deps, pool, payment, fresh.block);
    if (!check.ok) return refuse(check.code, check.held);
    let result: RelayResult;
    try {
      result = await deps.writer.relayDelegate(payment.signedDelegate, payment.maxBlockHeight);
    } catch (error) {
      // Nothing was sent. Any other error answers 503 like a failed read.
      if (error instanceof DelegateExpiredError) return refuse('expired', check.held);
      throw error;
    }
    return await answerRelay(deps, pool, payment, check.held, result);
  } finally {
    inFlight.end(payment.senderId);
  }
}

/**
 * Checks 4 and 5, before the buyer's in-flight slot is taken: the key is a full-access key of the
 * buyer's account, the nonce is above the key's and below the final height × 10^6, and
 * `max_block_height` is within the accepted window. The checks before these verify the signature only
 * against the delegate's own key; these are the ones that only the buyer's own fresh payment passes.
 * Check 4 ties that key to sender_id, and a used or expired payment, which anyone can copy from the
 * chain, fails check 5. So neither a payment signed with another key nor a replay holds the buyer's
 * slot. The later checks use the final block read here.
 */
async function checkFresh(deps: Deps, payment: CheckedPayment): Promise<FreshCheck> {
  const { chain, config, inFlight } = deps;
  const refused = (code: GatewayErrorCode): FreshCheck => ({ ok: false, code });

  const key = await chain.accessKey(payment.senderId, payment.publicKey);
  if (key === null || !key.fullAccess) return refused('not_full_access');
  if (payment.nonce <= key.nonce) return refused('stale_nonce');
  const block = await chain.finalBlock();
  // Frees each held buyer whose payment can no longer execute (this one too), so holds do not pile up.
  inFlight.passed(block.height);
  if (payment.nonce >= block.height * NONCE_RANGE_MULTIPLIER) return refused('nonce_too_large');
  const maxAhead = BigInt(Math.ceil((config.maxTimeoutSeconds * 1000) / config.blockTimeMs));
  const ahead = payment.maxBlockHeight - block.height;
  if (ahead <= EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS || ahead > maxAhead + EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS) return refused('expired');
  return { ok: true, block };
}

/**
 * Checks 6 to 8 once the buyer's slot is taken: the pool, judged against `block` (the final block
 * checkFresh read), the balance and the buyer's seats. The key and its nonce are checked again first:
 * an earlier payment of the buyer may have finished since checkFresh read the key.
 */
async function checkOnChain(
  deps: Deps,
  pool: PoolView,
  payment: CheckedPayment,
  block: BlockInfo,
): Promise<ChainCheck> {
  const { chain } = deps;
  const buyer = payment.senderId;
  const refused = (code: GatewayErrorCode): ChainCheck => ({ ok: false, code });

  const key = await chain.accessKey(buyer, payment.publicKey);
  if (key === null || !key.fullAccess) return refused('not_full_access');
  if (payment.nonce <= key.nonce) return refused('stale_nonce');
  if (pool.status !== 'open' || pool.taken >= pool.target || block.timestampMs >= pool.deadline_ms) {
    return refused('pool_closed');
  }
  if ((await chain.ftBalanceOf(buyer)) < payment.amount) return refused('insufficient_balance');
  // The contract refuses both of these, so relaying them would only cost the relayer gas.
  if (buyer === pool.seller) return refused('seller_commit');
  const held = (await chain.getBuyer(pool.id, buyer))?.seats ?? 0;
  if (pool.max_seats_per_buyer !== null && held + payment.seats > pool.max_seats_per_buyer) {
    return { ok: false, code: 'over_buyer_cap', held };
  }
  return { ok: true, held };
}

/** The response to a relay. `held` is the seats the buyer held before this payment. */
async function answerRelay(
  deps: Deps,
  pool: PoolView,
  payment: CheckedPayment,
  held: number,
  result: RelayResult,
): Promise<Reply> {
  if (result.kind === 'rejected') return reply(502, { error: 'relay_failed', txHash: result.txHash });
  if (result.kind === 'unknown') {
    // The delegate may still take seats: the buyer stays in flight until it no longer can. A delegate
    // included at its max_block_height still runs ft_transfer_call and ft_on_transfer in the blocks
    // after, and a new payment checked before they have run would not see the seats they take. That is
    // so also after a lookup that saw the delegate expire, which stops on the first final block above
    // its max_block_height: the height that lookup read lifts the hold at once only if it is already
    // above max_block_height plus EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS.
    deps.inFlight.hold(payment.senderId, payment.maxBlockHeight + EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS);
    if (result.expired) deps.inFlight.passed(result.finalHeight);
    return reply(502, { error: 'result_unknown', txHash: result.txHash });
  }
  try {
    return await answerCommit(deps, pool, payment, held, result.outcome);
  } catch (error) {
    // The transaction ran, so the payment may have landed: the buyer finds out through redemption.
    const { txHash } = result.outcome;
    console.error(`could not answer the payment of transaction ${txHash}:`, error);
    return reply(502, { error: 'result_unknown', txHash });
  }
}

async function answerCommit(
  deps: Deps,
  pool: PoolView,
  payment: CheckedPayment,
  held: number,
  outcome: TxOutcome,
): Promise<Reply> {
  const { config } = deps;
  const buyer = payment.senderId;
  const { txHash } = outcome;
  const commit = readCommit(outcome, { poolsContract: config.poolsContract, buyer, poolId: pool.id });

  // A failed delegate is recorded too (0 seats, not ok): its transaction ran and has a link.
  await appendActivity(deps, {
    at: deps.now(),
    poolId: pool.id,
    kind: 'commit',
    account: buyer,
    seats: commit.seats,
    amount: commit.amount.toString(),
    txHash,
    ok: commit.seats > 0,
  });
  if (commit.delegateFailed) return reply(502, { error: 'relay_failed', txHash });
  if (commit.seats === 0) return await answerNoSeats(deps, pool.id, outcome);

  const response: PaymentResponse = { success: true, transaction: txHash, network: config.network, payer: buyer };
  const headers = { [PAYMENT_RESPONSE_HEADER]: encodeHeader(response) };
  if (commit.filled) {
    const seats = held + commit.seats;
    const credential = await deps.credentials.issue({ buyer, poolId: pool.id, seats, terms: pool.terms });
    return reply(200, { status: 'filled', credential, poolId: pool.id, seats, terms: pool.terms }, headers);
  }
  return reply(
    202,
    {
      status: 'pending',
      receipt: { poolId: pool.id, buyer, seats: commit.seats, txHash },
      pool: { taken: commit.taken, target: commit.target, deadlineMs: pool.deadline_ms },
    },
    headers,
  );
}

/**
 * A commit that took no seats, so the token has returned the payment. The contract takes
 * `min(seats, target − taken)` seats of an Open pool before its deadline, so a payment lost a race
 * only if the pool filled or expired before it landed.
 */
async function answerNoSeats(deps: Deps, poolId: number, outcome: TxOutcome): Promise<Reply> {
  const { txHash } = outcome;
  const latest = await deps.chain.getPool(poolId);
  if (latest !== null && (await pastDeadline(deps, latest))) {
    return reply(410, { error: 'pool_expired', poolId, txHash });
  }
  const reachedPools = outcome.receipts.some((receipt) => receipt.executorId === deps.config.poolsContract);
  const seatLeft = latest?.status === 'open' && latest.taken < latest.target;
  if (!reachedPools || seatLeft) {
    // The refusal had another cause, such as the buyer's limit, so the same payment would be refused again.
    return reply(502, { error: 'relay_failed', txHash });
  }
  // The pool filled before the payment landed, so there is nothing left to offer.
  return reply(409, paymentRequired([], 'no_seats_taken'));
}

/**
 * Whether a pool is past its deadline: its view says Expired or Refunded, or says Open while the
 * latest final block's time is at or past the deadline. A Filled or Settled pool never is.
 */
async function pastDeadline(deps: Deps, pool: PoolView): Promise<boolean> {
  if (pool.status === 'expired' || pool.status === 'refunded') return true;
  return pool.status === 'open' && (await deps.chain.finalBlock()).timestampMs >= pool.deadline_ms;
}

/** Appends to the activity feed, logging a failure: the feed never changes a reply. */
async function appendActivity(deps: Deps, record: ActivityRecord): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await deps.activity.append(record);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('could not append to the activity feed:', error);
  }
}
```

### Task 3: The buyer package: settings, key files and the spend file

The swarm's scripted buyers and the MCP server act as buyers with the same configuration and keys,
so they share one package, `@quorum-on-near/buyer`, which imports only the protocol package and
near-api-js. It goes in first with its manifest, so that pnpm finds it and vitest is installed.
This task adds the three modules that touch configuration and files.

`settings.ts` reads configuration from `QUORUM_*` variables. `readBuyerSettings` reads what a buyer
shares with the gateway, each from the gateway's own variable with the gateway's own default
(section 7.6):

| Variable | Field | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUORUM_NETWORK` | `network` | `near:testnet` | `near:testnet` or `near:sandbox` |
| `QUORUM_RPC_URL` | `rpcUrl` | `https://test.rpc.fastnear.com` | an http or https URL, kept as written, never quoted in a problem |
| `QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL` | `gatewayUrl` | `http://localhost:8402` | an http or https URL, trailing slashes removed, never quoted |
| `QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT` | `parent` | required | a NEAR account id |
| `QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT` | `token` | Circle's testnet USDC | a NEAR account id |
| `QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT` | `poolsContract` | `pools.<parent>` | a NEAR account id |
| `QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS` | `blockTimeMs` | `1000` | a positive integer |
| `QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `maxTimeoutSeconds` | `120` | an integer from 30 to 3600: the buyer's own bound on a payment's life (section 6.3) |

`readMcpBuyerSettings` reads the MCP server's buyer, which the swarm also reads (it creates and
funds that buyer and clears its spend total): `QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT` (`buyer-llm.<parent>`),
`QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR` (an absolute path, `~/.near-credentials`) and `QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE` (an
absolute path, `data/mcp-spend.json` at the repository root, resolved from the module's own
location). A loader reads its variables with an `EnvReader` into one list of problems, one line per
missing or invalid variable, then `completeConfig` throws a single `ConfigError` listing them all. A
problem line quotes the raw value, except for a rule marked `secret` (the URLs, which may carry an
API key). The rules the swarm and the MCP server need for their own variables (`asInteger`,
`asPositiveInteger`, `asAmount`, `asNear`, `asAbsolutePath`) are exported; `asNear` reads a decimal
string such as `0.05` into yoctoNEAR without going through a JavaScript number.

`key-files.ts` reads and writes keys in near-cli's layout (section 7.1): `<dir>/<network>/<account>.json`
for an account's key, with `testnet` or `sandbox` as the network folder, and
`<dir>/<network>/<account>/<public key with ':' as '_'>.json` for an account with several keys, the
relayer's. `readKeyFile` reads the file near-cli-rs writes (no `account_id`) and the one
`writeKeyFile` writes (`account_id`, `public_key`, `private_key`), falls back to `secret_key`, and
checks that `public_key` belongs to the private key. An empty file counts as missing: a write cut
short leaves one. `writeKeyFile` creates the file with mode 0600 (its folder 0700), flushes it, syncs
its folder on POSIX systems, and never writes over a file that holds anything; an empty one is
replaced once. `readKeyFolder` reads every key of a folder, sorted by public key, each file named
after its key. A `KeyFileError` (`missing`, `exists` or `invalid`) names the path and never quotes the
file's content.

`spend-file.ts` keeps the MCP server's running total of what its buyer has spent, in base units, as
`{"account": "<buyer>", "spent": "<decimal>"}` (section 7.5). A missing file reads 0; a file that
holds another account's total, or no total, is a `SpendFileError` (`other_account` or `malformed`).
`writeSpendFile` writes a new temporary file in the same folder and renames it over the old one, so a
reader sees the old total or the new one, never part of one; callers serialise their writes.

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/buyer/package.json`, `packages/buyer/tsconfig.json`,
  `packages/buyer/src/settings.ts`, `packages/buyer/src/key-files.ts`,
  `packages/buyer/src/spend-file.ts`, `packages/buyer/src/index.ts` (re-exports these three; Tasks 4
  and 5 add the rest)
- Modify: `pnpm-lock.yaml` (the `packages/buyer` importer, written by `pnpm install`)
- Test: `packages/buyer/test/settings.test.ts`, `packages/buyer/test/key-files.test.ts`,
  `packages/buyer/test/spend-file.test.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing from earlier tasks. From the protocol package on `main`: `isAccountId`,
  `parseAmount`. From near-api-js: `KeyPair`, `PublicKey`, `nearToYocto`.
- Produces:
  - package `@quorum-on-near/buyer`: private, `"type": "module"`, `exports` `{".": "./src/index.ts"}`;
    dependencies `@quorum-on-near/protocol` (`workspace:*`) and `near-api-js` 7.4.0; devDependencies
    `@types/node` 22.20.5, `typescript` 5.9.3, `vitest` 4.1.12; scripts `test` = `vitest run`,
    `typecheck` = `tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
  - `settings.ts`: `export type Env = Record<string, string | undefined>`;
    `export type BuyerNetwork = 'near:testnet' | 'near:sandbox'`;
    `export const TESTNET_USDC = '3e2210e1184b45b64c8a434c0a7e7b23cc04ea7eb7a6c3c32520d03d4afcb8af'`;
    `export interface BuyerSettings { network: BuyerNetwork; rpcUrl: string; gatewayUrl: string; parent: string; token: string; poolsContract: string; blockTimeMs: number; maxTimeoutSeconds: number }`;
    `export interface McpBuyerSettings { mcpAccount: string; credentialsDir: string; spendFile: string }`;
    `export interface Rule<T> { expected: string; parse(raw: string): T | undefined; secret?: boolean }`;
    `export type Draft<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] | undefined }`;
    `export class ConfigError extends Error { readonly problems: readonly string[]; constructor(problems: readonly string[]) }`;
    `export class EnvReader { constructor(env: Env, problems: string[]); optional<T>(name: string, fallback: string, rule: Rule<T>): T | undefined; required<T>(name: string, rule: Rule<T>): T | undefined; nullable<T>(name: string, rule: Rule<T>): T | null | undefined; child(name: string, prefix: string, parent: string | undefined): string | undefined }`;
    `export function completeConfig<T>(draft: Draft<T>, problems: readonly string[]): T`;
    `export function readBuyerSettings(env: Env, problems: string[]): Draft<BuyerSettings>`;
    `export function readMcpBuyerSettings(env: Env, problems: string[], parent: string | undefined): Draft<McpBuyerSettings>`;
    `export function asInteger(min: number, max: number, expected?: string): Rule<number>`;
    `export const asPositiveInteger: Rule<number>`, `asAmount: Rule<bigint>`, `asNear: Rule<bigint>`,
    `asAbsolutePath: Rule<string>`.
  - `key-files.ts`: `export function defaultCredentialsDir(): string`;
    `export function keyFilePath(dir: string, network: BuyerNetwork, accountId: string): string`;
    `export function keyFolderPath(dir: string, network: BuyerNetwork, accountId: string): string`
    (both throw `RangeError` for a value that is not a NEAR account id);
    `export function folderKeyPath(folder: string, publicKey: PublicKey): string`;
    `export async function readKeyFile(path: string): Promise<KeyPair>`;
    `export async function writeKeyFile(path: string, accountId: string, keyPair: KeyPair): Promise<void>`;
    `export async function readKeyFolder(folder: string): Promise<KeyPair[]>`;
    `export type KeyFileProblem = 'missing' | 'exists' | 'invalid'`;
    `export class KeyFileError extends Error { readonly path: string; readonly problem: KeyFileProblem; constructor(path: string, problem: KeyFileProblem, message: string) }`.
  - `spend-file.ts`: `export function defaultSpendFile(): string`;
    `export async function readSpendFile(path: string, account: string): Promise<bigint>`;
    `export async function writeSpendFile(path: string, account: string, spent: bigint): Promise<void>`
    (throws `RangeError` for a negative total);
    `export type SpendFileProblem = 'other_account' | 'malformed'`;
    `export class SpendFileError extends Error { readonly path: string; readonly problem: SpendFileProblem; constructor(path: string, problem: SpendFileProblem, message: string) }`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing tests**

`key-files.test.ts` wraps `writeFile` and `open` of `node:fs/promises` in recording mocks that still
act on the disk, to observe the flush and the folder sync. Its test of the file modes runs on POSIX
systems only (`it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')`), since Windows does not apply them.

`packages/buyer/test/settings.test.ts`:

```typescript
import { homedir, tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { defaultSpendFile } from '../src/spend-file.ts';
import {
  asAbsolutePath,
  asAmount,
  asInteger,
  asNear,
  asPositiveInteger,
  completeConfig,
  ConfigError,
  EnvReader,
  readBuyerSettings,
  readMcpBuyerSettings,
  type BuyerSettings,
  type Env,
  type McpBuyerSettings,
} from '../src/settings.ts';

const PARENT = 'parent.testnet';

/** The buyer settings read from `env`, with the problems found. */
function read(env: Env): { settings: Partial<BuyerSettings>; problems: string[] } {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const settings = readBuyerSettings(env, problems);
  return { settings, problems };
}

describe('readBuyerSettings', () => {
  it("applies the gateway's defaults when only the parent account is set", () => {
    const { settings, problems } = read({ QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT });
    expect(problems).toEqual([]);
    expect(settings).toEqual<BuyerSettings>({
      network: 'near:testnet',
      rpcUrl: 'https://test.rpc.fastnear.com',
      gatewayUrl: 'http://localhost:8402',
      parent: PARENT,
      token: '3e2210e1184b45b64c8a434c0a7e7b23cc04ea7eb7a6c3c32520d03d4afcb8af',
      poolsContract: 'pools.parent.testnet',
      blockTimeMs: 1000,
      maxTimeoutSeconds: 120,
    });
  });

  it('reads every variable that is set', () => {
    const { settings, problems } = read({
      QUORUM_NETWORK: 'near:sandbox',
      QUORUM_RPC_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:3030',
      QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: 'https://gateway.example.com:8443',
      QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: 'test.near',
      QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT: 'musd.test.near',
      QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT: 'escrow.test.near',
      QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS: '600',
      QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '300',
    });
    expect(problems).toEqual([]);
    expect(settings).toEqual<BuyerSettings>({
      network: 'near:sandbox',
      rpcUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:3030',
      gatewayUrl: 'https://gateway.example.com:8443',
      parent: 'test.near',
      token: 'musd.test.near',
      poolsContract: 'escrow.test.near',
      blockTimeMs: 600,
      maxTimeoutSeconds: 300,
    });
  });

  it('strips trailing slashes from the gateway URL, as the gateway does', () => {
    const { settings } = read({ QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT, QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: 'http://localhost:8402//' });
    expect(settings.gatewayUrl).toBe('http://localhost:8402');
  });

  it('keeps the RPC URL as written', () => {
    const { settings } = read({ QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT, QUORUM_RPC_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:3030/' });
    expect(settings.rpcUrl).toBe('http://127.0.0.1:3030/');
  });

  it('reads the longest expiry the buyer signs, from 30 to 3600 seconds', () => {
    const at = (raw: string) => read({ QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT, QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: raw });
    expect(at('30').settings.maxTimeoutSeconds).toBe(30);
    expect(at('3600').settings.maxTimeoutSeconds).toBe(3600);
    expect(at('29').problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be an integer from 30 to 3600, got "29"']);
    expect(at('3601').problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be an integer from 30 to 3600, got "3601"']);
  });

  it('requires the parent account, and gives the pools account no default without it', () => {
    const { settings, problems } = read({});
    expect(problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT is required']);
    expect(settings.parent).toBeUndefined();
    expect(settings.poolsContract).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('treats an empty parent account as missing', () => {
    expect(read({ QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: '' }).problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT is required']);
  });

  it('collects one problem per invalid variable, naming each value but a URL', () => {
    const { settings, problems } = read({
      QUORUM_NETWORK: 'near:mainnet',
      QUORUM_RPC_URL: 'ftp://rpc.example.com',
      QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: 'localhost:8402',
      QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: 'Parent.testnet',
      QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT: 'usdc..testnet',
      QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT: 'pools/x',
      QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS: '0',
      QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '120.5',
    });
    expect(problems).toEqual([
      'QUORUM_NETWORK must be near:testnet or near:sandbox, got "near:mainnet"',
      'QUORUM_RPC_URL must be an http or https URL',
      'QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL must be an http or https URL',
      'QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT must be a NEAR account id, got "Parent.testnet"',
      'QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT must be a NEAR account id, got "usdc..testnet"',
      'QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT must be a NEAR account id, got "pools/x"',
      'QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS must be a positive integer, got "0"',
      'QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be an integer from 30 to 3600, got "120.5"',
    ]);
    expect(Object.values(settings).every((value) => value === undefined)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('never quotes the value of a URL variable, which may carry an API key', () => {
    const { problems } = read({
      QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT,
      QUORUM_RPC_URL: 'htps://rpc.example.org/?apiKey=SECRET-KEY',
      QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: 'gateway.example.org/?token=SECRET-TOKEN',
    });
    expect(problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_RPC_URL must be an http or https URL', 'QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL must be an http or https URL']);
  });

  it('appends to the problems already collected', () => {
    const problems = ['QUORUM_OTHER must be set'];
    readBuyerSettings({}, problems);
    expect(problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_OTHER must be set', 'QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT is required']);
  });
});

describe('readMcpBuyerSettings', () => {
  /** The MCP server's buyer read from `env` for the parent PARENT, with the problems found. */
  function readMcp(env: Env) {
    const problems: string[] = [];
    const settings = readMcpBuyerSettings(env, problems, PARENT);
    return { settings, problems };
  }

  it('names the buyer after the parent, and keeps its key and its spend total where the server looks by default', () => {
    const { settings, problems } = readMcp({});
    expect(settings).toEqual<McpBuyerSettings>({
      mcpAccount: 'buyer-llm.parent.testnet',
      credentialsDir: join(homedir(), '.near-credentials'),
      spendFile: defaultSpendFile(),
    });
    expect(problems).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('reads every variable that is set', () => {
    const credentialsDir = join(tmpdir(), 'near-keys');
    const spendFile = join(tmpdir(), 'spend.json');
    const { settings } = readMcp({
      QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT: 'agent.test.near',
      QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR: credentialsDir,
      QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE: spendFile,
    });
    expect(settings).toEqual<McpBuyerSettings>({ mcpAccount: 'agent.test.near', credentialsDir, spendFile });
  });

  it('appends one problem per invalid variable, in the order of the fields', () => {
    const problems = ['QUORUM_OTHER must be set'];
    const settings = readMcpBuyerSettings(
      { QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT: 'llm buyer', QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR: 'keys', QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE: 'data/mcp-spend.json' },
      problems,
      PARENT,
    );
    expect(problems).toEqual([
      'QUORUM_OTHER must be set',
      'QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT must be a NEAR account id, got "llm buyer"',
      'QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR must be an absolute path, got "keys"',
      'QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE must be an absolute path, got "data/mcp-spend.json"',
    ]);
    expect(Object.values(settings).every((value) => value === undefined)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('gives the buyer no default without a parent, adding no problem of its own', () => {
    const problems: string[] = [];
    const settings = readMcpBuyerSettings({}, problems, undefined);
    expect(settings.mcpAccount).toBeUndefined();
    expect(problems).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('completeConfig', () => {
  it('returns the draft when no problem was found', () => {
    const problems: string[] = [];
    const draft = readBuyerSettings({ QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT }, problems);
    expect(completeConfig<BuyerSettings>(draft, problems).poolsContract).toBe('pools.parent.testnet');
  });

  it('throws one ConfigError listing every problem, one per line', () => {
    const problems = ['QUORUM_A is required', 'QUORUM_B must be a positive integer, got "x"'];
    let thrown: unknown;
    try {
      completeConfig<{ a: string }>({ a: undefined }, problems);
    } catch (error) {
      thrown = error;
    }
    expect(thrown).toBeInstanceOf(ConfigError);
    const error = thrown as ConfigError;
    expect(error.problems).toEqual(problems);
    expect(error.message).toBe('QUORUM_A is required\nQUORUM_B must be a positive integer, got "x"');
  });
});

describe('EnvReader', () => {
  /** A reader of `env`, and the problems it collects. */
  function reader(env: Env): { read: EnvReader; problems: string[] } {
    const problems: string[] = [];
    return { read: new EnvReader(env, problems), problems };
  }

  it('optional reads the fallback when the variable is unset', () => {
    const { read, problems } = reader({});
    expect(read.optional('QUORUM_X', '5', asPositiveInteger)).toBe(5);
    expect(problems).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('optional checks an empty value with the rule rather than using the fallback', () => {
    const { read, problems } = reader({ QUORUM_X: '' });
    expect(read.optional('QUORUM_X', '5', asPositiveInteger)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_X must be a positive integer, got ""']);
  });

  it('required reports an unset variable', () => {
    const { read, problems } = reader({});
    expect(read.required('QUORUM_X', asPositiveInteger)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_X is required']);
  });

  it('nullable gives null for an unset or empty variable, and checks any other value', () => {
    const { read, problems } = reader({ QUORUM_EMPTY: '', QUORUM_SET: '7', QUORUM_BAD: 'seven' });
    expect(read.nullable('QUORUM_UNSET', asPositiveInteger)).toBeNull();
    expect(read.nullable('QUORUM_EMPTY', asPositiveInteger)).toBeNull();
    expect(read.nullable('QUORUM_SET', asPositiveInteger)).toBe(7);
    expect(read.nullable('QUORUM_BAD', asPositiveInteger)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_BAD must be a positive integer, got "seven"']);
  });

  it('child defaults to <prefix>.<parent>', () => {
    const { read } = reader({});
    expect(read.child('QUORUM_RELAYER_ACCOUNT', 'relay', PARENT)).toBe('relay.parent.testnet');
  });

  it('child reads the variable when it is set, checking it is an account id', () => {
    const { read, problems } = reader({ QUORUM_A: 'me.testnet', QUORUM_B: 'not an account' });
    expect(read.child('QUORUM_A', 'a', PARENT)).toBe('me.testnet');
    expect(read.child('QUORUM_B', 'b', PARENT)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(problems).toEqual(['QUORUM_B must be a NEAR account id, got "not an account"']);
  });

  it('child reports nothing without a parent, whose problem is listed already', () => {
    const { read, problems } = reader({});
    expect(read.child('QUORUM_RELAYER_ACCOUNT', 'relay', undefined)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(problems).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('rules', () => {
  it('asNear reads a decimal amount of NEAR into yoctoNEAR', () => {
    expect(asNear.parse('0.05')).toBe(50_000_000_000_000_000_000_000n);
    expect(asNear.parse('3')).toBe(3_000_000_000_000_000_000_000_000n);
    expect(asNear.parse('3.5')).toBe(3_500_000_000_000_000_000_000_000n);
    // A JS number this small is written 1e-7, which a NEAR amount parser refuses.
    expect(asNear.parse('0.0000001')).toBe(100_000_000_000_000_000n);
    expect(asNear.parse('0.000000000000000000000001')).toBe(1n);
    expect(asNear.parse('0')).toBe(0n);
  });

  it.each(['', '1e-7', '-1', '1,000', '.5', '5.', '01', '0.0000000000000000000000001', ' 1', 'one'])(
    'asNear refuses %j',
    (raw) => {
      expect(asNear.parse(raw)).toBeUndefined();
    },
  );

  it('asAmount reads a decimal amount of base units', () => {
    expect(asAmount.parse('0')).toBe(0n);
    expect(asAmount.parse('10000')).toBe(10_000n);
    expect(asAmount.parse('340282366920938463463374607431768211455')).toBe(2n ** 128n - 1n);
  });

  it.each(['', '01', '-1', '1.5', '1e3', ' 1'])('asAmount refuses %j', (raw) => {
    expect(asAmount.parse(raw)).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('asInteger accepts its bounds and refuses values outside them', () => {
    const rule = asInteger(1, 10);
    expect(rule.parse('1')).toBe(1);
    expect(rule.parse('10')).toBe(10);
    expect(rule.parse('0')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(rule.parse('11')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(rule.expected).toBe('an integer from 1 to 10');
  });

  it.each(['0', '-1', '1.5', '01', '', '9007199254740992'])('asPositiveInteger refuses %j', (raw) => {
    expect(asPositiveInteger.parse(raw)).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('asAbsolutePath accepts an absolute path and refuses a relative one', () => {
    const absolute = join(tmpdir(), 'near-keys');
    expect(asAbsolutePath.parse(absolute)).toBe(absolute);
    expect(asAbsolutePath.parse('keys')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(asAbsolutePath.parse('~/.near-credentials')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(asAbsolutePath.parse('')).toBeUndefined();
  });
});
```

`packages/buyer/test/key-files.test.ts`:

```typescript
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, open, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { homedir, tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { KeyPair } from 'near-api-js';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  defaultCredentialsDir,
  folderKeyPath,
  KeyFileError,
  keyFilePath,
  keyFolderPath,
  readKeyFile,
  readKeyFolder,
  writeKeyFile,
} from '../src/key-files.ts';

// writeFile and open record their calls; both still act on the disk.
vi.mock('node:fs/promises', async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('node:fs/promises')>();
  return { ...actual, writeFile: vi.fn(actual.writeFile), open: vi.fn(actual.open) };
});

const ACCOUNT = 'buyer-01.parent.testnet';

let dir: string;

beforeEach(async () => {
  dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'quorum-key-files-'));
});

afterEach(async () => {
  vi.mocked(open).mockClear();
  vi.mocked(writeFile).mockClear();
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

/** Runs `body` with process.platform reading `platform`. */
async function onPlatform(platform: NodeJS.Platform, body: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(process, 'platform');
  Object.defineProperty(process, 'platform', { value: platform, configurable: true });
  try {
    await body();
  } finally {
    if (descriptor !== undefined) Object.defineProperty(process, 'platform', descriptor);
  }
}

/** The calls to open for `path`. */
function opened(path: string): unknown[][] {
  return vi.mocked(open).mock.calls.filter(([opened]) => opened === path);
}

/** The error `promise` rejects with; fails the test if it resolves. */
async function rejection(promise: Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
  try {
    await promise;
  } catch (error) {
    return error;
  }
  throw new Error('the promise resolved');
}

/** Writes `content` as JSON to `name` in the temp folder and returns its path. */
async function jsonFile(name: string, content: unknown): Promise<string> {
  const path = join(dir, name);
  await writeFile(path, JSON.stringify(content));
  return path;
}

/** The fields near-cli-rs writes to a legacy keychain file: no account_id. */
function nearCliRsFile(keyPair: KeyPair): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    implicit_account_id: Buffer.from(keyPair.getPublicKey().data).toString('hex'),
    master_seed_phrase: 'placeholder words, not read by readKeyFile',
    private_key: keyPair.toString(),
    public_key: keyPair.getPublicKey().toString(),
    seed_phrase_hd_path: "m/44'/397'/0'",
  };
}

describe('key file paths', () => {
  it('keyFilePath is <dir>/testnet/<account>.json on testnet and <dir>/sandbox/… on a sandbox', () => {
    expect(keyFilePath('/keys', 'near:testnet', ACCOUNT)).toBe(join('/keys', 'testnet', `${ACCOUNT}.json`));
    expect(keyFilePath('/keys', 'near:sandbox', 'test.near')).toBe(join('/keys', 'sandbox', 'test.near.json'));
  });

  it('keyFolderPath is <dir>/<network>/<account>, the folder of an account with several keys', () => {
    expect(keyFolderPath('/keys', 'near:testnet', 'relay.parent.testnet')).toBe(
      join('/keys', 'testnet', 'relay.parent.testnet'),
    );
  });

  it('refuses an account id that is not one, so that no path leaves the folder', () => {
    expect(() => keyFilePath('/keys', 'near:testnet', '../../evil')).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => keyFolderPath('/keys', 'near:testnet', 'a/b')).toThrow(RangeError);
  });

  it("folderKeyPath names a key's file after its public key, with ':' replaced by '_'", () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const base58 = keyPair.getPublicKey().toString().slice('ed25519:'.length);
    expect(folderKeyPath('/keys/relay', keyPair.getPublicKey())).toBe(join('/keys/relay', `ed25519_${base58}.json`));
  });

  it("defaultCredentialsDir is near-cli's ~/.near-credentials", () => {
    expect(defaultCredentialsDir()).toBe(join(homedir(), '.near-credentials'));
  });
});

describe('writeKeyFile', () => {
  it('writes the account id and the key pair, which readKeyFile reads back', async () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const path = join(dir, 'testnet', `${ACCOUNT}.json`);
    await writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, keyPair);
    expect(JSON.parse(await readFile(path, 'utf8'))).toEqual({
      account_id: ACCOUNT,
      public_key: keyPair.getPublicKey().toString(),
      private_key: keyPair.toString(),
    });
    expect((await readKeyFile(path)).toString()).toBe(keyPair.toString());
  });

  it('creates the missing folders', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'a', 'b', 'key.json');
    await writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'));
    expect((await stat(path)).isFile()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('flushes the file to disk as it writes it, so that it is there before the transaction that funds its key', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'key.json');
    await writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'));
    const calls = vi.mocked(writeFile).mock.calls.filter(([written]) => written === path);
    expect(calls).toEqual([[path, expect.any(String), { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600, flush: true }]]);
  });

  it('replaces an empty file, which a write cut short leaves, with the new key', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'key.json');
    await writeFile(path, '');
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    await writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, keyPair);
    expect((await readKeyFile(path)).toString()).toBe(keyPair.toString());
  });

  it('never overwrites a file that is not empty, even one that holds no key', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'key.json');
    await writeFile(path, '{');
    const error = await rejection(writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')));
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ name: 'KeyFileError', problem: 'exists', path });
    expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toBe('{');
  });

  it("syncs the file's folder on POSIX systems, so that the new entry survives a power loss", async () => {
    const folder = join(dir, 'testnet');
    const path = join(folder, `${ACCOUNT}.json`);
    const handle = { sync: vi.fn(async () => {}), close: vi.fn(async () => {}) };
    vi.mocked(open).mockImplementationOnce(async () => handle as unknown as Awaited<ReturnType<typeof open>>);
    await onPlatform('linux', () => writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')));
    expect(opened(folder)).toEqual([[folder, 'r']]);
    expect(handle.sync).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(handle.close).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it.each(['EISDIR', 'EINVAL', 'EPERM', 'ENOTSUP'])(
    'writes the key file when the file system refuses to sync a folder with %s',
    async (code) => {
      const path = join(dir, 'key.json');
      vi.mocked(open).mockImplementationOnce(async () => {
        throw Object.assign(new Error(`${code}: cannot sync`), { code });
      });
      const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
      await onPlatform('linux', () => writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, keyPair));
      expect((await readKeyFile(path)).toString()).toBe(keyPair.toString());
    },
  );

  it('passes on any other error from syncing the folder', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'key.json');
    const failure = Object.assign(new Error('EIO: i/o error'), { code: 'EIO' });
    vi.mocked(open).mockImplementationOnce(async () => {
      throw failure;
    });
    let error: unknown;
    await onPlatform('linux', async () => {
      error = await rejection(writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')));
    });
    expect(error).toBe(failure);
  });

  it('does not open the folder on Windows, which cannot sync one', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'key.json');
    await onPlatform('win32', () => writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')));
    expect(opened(dirname(path))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('never overwrites a key file', async () => {
    const first = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const path = join(dir, 'key.json');
    await writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, first);
    const error = await rejection(writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(KeyFileError);
    expect((error as KeyFileError).problem).toBe('exists');
    expect((error as KeyFileError).path).toBe(path);
    expect((await readKeyFile(path)).toString()).toBe(first.toString());
  });

  // Node applies only the read-only bit of a mode on Windows.
  it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')('makes the file readable by its owner only, and the folder too', async () => {
    const folder = join(dir, 'testnet');
    const path = join(folder, `${ACCOUNT}.json`);
    await writeKeyFile(path, ACCOUNT, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'));
    expect((await stat(path)).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o600);
    expect((await stat(folder)).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o700);
  });
});

describe('readKeyFile', () => {
  it('reads the file near-cli-rs writes, which has no account_id', async () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const path = await jsonFile('near-cli-rs.json', nearCliRsFile(keyPair));
    expect((await readKeyFile(path)).toString()).toBe(keyPair.toString());
  });

  it('falls back to secret_key when there is no private_key', async () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const path = await jsonFile('secret-key-field.json', {
      account_id: ACCOUNT,
      public_key: keyPair.getPublicKey().toString(),
      secret_key: keyPair.toString(),
    });
    expect((await readKeyFile(path)).toString()).toBe(keyPair.toString());
  });

  it('reads a file without public_key', async () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const path = await jsonFile('no-public-key.json', { private_key: keyPair.toString() });
    expect((await readKeyFile(path)).toString()).toBe(keyPair.toString());
  });

  it('refuses a file whose public_key is not that of its private key, without quoting either', async () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const other = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519').getPublicKey().toString();
    const path = await jsonFile('mismatch.json', { private_key: keyPair.toString(), public_key: other });
    const error = await rejection(readKeyFile(path));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(KeyFileError);
    expect((error as KeyFileError).problem).toBe('invalid');
    expect((error as Error).message).toContain(path);
    expect((error as Error).message).not.toContain(keyPair.toString());
    expect((error as Error).message).not.toContain(other);
  });

  it('reports a missing file as missing', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'nowhere.json');
    const error = await rejection(readKeyFile(path));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(KeyFileError);
    expect((error as KeyFileError).problem).toBe('missing');
    expect((error as KeyFileError).path).toBe(path);
  });

  it('reports an empty file, which a write cut short leaves, as missing', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, 'empty.json');
    await writeFile(path, '');
    const error = await rejection(readKeyFile(path));
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ name: 'KeyFileError', problem: 'missing', path });
    expect((error as Error).message).toContain('is empty');
  });

  const malformed: [string, string][] = [
    ['text that is not JSON', 'ed25519:not json'],
    ['JSON that is not an object', '["ed25519:x"]'],
    ['an object without a private key', '{"public_key":"ed25519:x"}'],
    ['a private key that is not a string', '{"private_key":42}'],
    ['a private key that does not parse', '{"private_key":"ed25519:0OIl-not-base58"}'],
  ];
  it.each(malformed)('refuses %s, without quoting the file', async (_name, content) => {
    const path = join(dir, 'malformed.json');
    await writeFile(path, content);
    const error = await rejection(readKeyFile(path));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(KeyFileError);
    expect((error as KeyFileError).problem).toBe('invalid');
    expect((error as Error).message).toContain(path);
    expect((error as Error).message).not.toContain('ed25519:');
    expect((error as Error).cause).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe('readKeyFolder', () => {
  it('reads every key of the folder, sorted by public key', async () => {
    const folder = keyFolderPath(dir, 'near:testnet', 'relay.parent.testnet');
    const keys = [KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'), KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'), KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')];
    for (const keyPair of keys) await writeKeyFile(folderKeyPath(folder, keyPair.getPublicKey()), 'relay.parent.testnet', keyPair);
    const publicKeys = keys.map((keyPair) => keyPair.getPublicKey().toString()).sort();
    const read = await readKeyFolder(folder);
    expect(read.map((keyPair) => keyPair.getPublicKey().toString())).toEqual(publicKeys);
  });

  it('reads the files near-cli-rs writes there', async () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    await writeFile(folderKeyPath(dir, keyPair.getPublicKey()), JSON.stringify(nearCliRsFile(keyPair)));
    expect((await readKeyFolder(dir)).map(String)).toEqual([keyPair.toString()]);
  });

  it('skips an empty file, which a write cut short leaves: it holds no key', async () => {
    const folder = join(dir, 'relay.parent.testnet');
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    await writeKeyFile(folderKeyPath(folder, keyPair.getPublicKey()), ACCOUNT, keyPair);
    await writeFile(folderKeyPath(folder, KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519').getPublicKey()), '');
    expect((await readKeyFolder(folder)).map((key) => key.toString())).toEqual([keyPair.toString()]);
  });

  it('skips entries that are not .json files', async () => {
    await writeFile(join(dir, 'notes.txt'), 'not a key');
    await mkdir(join(dir, 'nested.json'));
    expect(await readKeyFolder(dir)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('refuses a file that is not named after its key', async () => {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    const path = join(dir, 'copy.json');
    await writeKeyFile(path, 'relay.parent.testnet', keyPair);
    const error = await rejection(readKeyFolder(dir));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(KeyFileError);
    expect((error as KeyFileError).problem).toBe('invalid');
    expect((error as KeyFileError).path).toBe(path);
  });

  it('reports a missing folder as missing', async () => {
    const folder = join(dir, 'relay.parent.testnet');
    const error = await rejection(readKeyFolder(folder));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(KeyFileError);
    expect((error as KeyFileError).problem).toBe('missing');
    expect((error as KeyFileError).path).toBe(folder);
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { defaultSpendFile, readSpendFile, SpendFileError, writeSpendFile } from '../src/spend-file.ts';

const ACCOUNT = 'buyer-llm.parent.testnet';

let dir: string;
let file: string;

beforeEach(async () => {
  dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'quorum-spend-file-'));
  file = join(dir, 'mcp-spend.json');
});

afterEach(async () => {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

/** The error `promise` rejects with; fails the test if it resolves. */
async function rejection(promise: Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
  try {
    await promise;
  } catch (error) {
    return error;
  }
  throw new Error('the promise resolved');
}

describe('defaultSpendFile', () => {
  it('is data/mcp-spend.json at the root of the repository, whatever the current folder', () => {
    const path = defaultSpendFile();
    expect(basename(path)).toBe('mcp-spend.json');
    expect(basename(dirname(path))).toBe('data');
    // The tests run from packages/buyer, so a path read against the current folder would miss the root.
    expect(existsSync(join(dirname(dirname(path)), 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'))).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('readSpendFile', () => {
  it('reads a missing file as nothing spent', async () => {
    expect(await readSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT)).toBe(0n);
  });

  it("reads back the account's total that writeSpendFile wrote", async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT, 3_600n);
    expect(await readSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT)).toBe(3_600n);
  });

  it("refuses another account's file", async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(file, 'buyer-01.parent.testnet', 180n);
    const error = await rejection(readSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(SpendFileError);
    expect((error as SpendFileError).problem).toBe('other_account');
    expect((error as SpendFileError).path).toBe(file);
  });

  const malformed: [string, string][] = [
    ['text that is not JSON', 'spent: 3600'],
    ['JSON that is not an object', '"3600"'],
    ['a file without an account', '{"spent":"3600"}'],
    ['a total written as a number', `{"account":"${ACCOUNT}","spent":3600}`],
    ['a negative total', `{"account":"${ACCOUNT}","spent":"-1"}`],
    ['a total with a leading zero', `{"account":"${ACCOUNT}","spent":"0360"}`],
  ];
  it.each(malformed)('refuses %s', async (_name, content) => {
    await writeFile(file, content);
    const error = await rejection(readSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(SpendFileError);
    expect((error as SpendFileError).problem).toBe('malformed');
  });
});

describe('writeSpendFile', () => {
  it('writes the account and its total as a decimal string', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT, 10_000n);
    expect(JSON.parse(await readFile(file, 'utf8'))).toEqual({ account: ACCOUNT, spent: '10000' });
  });

  it('creates the missing folders', async () => {
    const nested = join(dir, 'a', 'b', 'mcp-spend.json');
    await writeSpendFile(nested, ACCOUNT, 1n);
    expect(await readSpendFile(nested, ACCOUNT)).toBe(1n);
  });

  it('replaces the total, leaving no temporary file in the folder', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT, 360n);
    await writeSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT, 0n);
    expect(await readSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT)).toBe(0n);
    expect(await readdir(dir)).toEqual(['mcp-spend.json']);
  });

  it('removes its temporary file when the total cannot be put in place', async () => {
    // A folder where the file should be: the rename that would replace it fails.
    await mkdir(file);
    await expect(writeSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT, 360n)).rejects.toThrow();
    expect(await readdir(dir)).toEqual(['mcp-spend.json']);

  it('refuses a negative total', async () => {
    await expect(writeSpendFile(file, ACCOUNT, -1n)).rejects.toThrow(RangeError);

  });
});
```
