`packages/buyer/src/settings.ts`:

```typescript
import { isAbsolute } from 'node:path';
import { isAccountId } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { nearToYocto } from 'near-api-js';
import { defaultCredentialsDir } from './key-files.ts';
import { defaultSpendFile } from './spend-file.ts';

/** Environment variables, as `process.env` holds them. */
export type Env = Record<string, string | undefined>;

/** The networks a buyer pays on: NEAR testnet, or a local sandbox chain. */
export type BuyerNetwork = 'near:testnet' | 'near:sandbox';

/** Circle's USDC on NEAR testnet, the default token. */
export const TESTNET_USDC = '3e2210e1184b45b64c8a434c0a7e7b23cc04ea7eb7a6c3c32520d03d4afcb8af';

/**
 * What a buyer shares with the gateway, and the bound it puts on what it signs. Each shared value is
 * read from the gateway's own variable, with the gateway's default, so that one value configures every
 * app.
 */
export interface BuyerSettings {
  /** QUORUM_NETWORK: the network offers and payments name. */
  network: BuyerNetwork;
  /** QUORUM_RPC_URL: the NEAR RPC endpoint, as written. */
  rpcUrl: string;
  /**
   * QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL, without a trailing slash: where the gateway is reached. Its host is the
   * recipient of redemption proofs, so it must be written as the gateway's own QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL.
   */
  gatewayUrl: string;
  /** QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: the account the system's accounts are created under. */
  parent: string;
  /** QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT: the token the pools contract was initialised with. */
  token: string;
  /** QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT: the pools contract, `pools.<parent>` by default. */
  poolsContract: string;
  /** QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS: the average block time that turns an offer's timeout into blocks. */
  blockTimeMs: number;
  /**
   * QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: the longest a payment the buyer signs stays valid, 30 to 3600
   * seconds (120 by default). The buyer's own bound, not the gateway's: a payment expires after the
   * offer's timeout or this one, whichever is shorter.
   */
  maxTimeoutSeconds: number;
}

/** How one variable is read. */
export interface Rule<T> {
  /** Completes "<VARIABLE> must be …". */
  expected: string;
  /** The value, or undefined when `raw` is invalid. */
  parse(raw: string): T | undefined;
  /**
   * True for a value that may hold a secret, such as a URL with an API key in its query or path: a
   * problem line then names the variable and never quotes the value.
   */
  secret?: boolean;
}

/** A configuration being read: a value is undefined when its variable has a problem. */
export type Draft<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] | undefined };

/** Thrown by completeConfig with every missing or invalid variable, one per line of its message. */
export class ConfigError extends Error {
  override name = 'ConfigError';
  readonly problems: readonly string[];

  constructor(problems: readonly string[]) {
    super(problems.join('\n'));
    this.problems = problems;
  }
}

/**
 * Reads variables from `env` with rules, appending one line to `problems` for each variable that is
 * missing or invalid, so that a loader can list every problem at once. A value with a problem is
 * returned as undefined. Problem lines quote the raw value, except for a rule marked `secret`, such as
 * the URL rules: a URL may carry an API key.
 */
export class EnvReader {
  readonly #env: Env;
  readonly #problems: string[];

  constructor(env: Env, problems: string[]) {
    this.#env = env;
    this.#problems = problems;
  }

  /** The variable read with `rule`, or `fallback` read with it when the variable is unset. */
  optional<T>(name: string, fallback: string, rule: Rule<T>): T | undefined {
    return this.#check(name, this.#env[name] ?? fallback, rule);
  }

  /** The variable read with `rule`; a problem when it is unset or empty. */
  required<T>(name: string, rule: Rule<T>): T | undefined {
    const raw = this.#env[name];
    if (raw !== undefined && raw !== '') return this.#check(name, raw, rule);
    this.#problems.push(`${name} is required`);
    return undefined;
  }

  /** The variable read with `rule`, or null when it is unset or empty. */
  nullable<T>(name: string, rule: Rule<T>): T | null | undefined {
    const raw = this.#env[name];
    return raw === undefined || raw === '' ? null : this.#check(name, raw, rule);
  }

  /**
   * An account id that defaults to `<prefix>.<parent>`. Without a valid parent there is no default,
   * and the parent's problem is already listed, so an unset variable then gives undefined silently.
   */
  child(name: string, prefix: string, parent: string | undefined): string | undefined {
    const raw = this.#env[name] ?? (parent === undefined ? undefined : `${prefix}.${parent}`);
    return raw === undefined ? undefined : this.#check(name, raw, asAccountId);
  }

  #check<T>(name: string, raw: string, rule: Rule<T>): T | undefined {
    const value = rule.parse(raw);
    if (value === undefined) {
      const got = rule.secret === true ? '' : `, got ${JSON.stringify(raw)}`;
      this.#problems.push(`${name} must be ${rule.expected}${got}`);
    }
    return value;
  }
}

/**
 * The configuration once every variable has been read: throws a ConfigError listing `problems` if
 * there are any. A loader only leaves a value undefined after listing its problem, so without
 * problems every value of the draft is defined.
 */
export function completeConfig<T>(draft: Draft<T>, problems: readonly string[]): T {
  if (problems.length > 0) throw new ConfigError(problems);
  return draft as T;
}

/**
 * Reads the buyer settings from the gateway's variables and defaults (see BuyerSettings), appending
 * a line to `problems` for each missing or invalid one. The caller reads its own variables into the
 * same list, then calls completeConfig.
 */
export function readBuyerSettings(env: Env, problems: string[]): Draft<BuyerSettings> {
  const read = new EnvReader(env, problems);
  const network = read.optional('QUORUM_NETWORK', 'near:testnet', asNetwork);
  const rpcUrl = read.optional('QUORUM_RPC_URL', 'https://test.rpc.fastnear.com', asHttpUrl);
  const gatewayUrl = read.optional('QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL', 'http://localhost:8402', asBaseUrl);
  const parent = read.required('QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT', asAccountId);
  const token = read.optional('QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT', TESTNET_USDC, asAccountId);
  const poolsContract = read.child('QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT', 'pools', parent);
  const blockTimeMs = read.optional('QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS', '1000', asPositiveInteger);
  const maxTimeoutSeconds = read.optional('QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS', '120', asTimeoutSeconds);
  return { network, rpcUrl, gatewayUrl, parent, token, poolsContract, blockTimeMs, maxTimeoutSeconds };
}

/**
 * The MCP server's buyer, as both the swarm, which creates and funds it and clears its spend total,
 * and the MCP server, which acts for it and keeps that total, read it, with one set of defaults.
 */
export interface McpBuyerSettings {
  /** QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT: the buyer the MCP server acts for, `buyer-llm.<parent>` by default. */
  mcpAccount: string;
  /** QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR: the folder of the key files, `~/.near-credentials` by default. */
  credentialsDir: string;
  /** QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE: the MCP server's running spend total, `data/mcp-spend.json` at the repository root by default. */
  spendFile: string;
}

/**
 * Reads the MCP server's buyer (see McpBuyerSettings), appending a line to `problems` for each
 * invalid variable. `parent` is the parent account readBuyerSettings read: without it the buyer has
 * no default, and the parent's problem is listed already.
 */
export function readMcpBuyerSettings(env: Env, problems: string[], parent: string | undefined): Draft<McpBuyerSettings> {
  const read = new EnvReader(env, problems);
  return {
    mcpAccount: read.child('QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT', 'buyer-llm', parent),
    credentialsDir: read.optional('QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR', defaultCredentialsDir(), asAbsolutePath),
    spendFile: read.optional('QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE', defaultSpendFile(), asAbsolutePath),
  };
}

const NETWORKS: readonly BuyerNetwork[] = ['near:testnet', 'near:sandbox'];
const INTEGER = /^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/;
/** A NEAR amount: whole NEAR, then up to 24 decimals (yoctoNEAR). */
const NEAR_AMOUNT = /^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]{1,24})?$/;

const asNetwork: Rule<BuyerNetwork> = {
  expected: NETWORKS.join(' or '),
  parse: (raw) => NETWORKS.find((network) => network === raw),
};

/** An http or https URL, kept as written. It may carry an API key, so a problem never quotes it. */
const asHttpUrl: Rule<string> = {
  expected: 'an http or https URL',
  parse: (raw) => (URL.canParse(raw) && ['http:', 'https:'].includes(new URL(raw).protocol) ? raw : undefined),
  secret: true,
};

/** An http or https URL with its trailing slashes removed, as the gateway reads its own URL. */
const asBaseUrl: Rule<string> = {
  expected: asHttpUrl.expected,
  parse: (raw) => asHttpUrl.parse(raw)?.replace(/\/+$/, ''),
  secret: true,
};

/**
 * A payment's longest life, in seconds. At least 30, so that a payment signed on a slow chain still
 * lies more than the gateway's 5-block margin ahead of the final height; at most an hour.
 */
const asTimeoutSeconds = asInteger(30, 3600);

const asAccountId: Rule<string> = {
  expected: 'a NEAR account id',
  parse: (raw) => (isAccountId(raw) ? raw : undefined),
};

/** A decimal integer from `min` to `max`, written without sign or leading zero. */
export function asInteger(min: number, max: number, expected = `an integer from ${min} to ${max}`): Rule<number> {
  return {
    expected,
    parse(raw) {
      const value = INTEGER.test(raw) ? Number(raw) : Number.NaN;
      return value >= min && value <= max ? value : undefined;
    },
  };
}

/** A decimal integer from 1 to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. */
export const asPositiveInteger: Rule<number> = asInteger(1, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, 'a positive integer');

/** An amount in a token's base units: decimal digits, no sign, no leading zero. */
export const asAmount: Rule<bigint> = {
  expected: 'an amount in base units (decimal digits, such as 10000)',
  parse: (raw) => (INTEGER.test(raw) ? BigInt(raw) : undefined),
};

/**
 * An amount of NEAR written as a decimal number, such as `0.05`, read into yoctoNEAR. The string is
 * converted as written: a JS number would turn 0.0000001 into `1e-7`, which nearToYocto refuses.
 */
export const asNear: Rule<bigint> = {
  expected: 'an amount of NEAR as a decimal number with at most 24 decimals, such as 0.05',
  parse: (raw) => (NEAR_AMOUNT.test(raw) ? nearToYocto(raw as `${number}`) : undefined),
};

/** An absolute path. A relative one would depend on the folder the process was started from. */
export const asAbsolutePath: Rule<string> = {
  expected: 'an absolute path',
  parse: (raw) => (isAbsolute(raw) ? raw : undefined),
};
```

```typescript
import { mkdir, open, readdir, readFile, stat, unlink, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { isAccountId } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { KeyPair, type KeyPairString, type PublicKey } from 'near-api-js';
import type { BuyerNetwork } from './settings.ts';

/**
 * Key files in near-cli's legacy keychain layout: `<dir>/<network>/<account>.json` for an account's
 * key, and `<dir>/<network>/<account>/<public key>.json`, one file per key, for an account with
 * several keys (near-cli-rs writes both forms when it saves a key to the legacy keychain).
 */

/** The keychain's folder for each network. */
const NETWORK_FOLDERS: Record<BuyerNetwork, string> = {
  'near:testnet': 'testnet',
  'near:sandbox': 'sandbox',
};

/** What is wrong with a key file: there is none, there is one already, or it cannot be read as a key. */
export type KeyFileProblem = 'missing' | 'exists' | 'invalid';

/**
 * A key file or key folder that is missing, already exists, or does not hold a key. The message names
 * the path and never quotes the file's content.
 */
export class KeyFileError extends Error {
  override name = 'KeyFileError';
  readonly path: string;
  readonly problem: KeyFileProblem;

  constructor(path: string, problem: KeyFileProblem, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.path = path;
    this.problem = problem;
  }
}

/** near-cli's credentials folder, `~/.near-credentials`. */
export function defaultCredentialsDir(): string {
  return join(homedir(), '.near-credentials');
}

/** `<dir>/<network>/<accountId>.json`. Throws RangeError unless `accountId` is a NEAR account id. */
export function keyFilePath(dir: string, network: BuyerNetwork, accountId: string): string {
  return `${keyFolderPath(dir, network, accountId)}.json`;
}

/**
 * `<dir>/<network>/<accountId>`: the folder of an account with several keys. Throws RangeError unless
 * `accountId` is a NEAR account id, which holds no path separator and no `..`.
 */
export function keyFolderPath(dir: string, network: BuyerNetwork, accountId: string): string {
  if (!isAccountId(accountId)) throw new RangeError(`not a NEAR account id: ${JSON.stringify(accountId)}`);
  return join(dir, NETWORK_FOLDERS[network], accountId);
}

/** The file of one key in an account's key folder: `<folder>/<public key with ':' as '_'>.json`. */
export function folderKeyPath(folder: string, publicKey: PublicKey): string {
  return join(folder, folderKeyName(publicKey));
}

/**
 * Reads the key pair in a key file: the JSON that near-cli-rs writes (`public_key`, `private_key`
 * and seed-phrase fields, no `account_id`) or that writeKeyFile and the older near-cli write
 * (`account_id`, `public_key`, `private_key`). Reads `private_key`, or `secret_key` when it is absent,
 * and checks that `public_key`, when present, is that key's. Throws KeyFileError (`missing` or
 * `invalid`) otherwise. An empty file is `missing`: it is what a write cut short between creating the
 * file and writing it leaves, and it holds no key.
 */
export async function readKeyFile(path: string): Promise<KeyPair> {
  let text: string;
  try {
    text = await readFile(path, 'utf8');
  } catch (error) {
    if (errorCode(error) === 'ENOENT') throw new KeyFileError(path, 'missing', `there is no key file at ${path}`);
    throw error;
  }
  if (text === '') throw new KeyFileError(path, 'missing', `the key file ${path} is empty: a write was cut short`);
  return parseKeyFile(text, path);
}

/**
 * Writes `{account_id, public_key, private_key}` to a new file readable by its owner only (mode
 * 0o600), creating its folder (mode 0o700) if needed. The file is flushed to disk before the promise
 * resolves, and on POSIX systems its folder is synced too, so that a key written before the
 * transaction that funds it survives a crash of the machine, not only of the process. Never
 * overwrites a file that holds anything: throws KeyFileError (`exists`) if there is one. An empty file
 * holds no key (see readKeyFile), so it is replaced, once. The modes apply on POSIX systems; Windows
 * keeps only a read-only flag.
 */
export async function writeKeyFile(path: string, accountId: string, keyPair: KeyPair): Promise<void> {
  const content = { account_id: accountId, public_key: keyPair.getPublicKey().toString(), private_key: keyPair.toString() };
  const text = `${JSON.stringify(content)}\n`;
  await mkdir(dirname(path), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  try {
    await writeNew(path, text);
  } catch (error) {
    if (errorCode(error) !== 'EEXIST') throw error;
    if ((await stat(path)).size !== 0) throw new KeyFileError(path, 'exists', `there is a key file at ${path} already`);
    await unlink(path);
    try {
      await writeNew(path, text);
    } catch (again) {
      if (errorCode(again) === 'EEXIST') throw new KeyFileError(path, 'exists', `there is a key file at ${path} already`);
      throw again;
    }
  }
  await syncFolder(dirname(path));
}

/** Creates `path` with `text`, failing with EEXIST if it exists, and flushes it to disk. */
function writeNew(path: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
  return writeFile(path, text, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600, flush: true });
}

/** The errors of a file system that cannot sync a folder, which leave the file itself written. */
const UNSYNCABLE_FOLDER: ReadonlySet<unknown> = new Set(['EISDIR', 'EINVAL', 'EPERM', 'ENOTSUP']);

/**
 * Syncs a folder, so that a file just created in it is still listed after a power loss. Skipped on
 * Windows, which cannot open a folder to sync it; ignored where the file system refuses it.
 */
async function syncFolder(folder: string): Promise<void> {
  if (process.platform === 'win32') return;
  try {
    const handle = await open(folder, 'r');
    try {
      await handle.sync();
    } finally {
      await handle.close();
    }
  } catch (error) {
    if (!UNSYNCABLE_FOLDER.has(errorCode(error))) throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * Reads every `.json` file of an account's key folder as a key file, sorted by public key. Each file
 * must be named after its key (folderKeyPath), so no key is listed twice. Other entries are skipped,
 * and so is a file that readKeyFile reports `missing`: an empty one, which a write cut short leaves,
 * or one removed since the folder was listed. Throws KeyFileError: `missing` for a missing folder, or
 * readKeyFile's error for a file.
 */
export async function readKeyFolder(folder: string): Promise<KeyPair[]> {
  let names: string[];
  try {
    const entries = await readdir(folder, { withFileTypes: true });
    names = entries.filter((entry) => entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith('.json')).map((entry) => entry.name);
  } catch (error) {
    if (errorCode(error) === 'ENOENT') throw new KeyFileError(folder, 'missing', `there is no key folder at ${folder}`);
    throw error;
  }
  const keys: { publicKey: string; keyPair: KeyPair }[] = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    const path = join(folder, name);
    let keyPair: KeyPair;
    try {
      keyPair = await readKeyFile(path);
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof KeyFileError && error.problem === 'missing') continue;
      throw error;
    }
    if (folderKeyName(keyPair.getPublicKey()) !== name) {
      throw new KeyFileError(path, 'invalid', `the key file ${path} is not named after its public key`);
    }
    keys.push({ publicKey: keyPair.getPublicKey().toString(), keyPair });
  }
  keys.sort((a, b) => (a.publicKey < b.publicKey ? -1 : a.publicKey > b.publicKey ? 1 : 0));
  return keys.map((key) => key.keyPair);
}

function folderKeyName(publicKey: PublicKey): string {
  return `${publicKey.toString().replace(':', '_')}.json`;
}

/** The key pair in a key file's text. Nothing the parsers throw is kept: their messages may quote the key. */
function parseKeyFile(text: string, path: string): KeyPair {
  const invalid = (why: string): KeyFileError => new KeyFileError(path, 'invalid', `the key file ${path} ${why}`);
  let value: unknown;
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    throw invalid('is not JSON');
  }
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) throw invalid('is not a JSON object');
  const fields = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const privateKey = fields.private_key ?? fields.secret_key;
  if (typeof privateKey !== 'string') throw invalid('has no private_key or secret_key string');
  let keyPair: KeyPair;
  try {
    keyPair = KeyPair.fromString(privateKey as KeyPairString);
  } catch {
    throw invalid('holds a private key that is not a NEAR key');
  }
  if (fields.public_key !== undefined && fields.public_key !== keyPair.getPublicKey().toString()) {
    throw invalid('holds a public_key that is not the public key of its private key');
  }
  return keyPair;
}

function errorCode(error: unknown): unknown {
  return (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException | null)?.code;
}
```

`packages/buyer/src/spend-file.ts`:

```typescript
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdir, readFile, rename, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { parseAmount } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';

/**
 * The MCP server's running total of what its buyer has spent, in the token's base units, kept on
 * disk so that a restart does not reset it: `{"account": "<buyer>", "spent": "<base units>"}`. The
 * MCP server keeps it. `swarm setup` clears it on every run whose token top-ups go through, also when
 * none was needed, so that the cap bounds what the buyer spends between two such runs; a run stopped
 * before then, by a token shortfall for one, leaves it.
 */

/** What is wrong with a spend file: it holds another account's total, or no total at all. */
export type SpendFileProblem = 'other_account' | 'malformed';

/** A spend file that holds another account's total or cannot be read as one. */
export class SpendFileError extends Error {
  override name = 'SpendFileError';
  readonly path: string;
  readonly problem: SpendFileProblem;

  constructor(path: string, problem: SpendFileProblem, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.path = path;
    this.problem = problem;
  }
}

/**
 * `data/mcp-spend.json` at the root of the repository, which is gitignored. Resolved from this
 * module's own location, so it does not depend on the folder the process was started from.
 */
export function defaultSpendFile(): string {
  return fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../data/mcp-spend.json', import.meta.url));
}

/**
 * The total `account` has spent: 0 when there is no file. Throws SpendFileError for a file that holds
 * another account's total (`other_account`) or is not a spend file (`malformed`).
 */
export async function readSpendFile(path: string, account: string): Promise<bigint> {
  let text: string;
  try {
    text = await readFile(path, 'utf8');
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return 0n;
    throw error;
  }
  const malformed = (): SpendFileError =>
    new SpendFileError(path, 'malformed', `the spend file ${path} does not hold an account and a decimal total`);
  let value: unknown;
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    throw malformed();
  }
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) throw malformed();
  const fields = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const spent = parseAmount(fields.spent);
  if (typeof fields.account !== 'string' || spent === null) throw malformed();
  if (fields.account !== account) {
    throw new SpendFileError(path, 'other_account', `the spend file ${path} holds another account's total, not ${account}'s`);
  }
  return spent;
}

/**
 * Writes `account`'s total atomically: to a new temporary file in the same folder, then renamed over
 * `path`, so that a reader, or a process stopped mid-write, sees the old total or the new one, never
 * part of one. Creates the folder if needed. Writes to one file must not overlap: the caller
 * serialises them. Throws RangeError for a negative total.
 */
export async function writeSpendFile(path: string, account: string, spent: bigint): Promise<void> {
  if (spent < 0n) throw new RangeError(`a spent total cannot be negative: ${spent}`);
  const folder = dirname(path);
  await mkdir(folder, { recursive: true });
  const temporary = join(folder, `.${basename(path)}.${randomUUID()}.tmp`);
  try {
    await writeFile(temporary, `${JSON.stringify({ account, spent: spent.toString() })}\n`, { flag: 'wx' });
    await rename(temporary, path);
  } catch (error) {
    await rm(temporary, { force: true });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

---

### Task 4: The buyer package: the gateway client

`GatewayClient` is a typed client of the gateway's HTTP API (sections 6.1 to 6.5 and 6.7). Each
method sends one `GET`, never repeats it, and returns the documented answer as a discriminated union
on `kind`. The gateway is outside the buyer's trust (section 6.3), so:

- the client follows no redirect (`redirect: 'error'`), which would carry a payment or a proof to
  another server;
- every body is checked field by field and only the documented fields are kept; the strings a buyer
  passes on are bounded, so that an answer cannot carry megabytes of text to whoever reads it (a
  pool's terms to the 280 UTF-8 bytes the pools contract keeps, a transaction hash to the 44 base58
  characters of a NEAR hash, a credential to 4096 characters), and an offer's `resource` and
  `description` are kept as sent, since nothing passes them on;
- any other answer (an undocumented status, a body that is not JSON, a field missing or malformed) is
  a `GatewayResponseError` that names the request, the HTTP status and the field, and quotes nothing
  from the body, which may hold a credential;
- a pool id that is not a non-negative safe integer, or a seat count outside 1 to 1000
  (`MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST`), is a `RangeError` before anything is sent; no answer at all is fetch's
  own rejection.

The answers it knows:

| Request | Answers |
|---|---|
| `pools()`: `GET /pools` | `200` the listing (`pools`); `503` `unavailable` |
| `offer(poolId, seats)`: `GET /pools/:id/access?seats=N` | `402` with exactly one offer (`offer`); `404` `unknown_pool`; `409` `pool_closed` with the pool's status (`open`, `filled` or `settled`); `410` `pool_expired` (`expired` or `refunded`); `503` `unavailable` |
| `pay(poolId, seats, header)`: the same URL with `X-PAYMENT` | `202` `pending` and `200` `filled`, each with the transaction of `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` (a `202` receipt naming another transaction is undocumented); `402` `refused` with its code and the offer, if any; `409` `no_seats_taken`; `410` `pool_expired` with its transaction; `502` `relay_failed` or `result_unknown` with its transaction; `404` `unknown_pool`; `503` `unavailable` |
| `redeem(poolId, header)`: `GET /pools/:id/access` with `X-QUORUM-PROOF` | `202` `pending`; `200` `filled`; `410` `refund` with its status (`refunded`, `refund_pending` or `claimable`), amount, bonus share and transaction or null; `401` `invalid_proof` with its code; `404` `no_seats` or `unknown_pool`; `503` `unavailable` |
| `activity(poolId)`: `GET /activity?pool=<id>` | `200` the pool's records, oldest first |

Amounts in the client's own types (`PoolListing`, `ActivityRecord`, a refund) are `bigint` base
units, converted once from the gateway's decimal strings; the protocol's `Offer` keeps the decimal
strings of the wire, since the buyer signs the offer as it was sent. The tests give the client a
recording `fetch` (`test/stub-gateway.ts`) that answers as the gateway does, with offers built by the
protocol package's own `buildOffer`; Task 5's tests use it too.

- Create: `packages/buyer/src/gateway.ts`
- Modify: `packages/buyer/src/index.ts` (adds `export * from './gateway.ts'`)
- Test: `packages/buyer/test/gateway.test.ts`, `packages/buyer/test/stub-gateway.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing from earlier tasks of this plan. From the protocol package on `main`:
  `PAYMENT_HEADER`, `PAYMENT_RESPONSE_HEADER`, `PROOF_HEADER`, `decodeHeader`, `isAccountId`,
  `parseAmount`, `type Network`, `type Offer`, `type PaymentErrorCode`, `type PoolStatus`,
  `type ProofErrorCode`; in the tests, `buildOffer`, `encodeHeader`, `paymentRequired`.
- Produces, from `gateway.ts`:
  - `export class GatewayClient { constructor(opts: { gatewayUrl: string; fetch?: typeof fetch }); pools(): Promise<PoolsAnswer>; offer(poolId: number, seats: number): Promise<OfferAnswer>; pay(poolId: number, seats: number, paymentHeader: string): Promise<PaymentAnswer>; redeem(poolId: number, proofHeader: string): Promise<RedeemAnswer>; activity(poolId: number): Promise<ActivityRecord[]> }`
  - `export const MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST = 1000`
  - `export function checkAccessRequest(poolId: number, seats: number): void` (throws `RangeError`)
  - `export class GatewayResponseError extends Error { readonly route: GatewayRoute; readonly status: number; constructor(route: GatewayRoute, path: string, status: number, detail: string) }`
  - the answer types, each a union on `kind` (the table above gives the status of each case):
    `export type PoolsAnswer = { kind: 'pools'; pools: PoolListing[] } | { kind: 'unavailable' }`;
    `export type OfferAnswer = { kind: 'offer'; offer: Offer } | { kind: 'unknown_pool' } | { kind: 'pool_closed'; status: Extract<PoolStatus, 'open' | 'filled' | 'settled'> } | { kind: 'pool_expired'; status: Extract<PoolStatus, 'expired' | 'refunded'> } | { kind: 'unavailable' }`;
    `export type PaymentAnswer = { kind: 'pending'; txHash: string; poolId: number; buyer: string; seats: number; taken: number; target: number; deadlineMs: number } | { kind: 'filled'; txHash: string; credential: string; poolId: number; seats: number; terms: string } | { kind: 'refused'; error: PaymentErrorCode; offer: Offer | null } | { kind: 'no_seats_taken' } | { kind: 'pool_expired'; txHash: string } | { kind: 'relay_failed'; txHash: string } | { kind: 'result_unknown'; txHash: string } | { kind: 'unknown_pool' } | { kind: 'unavailable' }`;
    `export type RedeemAnswer = { kind: 'pending'; seats: number; taken: number; target: number; deadlineMs: number } | { kind: 'filled'; credential: string; poolId: number; seats: number; terms: string } | { kind: 'refund'; status: RefundStatus; amount: bigint; bonusShare: bigint; txHash: string | null } | { kind: 'no_seats' } | { kind: 'invalid_proof'; error: RedeemErrorCode } | { kind: 'unknown_pool' } | { kind: 'unavailable' }`;

```typescript
  minGas: 50_000_000_000_000n,
  maxGas: 100_000_000_000_000n,
  maxTimeoutSeconds: 120,
};

/** The gateway's offer for `seats` seats of POOL. */
export function offerFor(seats: number): Offer {
  return buildOffer(POOL, seats, CONTEXT);
}

/** A transaction hash: base58 of 32 random bytes. */
export function txHash(): string {
  return baseEncode(randomBytes(32));
}

/** A compact JWS, as the gateway's credentials are. */
export const CREDENTIAL = 'eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJidXllci0wMS5wYXJlbnQudGVzdG5ldCJ9.c2lnbmF0dXJl';

/** The `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header of a relayed payment. */
export function paymentResponseHeader(transaction: string, payer = BUYER): Record<string, string> {
  const response: PaymentResponse = { success: true, transaction, network: 'near:testnet', payer };
  return { 'X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE': encodeHeader(response) };
}

/** A response with `body` as JSON. */
export function jsonResponse(status: number, body: unknown, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Response {
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...headers } });
}

/** A fetch that records each request, then answers it with `handler`. */
export function stubFetch(handler: (request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>): {
  fetch: typeof fetch;
  requests: Request[];
} {
  const requests: Request[] = [];
  const fetch = async (input: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response> => {
    const request = new Request(input, init);
    requests.push(request);
    return handler(request);
  };
  return { fetch, requests };
}
```

```typescript
const HASH = txHash();
/** A row of `GET /pools` as the gateway writes it, its amounts as decimal strings. */

  id: POOL_ID,
  terms: POOL.terms,
  seat_price: '180',
  target: 192,
  taken: 148,
  deadline_ms: POOL.deadline_ms,
  bonus: '1728',
  min_bonus_per_seat: '9',
};
/** LISTING as the client returns it, its amounts as bigints. */

/** A record of the activity feed as the gateway writes it. */
const RECORD = {
  at: 1_800_000_000_000,
  poolId: POOL_ID,
  kind: 'commit',
  account: BUYER,
  seats: 2,
  amount: '360',
  txHash: HASH,
  ok: true,
};
/** RECORD as the client returns it. */
const RECORDED: ActivityRecord = { ...RECORD, kind: 'commit', amount: 360n };

/** A client whose fetch answers every request with `answer()`, and the requests it sent. */
function client(answer: () => Response = () => jsonResponse(503, { error: 'chain_unavailable' })) {
  const { fetch, requests } = stubFetch(answer);
  return { gateway: new GatewayClient({ gatewayUrl: GATEWAY_URL, fetch }), requests };
}

/** One answer of the gateway: its status, its body and its headers. */
interface Answer {
  status: number;
  body: unknown;
  headers?: Record<string, string>;
}

/** Sends the request of `route` to a gateway that answers with `answer`. */
async function ask(route: GatewayRoute, answer: Answer): Promise<unknown> {
  const { gateway } = client(() => jsonResponse(answer.status, answer.body, answer.headers));
  switch (route) {
    case 'pools':
      return gateway.pools();
    case 'offer':
      return gateway.offer(POOL_ID, 2);
    case 'payment':
      return gateway.pay(POOL_ID, 2, PAYMENT);
    case 'redemption':
      return gateway.redeem(POOL_ID, PROOF);
    case 'activity':
      return gateway.activity(POOL_ID);
  }
}

/** The error `promise` rejects with; fails the test if it resolves. */
async function rejection(promise: Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
  try {
    await promise;
  } catch (error) {
    return error;
  }
  throw new Error('the promise resolved');
}

describe('GatewayClient requests', () => {
  it('pools() asks GET /pools', async () => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client(() => jsonResponse(200, []));
    await gateway.pools();
    expect(requests.map((r) => [r.method, r.url])).toEqual([['GET', `${GATEWAY_URL}/pools`]]);
  });

  it('offer() asks for the seats with neither a payment nor a proof', async () => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client();
    await gateway.offer(POOL_ID, 2);
    const [request] = requests;
    expect(request?.url).toBe(`${GATEWAY_URL}/pools/7/access?seats=2`);
    expect(request?.headers.has('X-PAYMENT')).toBe(false);
    expect(request?.headers.has('X-QUORUM-PROOF')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('pay() sends the payment header once, at the URL of the seats requested', async () => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client();
    await gateway.pay(POOL_ID, 2, PAYMENT);

    expect(requests[0]?.url).toBe(`${GATEWAY_URL}/pools/7/access?seats=2`);
    expect(requests[0]?.headers.get('X-PAYMENT')).toBe(PAYMENT);
  });

  it('redeem() sends the proof header, with no seats', async () => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client();
    await gateway.redeem(POOL_ID, PROOF);
    expect(requests[0]?.url).toBe(`${GATEWAY_URL}/pools/7/access`);
    expect(requests[0]?.headers.get('X-QUORUM-PROOF')).toBe(PROOF);
    expect(requests[0]?.headers.has('X-PAYMENT')).toBe(false);
  });

  it("activity() asks for one pool's records", async () => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client(() => jsonResponse(200, []));
    await gateway.activity(POOL_ID);
    expect(requests[0]?.url).toBe(`${GATEWAY_URL}/activity?pool=7`);
  });

  it('refuses to follow a redirect, which would carry a payment or a proof to another server', async () => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client();
    await gateway.pay(POOL_ID, 2, PAYMENT);
    await gateway.redeem(POOL_ID, PROOF);
    expect(requests.map((r) => r.redirect)).toEqual(['error', 'error']);
  });

  it.each([-1, 1.5, Number.NaN, 2 ** 53])('refuses the pool id %s before sending anything', async (poolId) => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client();
    await expect(gateway.offer(poolId, 1)).rejects.toThrow(RangeError);
    await expect(gateway.pay(poolId, 1, PAYMENT)).rejects.toThrow(RangeError);
    await expect(gateway.redeem(poolId, PROOF)).rejects.toThrow(RangeError);
    await expect(gateway.activity(poolId)).rejects.toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(requests).toEqual([]);
  });

  it.each([0, 1001, 2.5])('refuses %s seats, outside the 1 to 1000 a request may ask for', async (seats) => {
    const { gateway, requests } = client();
    await expect(gateway.offer(POOL_ID, seats)).rejects.toThrow(RangeError);
    await expect(gateway.pay(POOL_ID, seats, PAYMENT)).rejects.toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(requests).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('passes on the error of a request that never got an answer, without sending it again', async () => {
    const failure = new TypeError('fetch failed');
    const { gateway, requests } = client(() => {
      throw failure;
    });
    expect(await rejection(gateway.pay(POOL_ID, 2, PAYMENT))).toBe(failure);
    expect(requests).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```

```typescript
import {
  PAYMENT_HEADER,
  PAYMENT_RESPONSE_HEADER,
  PROOF_HEADER,
  decodeHeader,
  isAccountId,
  parseAmount,
  type Network,
  type Offer,
  type PaymentErrorCode,
  type PoolStatus,
  type ProofErrorCode,
} from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';

/** The most seats one request may ask for: the gateway's limit, the contract's largest target. */
export const MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST = 1000;

/** A row of `GET /pools`: an open pool of the gateway's provider with seats left, amounts in base units. */
export interface PoolListing {
  id: number;
  terms: string;
  seat_price: bigint;
  target: number;
  taken: number;
  deadline_ms: number;
  bonus: bigint;
  min_bonus_per_seat: bigint;
}

/** What an activity record is of: a relayed commit, a settlement, a pushed refund, or the dust sent back. */
export type ActivityKind = 'commit' | 'settle' | 'refund' | 'dust';

/**
 * One record of the gateway's activity feed. `at` is milliseconds since the epoch. `account` is the
 * buyer for a commit and for a buyer's refund, and the seller otherwise (a settlement, the dust, a
 * keeper call that moved nothing). `amount` is in the token's base units. `ok` is false for a commit
 * that took no seats, a refund that failed, and a keeper call that moved nothing.
 */
export interface ActivityRecord {
  at: number;
  poolId: number;
  kind: ActivityKind;
  account: string;
  seats: number;
  amount: bigint;
  txHash: string;
  ok: boolean;
}

/** The codes a redemption proof is refused with (`401`). */
export type RedeemErrorCode = ProofErrorCode | 'not_full_access' | 'replayed_proof';

/** The status of a refund, by the buyer's state on the contract. */
export type RefundStatus = 'refunded' | 'refund_pending' | 'claimable';

/** The answer to `GET /pools`. */
export type PoolsAnswer = { kind: 'pools'; pools: PoolListing[] } | { kind: 'unavailable' };

/** The answer to an offer request: `GET /pools/:id/access?seats=N` with no header. */
export type OfferAnswer =
  /** 402: the offer, for the seats requested or fewer. */
  | { kind: 'offer'; offer: Offer }
  /** 404: the gateway does not serve the pool. */
  | { kind: 'unknown_pool' }
  /** 409 `pool_closed`: filled, settled, or open with no seat left to offer. */
  | { kind: 'pool_closed'; status: Extract<PoolStatus, 'open' | 'filled' | 'settled'> }
  /** 410 `pool_expired`: past its deadline. */
  | { kind: 'pool_expired'; status: Extract<PoolStatus, 'expired' | 'refunded'> }
  /** 503: the gateway cannot read the chain. */
  | { kind: 'unavailable' };

/** The answer to a payment: `GET /pools/:id/access?seats=N` with `X-PAYMENT`. */
export type PaymentAnswer =
  /**
   * 202: the payment took `seats` seats and the pool is still open with `taken` of `target`.
   * `txHash` is the relayed transaction, from `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`.
   */
  | {
      kind: 'pending';
      txHash: string;
      poolId: number;
      buyer: string;
      seats: number;
      taken: number;
      target: number;
      deadlineMs: number;
    }
  /**
   * 200: the payment filled the pool. `seats` is every seat the buyer holds in the pool, not only
   * this payment's. `txHash` is the relayed transaction, from `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`.
   */
  | { kind: 'filled'; txHash: string; credential: string; poolId: number; seats: number; terms: string }
  /** 402: a check failed and nothing was relayed; `offer` is the offer as it stands, if there is one. */
  | { kind: 'refused'; error: PaymentErrorCode; offer: Offer | null }
  /** 409: the pool filled before the payment landed; the token returned the money. */
  | { kind: 'no_seats_taken' }
  /** 410 `pool_expired`: the pool expired before the payment landed; the token returned the money. */
  | { kind: 'pool_expired'; txHash: string }
  /** 502: the relay was refused, the delegate failed, or something other than a full pool refused the commit. */
  | { kind: 'relay_failed'; txHash: string }
  /** 502: the result is unknown, and the payment may still land: redemption tells. */
  | { kind: 'result_unknown'; txHash: string }
  /** 404: the gateway does not serve the pool. */
  | { kind: 'unknown_pool' }
  /** 503: the gateway could not read the chain, or had no relayer key free, and relayed nothing. */
  | { kind: 'unavailable' };

/** The answer to a redemption: `GET /pools/:id/access` with `X-QUORUM-PROOF`. */
export type RedeemAnswer =
  /** 202: the buyer holds `seats` seats and the pool is still open. */
  | { kind: 'pending'; seats: number; taken: number; target: number; deadlineMs: number }
  /** 200: the pool filled; the credential is for every seat the buyer holds. */
  | { kind: 'filled'; credential: string; poolId: number; seats: number; terms: string }
  /**
   * 410: the pool expired. `amount` is what the buyer's seats are refunded, `bonusShare` the part of it
   * that is bonus, and `txHash` the refund's transaction when the gateway's keeper sent it.
   */
  | { kind: 'refund'; status: RefundStatus; amount: bigint; bonusShare: bigint; txHash: string | null }
  /** 404: the account holds no seats in the pool. */
  | { kind: 'no_seats' }
  /** 401: the proof was refused. */
  | { kind: 'invalid_proof'; error: RedeemErrorCode }
  /** 404: the gateway does not serve the pool. */
  | { kind: 'unknown_pool' }
  /** 503: the gateway cannot read the chain. */
  | { kind: 'unavailable' };

/** The requests GatewayClient sends. */
export type GatewayRoute = 'pools' | 'offer' | 'payment' | 'redemption' | 'activity';

/**
 * An answer that is not one the gateway documents for the request: an unexpected status, a body that
 * is not JSON, or a field that is missing or malformed. The message names the request, the status and
 * the field, never a value from the body, which may hold a credential.
 */
export class GatewayResponseError extends Error {
  override name = 'GatewayResponseError';
  readonly route: GatewayRoute;
  readonly status: number;

  constructor(route: GatewayRoute, path: string, status: number, detail: string) {
    super(`the gateway's answer to the ${route} request GET ${path} is not a documented one: HTTP ${status}, ${detail}`);
    this.route = route;
    this.status = status;
  }
}

/**
 * A typed HTTP client of the gateway. Each method sends one GET request, never repeats it, and
 * returns the documented answer as a discriminated union on `kind`. Every body is checked field by
 * field, and only the documented fields are kept, since the gateway is outside the buyer's trust.
 * The strings a buyer passes on are bounded, so that an answer cannot carry megabytes of text to
 * whoever reads it: a pool's terms to the 280 UTF-8 bytes the pools contract keeps, a transaction
 * hash to the 44 base58 characters of a NEAR hash, and a credential to 4096 characters. An offer's
 * `resource` and `description` are kept as sent: nothing passes them on.
 *
 * Amounts: every amount of a type this client defines (PoolListing, ActivityRecord, a refund of
 * RedeemAnswer) is a bigint in the token's base units, converted once here from the gateway's decimal
 * string. The protocol's Offer keeps its amounts as the decimal strings of the wire, since the buyer
 * signs the offer as it was sent.
 * Rejects with RangeError, before sending anything, for a pool id that is not a non-negative safe
 * integer or a seat count outside 1 to MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST; with GatewayResponseError for an answer
 * that is not documented; and with fetch's own error when no answer arrives. The client follows no
 * redirect, which would carry a payment or a proof to another server.
 */
export class GatewayClient {
  readonly #url: string;
  readonly #fetch: typeof fetch;

  /** `gatewayUrl` is the gateway's base URL without a trailing slash, as BuyerSettings has it. */
  constructor(opts: { gatewayUrl: string; fetch?: typeof fetch }) {
    this.#url = opts.gatewayUrl;
    this.#fetch = opts.fetch ?? fetch;
  }

  /** `GET /pools`: the open pools of the gateway's provider, in id order. */
  async pools(): Promise<PoolsAnswer> {
    return this.#get('pools', '/pools', {}, poolsAnswer);
  }

  /** The offer for `seats` seats of a pool. */
  async offer(poolId: number, seats: number): Promise<OfferAnswer> {
    return this.#get('offer', accessPath(poolId, seats), {}, offerAnswer);
  }

  /**
   * Sends a payment, at the URL of the seats requested (the payment may be for fewer, as a reduced
   * offer is). A rejected promise or a GatewayResponseError leaves it unknown whether the payment
   * landed: redemption tells.
   */
  async pay(poolId: number, seats: number, paymentHeader: string): Promise<PaymentAnswer> {
    return this.#get('payment', accessPath(poolId, seats), { [PAYMENT_HEADER]: paymentHeader }, paymentAnswer);
  }

  /** Sends a redemption proof for a pool. */
  async redeem(poolId: number, proofHeader: string): Promise<RedeemAnswer> {
    checkPoolId(poolId);
    return this.#get('redemption', `/pools/${poolId}/access`, { [PROOF_HEADER]: proofHeader }, redeemAnswer);
  }

  /** `GET /activity?pool=<id>`: the pool's records in the activity feed, oldest first. */
  async activity(poolId: number): Promise<ActivityRecord[]> {
    checkPoolId(poolId);
    return this.#get('activity', `/activity?pool=${poolId}`, {}, activityAnswer);
  }

  async #get<T>(route: GatewayRoute, path: string, headers: Record<string, string>, read: Reader<T>): Promise<T> {
    const response = await this.#fetch(`${this.#url}${path}`, { headers, redirect: 'error' });
    const text = await response.text();
    try {
      return read(response.status, parseJson(text), response.headers);
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof Malformed) throw new GatewayResponseError(route, path, response.status, error.message);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

/** Reads one route's answer; throws Malformed for anything that is not documented. */
type Reader<T> = (status: number, body: unknown, headers: Headers) => T;

/** An undocumented answer, described without quoting the body. */
class Malformed extends Error {}

type Fields = Record<string, unknown>;

function parseJson(text: string): unknown {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    throw new Malformed('the body is not JSON');
  }
}

function poolsAnswer(status: number, body: unknown): PoolsAnswer {
  if (status === 503) return unavailable(body);
  if (status !== 200) throw unexpectedStatus(status);
  return { kind: 'pools', pools: list(body, 'body').map((row, i) => poolListing(row, `body[${i}]`)) };
}

function offerAnswer(status: number, body: unknown): OfferAnswer {
  switch (status) {
    case 402: {
      const { error, accepts } = paymentRequiredBody(body);
      if (error !== 'payment required') throw new Malformed('body.error is not "payment required"');
      const [offer] = accepts;
      if (offer === undefined || accepts.length !== 1) throw new Malformed('body.accepts does not hold exactly one offer');
      return { kind: 'offer', offer };
    }
    case 404:
      expectError(body, 'unknown_pool');
      return { kind: 'unknown_pool' };
    case 409:
      expectError(body, 'pool_closed');
      return { kind: 'pool_closed', status: oneOf(fields(body, 'body'), 'status', 'body', ['open', 'filled', 'settled']) };
    case 410:
      expectError(body, 'pool_expired');
      return { kind: 'pool_expired', status: oneOf(fields(body, 'body'), 'status', 'body', ['expired', 'refunded']) };
    case 503:
      return unavailable(body);
  }
  throw unexpectedStatus(status);
}

function paymentAnswer(status: number, body: unknown, headers: Headers): PaymentAnswer {
  switch (status) {
    case 202: {
      const b = fields(body, 'body');
      literal(b, 'status', 'body', 'pending');
      const receipt = fields(b.receipt, 'body.receipt');
      const pool = fields(b.pool, 'body.pool');
      const txHash = paymentTransaction(headers);
      if (hash(receipt, 'txHash', 'body.receipt') !== txHash) {
        throw new Malformed(`body.receipt.txHash is not the transaction of ${PAYMENT_RESPONSE_HEADER}`);
      }
      return {
        kind: 'pending',
        txHash,
        poolId: integer(receipt, 'poolId', 'body.receipt'),
        buyer: account(receipt, 'buyer', 'body.receipt'),
        seats: integer(receipt, 'seats', 'body.receipt'),
        taken: integer(pool, 'taken', 'body.pool'),
        target: integer(pool, 'target', 'body.pool'),
        deadlineMs: integer(pool, 'deadlineMs', 'body.pool'),
      };
    }
    case 200:
      return { kind: 'filled', txHash: paymentTransaction(headers), ...filledBody(body) };
    case 402: {
      const { error, accepts } = paymentRequiredBody(body);
      if (!isCode(PAYMENT_ERRORS, error)) throw new Malformed('body.error is not a documented payment error');
      if (accepts.length > 1) throw new Malformed('body.accepts holds more than one offer');
      return { kind: 'refused', error, offer: accepts[0] ?? null };
    }
    case 409: {
      const { error, accepts } = paymentRequiredBody(body);
      if (error !== 'no_seats_taken') throw new Malformed('body.error is not "no_seats_taken"');
      if (accepts.length > 0) throw new Malformed('body.accepts is not empty');
      return { kind: 'no_seats_taken' };
    }
    case 410:
      expectError(body, 'pool_expired');
      return { kind: 'pool_expired', txHash: hash(fields(body, 'body'), 'txHash', 'body') };
    case 502: {
      const b = fields(body, 'body');
      const kind = oneOf(b, 'error', 'body', ['relay_failed', 'result_unknown']);
      return { kind, txHash: hash(b, 'txHash', 'body') };
    }
    case 404:
      expectError(body, 'unknown_pool');
      return { kind: 'unknown_pool' };
    case 503:
      return unavailable(body);
  }
  throw unexpectedStatus(status);
}

function redeemAnswer(status: number, body: unknown): RedeemAnswer {
  switch (status) {
    case 202: {
      const b = fields(body, 'body');
      literal(b, 'status', 'body', 'pending');
      return {
        kind: 'pending',
        seats: integer(b, 'seats', 'body'),
        taken: integer(b, 'taken', 'body'),
        target: integer(b, 'target', 'body'),
        deadlineMs: integer(b, 'deadlineMs', 'body'),
      };
    }
    case 200:
      return { kind: 'filled', ...filledBody(body) };
    case 410: {
      const b = fields(body, 'body');
      return {
        kind: 'refund',
        status: oneOf(b, 'status', 'body', ['refunded', 'refund_pending', 'claimable']),
        amount: baseUnits(b, 'amount', 'body'),
        bonusShare: baseUnits(b, 'bonusShare', 'body'),
        txHash: b.txHash === null ? null : hash(b, 'txHash', 'body'),
      };
    }
    case 401: {
      const error = text(fields(body, 'body'), 'error', 'body');
      if (!isCode(REDEEM_ERRORS, error)) throw new Malformed('body.error is not a documented proof error');
      return { kind: 'invalid_proof', error };
    }
    case 404: {
      const error = oneOf(fields(body, 'body'), 'error', 'body', ['unknown_pool', 'no_seats']);
      return { kind: error };
    }
    case 503:
      return unavailable(body);
  }
  throw unexpectedStatus(status);
}

function activityAnswer(status: number, body: unknown): ActivityRecord[] {
  if (status !== 200) throw unexpectedStatus(status);
  return list(body, 'body').map((value, i) => {
    const where = `body[${i}]`;
    const r = fields(value, where);
    if (typeof r.ok !== 'boolean') throw new Malformed(`${where}.ok is not a boolean`);
    return {
      at: integer(r, 'at', where),
      poolId: integer(r, 'poolId', where),
      kind: oneOf(r, 'kind', where, ['commit', 'settle', 'refund', 'dust']),
      account: account(r, 'account', where),
      seats: integer(r, 'seats', where),
      amount: baseUnits(r, 'amount', where),
      txHash: hash(r, 'txHash', where),
      ok: r.ok,
    };
  });
}

/** A `{x402Version: 1, error, accepts}` body. Its offers keep only their documented fields. */
function paymentRequiredBody(body: unknown): { error: string; accepts: Offer[] } {
  const b = fields(body, 'body');
  if (b.x402Version !== 1) throw new Malformed('body.x402Version is not 1');
  const accepts = list(b.accepts, 'body.accepts').map((offer, i) => readOffer(offer, `body.accepts[${i}]`));
  return { error: text(b, 'error', 'body'), accepts };
}

function readOffer(value: unknown, where: string): Offer {
  const o = fields(value, where);
  literal(o, 'scheme', where, 'quorum');
  literal(o, 'mimeType', where, 'application/json');
  const maxTimeoutSeconds = integer(o, 'maxTimeoutSeconds', where);
  if (maxTimeoutSeconds < 1) throw new Malformed(`${where}.maxTimeoutSeconds is not positive`);
  const at = `${where}.extra`;
  const extra = fields(o.extra, at);
  return {
    scheme: 'quorum',
    network: network(o, 'network', where),
    maxAmountRequired: amount(o, 'maxAmountRequired', where),
    resource: text(o, 'resource', where),
    description: text(o, 'description', where),
    mimeType: 'application/json',
    payTo: account(o, 'payTo', where),
    maxTimeoutSeconds,
    asset: account(o, 'asset', where),
    extra: {
      poolId: integer(extra, 'poolId', at),
      seats: integer(extra, 'seats', at),
      seatPrice: amount(extra, 'seatPrice', at),
      target: integer(extra, 'target', at),
      taken: integer(extra, 'taken', at),
      deadlineMs: integer(extra, 'deadlineMs', at),
      bonus: amount(extra, 'bonus', at),
      minBonusPerSeat: amount(extra, 'minBonusPerSeat', at),
      terms: terms(extra, 'terms', at),
      relayer: account(extra, 'relayer', at),
      minGas: amount(extra, 'minGas', at),
      maxGas: amount(extra, 'maxGas', at),
    },
  };
}

function poolListing(value: unknown, where: string): PoolListing {
  const p = fields(value, where);
  return {
    id: integer(p, 'id', where),
    terms: terms(p, 'terms', where),
    seat_price: baseUnits(p, 'seat_price', where),
    target: integer(p, 'target', where),
    taken: integer(p, 'taken', where),
    deadline_ms: integer(p, 'deadline_ms', where),
    bonus: baseUnits(p, 'bonus', where),
    min_bonus_per_seat: baseUnits(p, 'min_bonus_per_seat', where),
  };
}

/** A `{status: "filled", credential, poolId, seats, terms}` body. */
function filledBody(body: unknown): { credential: string; poolId: number; seats: number; terms: string } {
  const b = fields(body, 'body');
  literal(b, 'status', 'body', 'filled');
  const credential = text(b, 'credential', 'body');
  if (credential.length > MAX_CREDENTIAL_LENGTH) throw new Malformed(`body.credential is longer than ${MAX_CREDENTIAL_LENGTH} characters`);
  if (!COMPACT_JWS.test(credential)) throw new Malformed('body.credential is not a compact JWS');
  return { credential, poolId: integer(b, 'poolId', 'body'), seats: integer(b, 'seats', 'body'), terms: terms(b, 'terms', 'body') };
}

/** The transaction named by a well-formed `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header. */
function paymentTransaction(headers: Headers): string {
  const where = `the ${PAYMENT_RESPONSE_HEADER} header`;
  const header = headers.get(PAYMENT_RESPONSE_HEADER);
  if (header === null) throw new Malformed(`${where} is missing`);
  let value: unknown;
  try {
    value = decodeHeader(header);
  } catch {
    throw new Malformed(`${where} is not base64 of JSON`);
  }
  const response = fields(value, where);
  if (response.success !== true) throw new Malformed(`${where} does not say success`);
  network(response, 'network', where);
  account(response, 'payer', where);
  return hash(response, 'transaction', where);
}

function unavailable(body: unknown): { kind: 'unavailable' } {
  expectError(body, 'chain_unavailable');
  return { kind: 'unavailable' };
}

function expectError(body: unknown, error: string): void {
  literal(fields(body, 'body'), 'error', 'body', error);
}

function unexpectedStatus(status: number): Malformed {
  return new Malformed(`status ${status} is not one this request is answered with`);
}

/** Every code a payment is refused with (`402`); a Record so that the compiler checks it is complete. */
const PAYMENT_ERRORS: Record<PaymentErrorCode, true> = {
  invalid_payload: true,
  invalid_signature: true,
  wrong_receiver: true,
  wrong_method: true,
  wrong_deposit: true,
  gas_too_low: true,
  gas_too_high: true,
  wrong_args: true,
  wrong_amount: true,
  wrong_pool: true,
  not_full_access: true,
  stale_nonce: true,
  nonce_too_large: true,
  expired: true,
  pool_closed: true,
  insufficient_balance: true,
  seller_commit: true,
  over_buyer_cap: true,
  payment_in_flight: true,
};

/** Every code a redemption proof is refused with (`401`). */
const REDEEM_ERRORS: Record<RedeemErrorCode, true> = {
  invalid_proof: true,
  wrong_message: true,
  wrong_recipient: true,
  stale_proof: true,
  invalid_signature: true,
  not_full_access: true,
  replayed_proof: true,
};

function isCode<T extends string>(codes: Record<T, true>, value: string): value is T {
  return Object.hasOwn(codes, value);
}

const COMPACT_JWS = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/;
/**
 * A NEAR transaction hash: 32 bytes in base58, at most 44 characters, fewer when it starts with
 * zero bytes (each written `1`). The alphabet also keeps control characters out of logs.
 */
const TX_HASH = /^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/;
/** The most UTF-8 bytes of terms the pools contract keeps for a pool. */
const MAX_TERMS_BYTES = 280;
/** The longest credential accepted, in characters: the gateway's are a few hundred. */
const MAX_CREDENTIAL_LENGTH = 4096;

function accessPath(poolId: number, seats: number): string {
  checkAccessRequest(poolId, seats);
  return `/pools/${poolId}/access?seats=${seats}`;
}

/**
 * Throws RangeError unless `poolId` is a non-negative safe integer and `seats` is from 1 to
 * MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST: the offer and payment requests GatewayClient refuses to send.
 */
export function checkAccessRequest(poolId: number, seats: number): void {
  checkPoolId(poolId);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(seats) || seats < 1 || seats > MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST) {
    throw new RangeError(`a request asks for 1 to ${MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST} seats, not ${seats}`);
  }
}

function checkPoolId(poolId: number): void {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(poolId) || poolId < 0) throw new RangeError(`invalid pool id: ${poolId}`);
}

function fields(value: unknown, where: string): Fields {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) throw new Malformed(`${where} is not an object`);
  return value as Fields;
}

function list(value: unknown, where: string): unknown[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) throw new Malformed(`${where} is not an array`);
  return value;
}

function literal(o: Fields, key: string, where: string, value: string): void {
  if (o[key] !== value) throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
}

function oneOf<T extends string>(o: Fields, key: string, where: string, values: readonly T[]): T {
  const value = values.find((v) => v === o[key]);
  if (value === undefined) throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not one of ${values.join(', ')}`);
  return value;
}

function text(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): string {
  const value = o[key];
  if (typeof value !== 'string') throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not a string`);
  return value;
}

/** A pool's terms: a string of at most MAX_TERMS_BYTES in UTF-8, as the pools contract keeps them. */
function terms(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): string {
  const value = text(o, key, where);
  if (Buffer.byteLength(value, 'utf8') > MAX_TERMS_BYTES) {
    throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is longer than the ${MAX_TERMS_BYTES} bytes the pools contract keeps`);
  }
  return value;
}

/** A non-negative safe integer. */
function integer(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): number {
  const value = o[key];
  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(value) || value < 0) {
    throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not a non-negative integer`);
  }
  return value;
}

/** An amount as a decimal string, kept as the string: the protocol's Offer holds amounts so. */
function amount(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): string {
  const value = o[key];
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || parseAmount(value) === null) throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not a decimal amount`);
  return value;
}

/** An amount written as a decimal string, read into base units: the form of the client's own types. */
function baseUnits(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): bigint {
  const value = parseAmount(o[key]);
  if (value === null) throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not a decimal amount`);
  return value;
}

function account(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): string {
  const value = o[key];
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !isAccountId(value)) throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not a NEAR account id`);
  return value;
}

function hash(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): string {
  const value = o[key];
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !TX_HASH.test(value)) throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not a base58 transaction hash`);
  return value;
}

function network(o: Fields, key: string, where: string): Network {
  const value = o[key];
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !value.startsWith('near:')) throw new Malformed(`${where}.${key} is not a NEAR network`);
  return value as Network;
}
```

### Task 5: The buyer package: chain reads, Buyer and error descriptions

`Buyer` is the one payment path the scripted buyers and the MCP server share (section 6.3). Its
`pay(offer, request)`:

1. checks the offer with the protocol package's `checkOffer` against the buyer's own network, token
   and pools contract, never the offer's, and against the request (pool, seats, spending limit); a
   refused offer is answered `declined` with the refusal, and nothing is read, signed or sent;
2. reads the key's next nonce (the key's nonce plus 1, at optimistic finality, as the gateway reads
   it) and the final block's height;
3. signs a delegate action whose `max_block_height` is that height plus the blocks of the shorter of
   the offer's `maxTimeoutSeconds` and the buyer's own `maxTimeoutSeconds`, at `blockTimeMs` a block
   (`maxBlockHeightFor`), so that no offer makes it sign a payment that stays valid longer than its
   own bound;
4. sends it once, at the URL of the seats requested, and returns the gateway's answer with what it
   signed (`signed`: the nonce, the final height and the `max_block_height`).

A payment that fails before it leaves the buyer is a `PaymentNotSentError`, safe to follow with a new
payment: `key_not_found` (the account has no such access key), `chain_read` (the nonce or the height
cannot be read), `signing`, or `gateway_unreachable`, when fetch's `TypeError` comes from a
connection that was never made (`ECONNREFUSED`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, or an `AggregateError` of
those only). Any other failure once the payment is signed is a `PaymentUnknownError` carrying
`signed`: the payment may have been relayed, and the swarm and the MCP server count it as able to
take seats until a final block above `max_block_height` plus `SETTLE_MARGIN_BLOCKS` (20 blocks,
section 6.3). `redeem(poolId)` signs a fresh NEP-413 proof naming the gateway URL's host as its
recipient (section 6.5).

`chain.ts` holds what a buyer reads over RPC. `RpcBuyerChain` reads the key's next nonce at
optimistic finality, turning near-api-js's missing-account and missing-key errors into
`AccessKeyNotFoundError`, and the final height. `RpcPoolReads.getPool` calls `get_pool` on the
configured pools contract at optimistic finality and checks every field of the view, keeping only
those fields; a malformed view is a `PoolViewError` that names the field and never quotes the terms,
which are the seller's text.

`errors.ts` names failures for agents and buyers' log lines without library or RPC text, which can
hold the RPC URL and its key (near-api-js even makes the body of an RPC's `429` answer the message).
`transportReason` gives a short reason that never quotes a message: `HTTP <status>`, an errno or
undici code, `retries exceeded`, or `error`. `describeError` gives the whole message chain, causes
included, for the operator's standard error only, through `redact`, which writes the RPC URL as
`QUORUM_RPC_URL`.

```typescript
import {
```
