- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

`apps/swarm/src/setup.ts`:

```typescript
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import {
  folderKeyPath,
  KeyFileError,
  keyFilePath,
  keyFolderPath,
  readKeyFile,
  readKeyFolder,
  readSpendFile,
  SpendFileError,
  writeKeyFile,
  writeSpendFile,
} from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { KeyPair, yoctoToNear } from 'near-api-js';
import { swarmAccounts, type SwarmAccount } from './accounts.ts';
import {
  BATCHED_CALL_GAS,
  checkChain,
  freeBalance,
  MAX_CALLS_PER_TRANSACTION,
  rerunAdvice,
  type AccountKey,
  type AccountState,
  type SwarmChain,
  type TokenTransfer,
} from './chain.ts';
import type { SwarmConfig } from './config.ts';
import { count } from './words.ts';

/** What runSetup works with besides the configuration. */
export interface SetupDeps {
  chain: SwarmChain;
  /** Receives one line for each action as it is taken, or `nothing to do` after a run that took none. */
  log: (line: string) => void;
}

/** What a setup did. */
export interface SetupReport {
  /** One line for each transaction sent and each file written, in order; empty when all was in place. */
  actions: string[];
}

/** Why setup stopped. */
export type SetupProblem =
  /** An account setup does not create is missing: the parent, or an account outside it. */
  | 'missing_account'
  /** An account that exists, the parent included, has no key file, so it cannot sign. */
  | 'missing_key'
  /** The pools contract must be deployed, but QUORUM_POOLS_WASM is not set. */
  | 'missing_wasm'
  /** The pools contract was initialised with another token than QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT. */
  | 'wrong_token'
  /** The parent cannot pay for what setup would send from it. */
  | 'near_shortfall'
  /** The funding account cannot cover the token top-ups. */
  | 'token_shortfall';

/** Setup stopped before it was done. The message says why; it names accounts and files, never a key. */
export class SetupError extends Error {
  override name = 'SetupError';
  readonly problem: SetupProblem;

  constructor(problem: SetupProblem, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.problem = problem;
  }
}

/** An account setup pays from does not hold what setup must send: `shortfall` is what it lacks. */
export class ShortfallError extends SetupError {
  override name = 'ShortfallError';
  readonly account: string;
  /** In yoctoNEAR for `near_shortfall`, in the token's base units for `token_shortfall`. */
  readonly shortfall: bigint;

  constructor(problem: 'near_shortfall' | 'token_shortfall', account: string, shortfall: bigint, message: string) {
    super(problem, message);
    this.account = account;
    this.shortfall = shortfall;
  }
}

/**
 * Setup tops an account up once it holds less than this share of its NEAR target, in percent. Every
 * transaction an account signs burns some of its NEAR, and the funding account signs setup's own
 * token transfers, so topping up any shortfall at all would make each run send something.
 */
const TOP_UP_BELOW_PERCENT = 90n;

/**
 * 0.1 NEAR: the base of what the parent keeps for gas beyond what setup sends from it. It covers the
 * gas its transactions burn (a NEAR transfer burns 0.000045 NEAR at the floor gas price of 0.0001
 * NEAR per Tgas), and the gas a creation or a NEAR transfer buys upfront while it runs (about 0.01
 * NEAR at GAS_PURCHASE_PRICE).
 */
const BASE_GAS_MARGIN = 100_000_000_000_000_000_000_000n;

/**
 * 0.008 NEAR, kept for each account setup creates: NEAR charges a fixed 0.007 NEAR for each account
 * creation, which it keeps back from the transaction's gas refund, about 0.00707 NEAR in all with the
 * fees of sending the creation.
 */
const CREATION_COST = 8_000_000_000_000_000_000_000n;

/**
 * The yoctoNEAR per unit of gas at which a transaction's gas is bought when it is sent: NEAR's
 * `min_gas_purchase_price`, 0.001 NEAR per Tgas, the buy price while the gas price is below it (its
 * floor is 0.0001 NEAR per Tgas). The signer must hold the gas a function call attaches at this price
 * while the transaction runs; the gas it does not burn, and the difference with the price it burns
 * at, are refunded once it is done.
 */
const GAS_PURCHASE_PRICE = 1_000_000_000n;

/** An account as setup found it before acting. */
interface Found {
  account: SwarmAccount;
  /** null when the account does not exist. */
  state: AccountState | null;
  /** The keys its key file holds (its key folder's, for the relayer); empty when there is none, or none is needed. */
  keys: KeyPair[];
  /** Whether it is registered on the token; false for an account that is not to be. */
  registered: boolean;
}

/** A NEAR transfer from the parent, and what its line adds to the amount, if anything. */
interface NearTopUp {
  receiverId: string;
  amount: bigint;
  note?: string;
}

/** What step 0 found and checked: everything steps 1 to 5 will do, worked out before any is done. */
interface Plan {
  parent: AccountKey;
  found: Found[];
  /** The pools contract's code when step 3 must deploy it, else null. */
  code: Uint8Array | null;
  topUps: NearTopUp[];
  registrations: string[];
  /** The deposit that registers one account on the token, in yoctoNEAR. */
  deposit: bigint;
  /** Step 5's token transfers, which the funding account makes only if it can cover them all. */
  tokenTopUps: TokenTransfer[];
}

/** What one run works with. */
interface Run {
  config: SwarmConfig;
  chain: SwarmChain;
  report: (line: string) => void;
}

/**
 * Prepares every account of the system (spec section 7.2). It is idempotent: a run that finds
 * everything in place sends nothing and logs `nothing to do`.
 *
 * 0. Reads and checks everything before it sends anything: the RPC's chain (ConfigError, as the
 *    command line gives, when it is not the one QUORUM_NETWORK names), the parent's key file
 *    and account, each account's state, key file and token balance, the pools contract's token, and
 *    that the parent holds, free of its storage (freeBalance), what steps 1, 2 and 4 send from it plus
 *    a margin for gas: 0.1 NEAR, plus
 *    0.008 NEAR for each account it creates, plus the gas that the largest batch of calls it signs
 *    (registrations, and token top-ups when it is the funding account) buys upfront, 0.02 NEAR a
 *    call. Throws SetupError if not.
 * 1. Creates each missing sub-account of the parent with its NEAR target as balance. A key that an
 *    earlier run left in the account's key file is reused; a new key is written to its key file
 *    before the transaction is sent. The relayer gets QUORUM_RELAYER_KEY_COUNT keys.
 * 2. Tops each existing account up to its NEAR target from the parent, once it holds less than 90%
 *    of it. A funding account that is the parent is never topped up. The pools contract, once it
 *    holds code, is topped up instead to QUORUM_POOLS_FREE_NEAR of NEAR free of its storage, once
 *    less than 90% of that is free.
 * 3. Deploys the pools contract, initialised with the configured token, if it holds no code. It
 *    comes after the top-ups, so that a pools account holding less than its code locks has been
 *    topped up first.
 * 4. Registers the funding account, the pools contract, the provider and each buyer on the token,
 *    paid by the parent, at most 10 per transaction.
 * 5. Tops the provider and each buyer up to its token amount from the funding account, at most 10 per
 *    transaction, or throws ShortfallError and makes none of them if the funding account cannot
 *    cover them all. Then clears the MCP server's spend total.
 *
 * Each action is logged as it is taken, and returned. A write that fails throws its error; one that
 * got no result (OutcomeUnknownError) also says that setup can be run again once it is final.
 */
export async function runSetup(config: SwarmConfig, deps: SetupDeps): Promise<SetupReport> {
  try {
    return await setUp(config, deps);
  } catch (error) {
    throw rerunAdvice(error, 'Setup', 'it sends only what is still missing');
  }
}

async function setUp(config: SwarmConfig, deps: SetupDeps): Promise<SetupReport> {
  const { chain } = deps;
  const actions: string[] = [];
  const run: Run = {
    config,
    chain,
    report(line) {
      actions.push(line);
      deps.log(line);
    },
  };

  const { parent, found, code, topUps, registrations, deposit, tokenTopUps } = await prepare(config, chain);
  /** The key each account signs with, by account id. */
  const signers = new Map<string, KeyPair>();
  for (const { account, keys } of found) {
    if (keys[0] !== undefined) signers.set(account.id, keys[0]);
  }

  // 1. Creations.
  for (const entry of found) {
    if (entry.state === null) signers.set(entry.account.id, await create(run, parent, entry));
  }
  // 2. NEAR top-ups.
  for (const { receiverId, amount, note } of topUps) {
    const outcome = await chain.transferNear(parent, receiverId, amount);
    run.report(`topped up  ${receiverId}  +${near(amount)}${note === undefined ? '' : `  ${note}`}  tx ${outcome.txHash}`);
  }
  // 3. The pools contract.
  if (code !== null) await deploy(run, signerOf(signers, config.poolsContract), code);
  // 4. Registrations.
  for (const batch of batches(registrations)) {
    const outcome = await chain.storageDeposits(parent, batch, deposit);
    run.report(`registered on the token  ${batch.join(', ')}  tx ${outcome.txHash}`);
  }
  // 5. Token top-ups, then the spend total.
  await topUpTokens(run, tokenTopUps, signerOf(signers, config.funding));
  await clearSpendTotal(run);

  if (actions.length === 0) deps.log('nothing to do');
  return { actions };
}

/** Step 0: reads and checks everything, and works out steps 1 to 5. Sends and writes nothing. */
async function prepare(config: SwarmConfig, chain: SwarmChain): Promise<Plan> {
  await checkChain(config.network, chain);

  const [parentKey] = await storedKeys(config, config.parent, false);
  if (parentKey === undefined) {
    const path = keyLocation(config, config.parent, false);
    throw new SetupError('missing_key', `there is no key for the parent account ${config.parent} at ${path}`);
  }
  const parentState = await chain.account(config.parent);
  if (parentState === null) throw new SetupError('missing_account', `the parent account ${config.parent} does not exist`);

  const found = await survey(config, chain);
  const code = await poolsCode(config, chain, found);
  const topUps = nearTopUps(config, found);
  const registrations = found
    .filter(({ account, registered }) => account.onToken && !registered)
    .map(({ account }) => account.id);
  const deposit = registrations.length > 0 ? await chain.registrationDeposit() : 0n;
  const tokenTopUps = await tokenShortfalls(chain, found);

  const created = found.filter(({ state }) => state === null);
  const sends =
    created.reduce((sum, { account }) => sum + (account.near ?? 0n), 0n) +
    topUps.reduce((sum, topUp) => sum + topUp.amount, 0n) +
    deposit * BigInt(registrations.length);
  // The parent signs the registrations, and the token top-ups when it is the funding account.
  const calls = Math.max(
    Math.min(registrations.length, MAX_CALLS_PER_TRANSACTION),
    config.funding === config.parent ? Math.min(tokenTopUps.length, MAX_CALLS_PER_TRANSACTION) : 0,
  );
  const margin = gasMargin(created.length, calls);
  // What the parent's storage locks it cannot send.
  const free = freeBalance(parentState);
  // Without anything to send or call, the parent signs nothing and needs no gas.
  if ((sends > 0n || calls > 0) && free < sends + margin.total) {
    const shortfall = sends + margin.total - free;
    throw new ShortfallError(
      'near_shortfall',
      config.parent,
      shortfall,
      `the parent account ${config.parent} holds ${near(free)} free of its storage, but setup sends ${near(sends)} from it ` +
        `and keeps ${near(margin.total)} for gas (${margin.parts.join(', plus ')}): send it ${near(shortfall)} more, ` +
        'then run setup again',
    );
  }
  const parent = { accountId: config.parent, keyPair: parentKey };
  return { parent, found, code, topUps, registrations, deposit, tokenTopUps };
}

/**
 * What the parent keeps for gas beyond what it sends: BASE_GAS_MARGIN, CREATION_COST for each of
 * `creations` accounts, and the gas a batch of `calls` function calls buys upfront at
 * GAS_PURCHASE_PRICE (batches are sent one after another, so only the largest counts). `parts` says
 * what the total is made of.
 */
function gasMargin(creations: number, calls: number): { total: bigint; parts: string[] } {
  const upfront = GAS_PURCHASE_PRICE * BATCHED_CALL_GAS * BigInt(calls);
  const parts = [near(BASE_GAS_MARGIN)];
  if (creations > 0) {
    parts.push(`${near(CREATION_COST)} for ${creations === 1 ? 'the account' : `each of the ${creations} accounts`} it creates`);
  }
  if (calls > 0) parts.push(`${near(upfront)} its largest batch of ${count(calls, 'call')} buys upfront, refunded after`);
  return { total: BASE_GAS_MARGIN + CREATION_COST * BigInt(creations) + upfront, parts };
}

/**
 * Reads each account's state, key file and registration, in swarmAccounts order. Throws SetupError
 * for a missing account setup cannot create, and for an existing account without a key file. Every
 * account signs, for setup or another command, except the pools contract once it holds code.
 */
async function survey(config: SwarmConfig, chain: SwarmChain): Promise<Found[]> {
  const found: Found[] = [];
  for (const account of swarmAccounts(config)) {
    const state = await chain.account(account.id);
    if (state === null && !account.create) {
      throw new SetupError(
        'missing_account',
        `${account.id} does not exist, and setup creates only direct sub-accounts of the parent account ${config.parent}`,
      );
    }
    const signs = state === null || account.role !== 'pools' || !state.hasCode;
    const keys = signs ? await storedKeys(config, account.id, account.role === 'relayer') : [];
    if (state !== null && signs && keys.length === 0) {
      const path = keyLocation(config, account.id, account.role === 'relayer');
      throw new SetupError('missing_key', `${account.id} exists, but there is no key for it at ${path}, so it cannot sign`);
    }
    const registered = account.onToken && (await chain.isRegistered(account.id));
    found.push({ account, state, keys, registered });
  }
  return found;
}

/**
 * The code step 3 deploys, read from QUORUM_POOLS_WASM, when the pools contract holds none; null when
 * it holds code, after checking that its token is the configured one.
 */
async function poolsCode(config: SwarmConfig, chain: SwarmChain, found: readonly Found[]): Promise<Uint8Array | null> {
  const pools = found.find((entry) => entry.account.role === 'pools');
  if (pools?.state?.hasCode === true) {
    const token = await chain.getToken();
    if (token !== config.token) {
      throw new SetupError(
        'wrong_token',
        `the pools contract ${config.poolsContract} was initialised with the token ${token}, not QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT ` +
          `${config.token}; a contract's token is set once, so another token needs another pools account`,
      );
    }
    return null;
  }
  if (config.poolsWasm === null) {
    throw new SetupError(
      'missing_wasm',
      `the pools contract ${config.poolsContract} holds no code: set QUORUM_POOLS_WASM to the path of its wasm file`,
    );
  }
  return readFile(config.poolsWasm);
}

/**
 * Step 2's transfers: an existing account with a NEAR target is topped up back to it once it holds
 * less than TOP_UP_BELOW_PERCENT of it. An account created in step 1 starts at its target. The pools
 * contract, once it holds code, goes by its free NEAR instead (freeBalance): the records it keeps for
 * each pool and each buyer lock more of its balance as they grow and are never freed, while the
 * balance itself stays where it was. It is topped up back to QUORUM_POOLS_FREE_NEAR free once less
 * than TOP_UP_BELOW_PERCENT of that is free, and its line says what was free.
 */
function nearTopUps(config: Pick<SwarmConfig, 'poolsFreeNear'>, found: readonly Found[]): NearTopUp[] {
  return found.flatMap(({ account, state }): NearTopUp[] => {
    if (state === null) return [];
    if (account.role === 'pools' && state.hasCode) {
      const free = freeBalance(state);
      const target = config.poolsFreeNear;
      if (free * 100n >= target * TOP_UP_BELOW_PERCENT) return [];
      return [{ receiverId: account.id, amount: target - free, note: `${near(free)} was free of its storage, now ${near(target)}` }];
    }
    const target = account.near;
    if (target === null || state.balance * 100n >= target * TOP_UP_BELOW_PERCENT) return [];
    return [{ receiverId: account.id, amount: target - state.balance }];
  });
}

/**
 * Where an account's keys are kept: in its key folder, one file per key, for an account with several
 * keys (the relayer), else in its key file.
 */
function keyLocation(config: SwarmConfig, accountId: string, several: boolean): string {
  const { credentialsDir, network } = config;
  return several ? keyFolderPath(credentialsDir, network, accountId) : keyFilePath(credentialsDir, network, accountId);
}

/** The keys kept for an account (see keyLocation); none when there is no key file or key folder. */
async function storedKeys(config: SwarmConfig, accountId: string, several: boolean): Promise<KeyPair[]> {
  const location = keyLocation(config, accountId, several);
  try {
    return several ? await readKeyFolder(location) : [await readKeyFile(location)];
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof KeyFileError && error.problem === 'missing') return [];
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * Step 1 for one account: creates it with its NEAR target as balance, and returns the key it signs
 * with. It is given the keys its key files kept from an earlier run, completed with new ones up to
 * its key count. Each new key is written to its key file before the transaction is sent, so that a
 * run stopped before the account exists leaves the key behind for the next run. The relayer's keys
 * go to its key folder, and the first of them to its key file too, unless that file exists.
 */
async function create(run: Run, parent: AccountKey, entry: Found): Promise<KeyPair> {
  const { config } = run;
  const { id, keyCount } = entry.account;
  const several = entry.account.role === 'relayer';
  const keys = [...entry.keys];
  const file = keyFilePath(config.credentialsDir, config.network, id);
  while (keys.length < keyCount) {
    const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
    await writeKey(run, several ? folderKeyPath(keyLocation(config, id, several), keyPair.getPublicKey()) : file, id, keyPair);
    keys.push(keyPair);
  }
  const [first] = keys;
  if (first === undefined) throw new RangeError(`${id} has a key count of ${keyCount}`);
  if (several) {
    try {
      await writeKey(run, file, id, first);
    } catch (error) {
      if (!(error instanceof KeyFileError && error.problem === 'exists')) throw error;
    }
  }
  const balance = entry.account.near ?? 0n;
  const publicKeys = keys.map((key) => key.getPublicKey());
  const outcome = await run.chain.createAccount(parent, { accountId: id, balance, publicKeys });
  run.report(`created  ${id}  ${near(balance)}  tx ${outcome.txHash}`);
  return first;
}

async function writeKey(run: Run, path: string, accountId: string, keyPair: KeyPair): Promise<void> {
  await writeKeyFile(path, accountId, keyPair);
  run.report(`wrote key file  ${path}`);
}

/** Step 3: deploys the pools contract with the configured token, signed by the pools account. */
async function deploy(run: Run, pools: AccountKey, code: Uint8Array): Promise<void> {
  const outcome = await run.chain.deployPools(pools, code);
  run.report(`deployed the pools contract  ${pools.accountId}  token ${run.config.token}  tx ${outcome.txHash}`);
}

/**
 * Step 5's top-ups, read in step 0: each account with a token amount that holds less is to receive
 * the difference. An account not created or not registered on the token yet holds none of it and
 * lacks its whole amount; its balance is not read, so that setup does not depend on what the token
 * answers for an account it does not know.
 */
async function tokenShortfalls(chain: SwarmChain, found: readonly Found[]): Promise<TokenTransfer[]> {
  const transfers: TokenTransfer[] = [];
  for (const { account, state, registered } of found) {
    if (account.tokens === null) continue;
    const balance = state === null || !registered ? 0n : await chain.ftBalanceOf(account.id);
    if (balance < account.tokens) transfers.push({ receiverId: account.id, amount: account.tokens - balance });
  }
  return transfers;
}

/**
 * Step 5: sends the top-ups from the funding account. Throws ShortfallError, and makes none of them,
 * unless the funding account covers them all.
 */
async function topUpTokens(run: Run, transfers: readonly TokenTransfer[], funding: AccountKey): Promise<void> {
  const { chain, config } = run;
  const needed = transfers.reduce((sum, transfer) => sum + transfer.amount, 0n);
  if (needed === 0n) return;
  const held = await chain.ftBalanceOf(config.funding);
  if (held < needed) {
    throw new ShortfallError(
      'token_shortfall',
      config.funding,
      needed - held,
      `the funding account ${config.funding} holds ${held} base units of the token ${config.token}, but the top-ups ` +
        `need ${needed}: send it ${needed - held} more, then run setup again`,
    );
  }
  for (const batch of batches(transfers)) {
    const outcome = await chain.ftTransfers(funding, batch);
    const sent = batch.map((transfer) => `${transfer.receiverId} +${transfer.amount}`).join(', ');
    run.report(`sent tokens  ${sent}  tx ${outcome.txHash}`);
  }
}

/**
 * Writes a zero total for the MCP server's buyer to its spend file, unless the file reads 0 already
 * (a missing file does). Replaces another account's total, left by an earlier QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT,
 * but passes on readSpendFile's error for a file that is not a spend file, which it never overwrites.
 */
async function clearSpendTotal(run: Run): Promise<void> {
  const { spendFile, mcpAccount } = run.config;
  try {
    if ((await readSpendFile(spendFile, mcpAccount)) === 0n) return;
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof SpendFileError && error.problem === 'other_account')) throw error;
  }
  await writeSpendFile(spendFile, mcpAccount, 0n);
  run.report(`cleared the spend total of ${mcpAccount}  ${spendFile}`);
}

function signerOf(signers: ReadonlyMap<string, KeyPair>, accountId: string): AccountKey {
  const keyPair = signers.get(accountId);
  if (keyPair === undefined) throw new RangeError(`setup holds no key for ${accountId}`);
  return { accountId, keyPair };
}

/** `items` in consecutive batches of at most MAX_CALLS_PER_TRANSACTION. */
function batches<T>(items: readonly T[]): T[][] {
  const result: T[][] = [];
  for (let start = 0; start < items.length; start += MAX_CALLS_PER_TRANSACTION) {
    result.push(items.slice(start, start + MAX_CALLS_PER_TRANSACTION));
  }
  return result;
}

function near(yocto: bigint): string {
  return `${yoctoToNear(yocto)} NEAR`;
}
```

`apps/swarm/src/env-files.ts`:

```typescript
import { generateKeyPairSync } from 'node:crypto';
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util';
import { keyFolderPath, readKeyFolder } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import type { KeyPair } from 'near-api-js';
import type { SwarmConfig } from './config.ts';

/**
 * The `.env` files of the gateway and the MCP server, written from the swarm's configuration, so that
 * the three apps share one value of each shared variable. The text is checked with Node's own env
 * file parser, which `process.loadEnvFile` and `--env-file` use, so each value reads back as written.
 */

/** An app whose `.env` file the swarm writes. */
export type EnvApp = 'gateway' | 'mcp';

/** A private Ed25519 JWK with only the members the gateway reads. */
export interface CredentialJwk {
  kty: 'OKP';
  crv: 'Ed25519';
  /** The public key, base64url. */
  x: string;
  /** The private key, base64url. */
  d: string;
}

/** An env file that already exists: the swarm never writes over one. */
export class EnvFileExistsError extends Error {
  override name = 'EnvFileExistsError';
  readonly path: string;

  constructor(path: string) {
    super(`there is an env file at ${path} already, and it is left as it is: remove it to write a new one`);
    this.path = path;
  }
}

/** One variable of an env file and its value. */
type EnvEntry = readonly [name: string, value: string];

/** `apps/<app>/.env`, resolved from this module's own location: it does not depend on the current folder. */
export function envFilePath(app: EnvApp): string {
  return fileURLToPath(new URL(`../../${app}/.env`, import.meta.url));
}

/** A new credential key for the gateway: an Ed25519 key pair from node:crypto, as a private JWK. */
export function newCredentialJwk(): CredentialJwk {
  const { x, d } = generateKeyPairSync('ed25519').privateKey.export({ format: 'jwk' });
  if (typeof x !== 'string' || typeof d !== 'string') {
    throw new TypeError('node:crypto exported an Ed25519 key without x and d');
  }
  return { kty: 'OKP', crv: 'Ed25519', x, d };
}

/**
 * The gateway's `.env`: the variables it shares with the swarm, its relayer and provider accounts,
 * the relayer's keys (QUORUM_RELAYER_KEYS) and the credential key (QUORUM_CREDENTIAL_JWK). Its other
 * variables keep the gateway's defaults. Throws RangeError without a relayer key, or for a value that
 * would not read back as it is; the message names the variable, never the value.
 */
export function gatewayEnvText(config: SwarmConfig, relayerKeys: readonly KeyPair[], credentialJwk: CredentialJwk): string {
  if (relayerKeys.length === 0) throw new RangeError(`the gateway needs at least one key of the relayer ${config.relayer}`);
  return envText(
    [
      "Written by `swarm env gateway` from the swarm's configuration.",
      "Secret: it holds the relayer's keys and the credential key. Keep it private, and never commit it.",
    ],
    [
      ...sharedEntries(config),
      ['QUORUM_RELAYER_ACCOUNT', config.relayer],
      ['QUORUM_PROVIDER_ACCOUNT', config.provider],
      ['QUORUM_RELAYER_KEYS', relayerKeys.map((key) => key.toString()).join(',')],
      ['QUORUM_CREDENTIAL_JWK', JSON.stringify(credentialJwk)],
      ['QUORUM_COMMIT_MIN_GAS', config.commitMinGas.toString()],
      ['QUORUM_COMMIT_MAX_GAS', config.commitMaxGas.toString()],
      ['QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS', config.blockTimeMs.toString()],
    ],
  );
}

/**
 * The MCP server's `.env`: the variables it shares with the swarm (the longest expiry its buyer signs
 * among them), its buyer, the folder of the key files, the spend file, and a spend cap equal to the
 * budget setup tops its buyer up to. It holds no key: the server reads its buyer's key file. Throws
 * RangeError for a value that would not read back as it is.
 */
export function mcpEnvText(config: SwarmConfig): string {
  return envText(
    ["Written by `swarm env mcp` from the swarm's configuration."],
    [
      ...sharedEntries(config),
      ['QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS', config.blockTimeMs.toString()],
      ['QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS', config.maxTimeoutSeconds.toString()],
      ['QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT', config.mcpAccount],
      ['QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR', config.credentialsDir],
      ['QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP', config.buyerBudget.toString()],
      ['QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE', config.spendFile],
    ],
  );
}

/**
 * Writes `text` to a new file readable by its owner only (mode 0o600, on POSIX systems; see aclNotice
 * for Windows). Never writes over a file: throws EnvFileExistsError if there is one.
 */
export async function writeEnvFile(path: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await writeFile(path, text, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 });
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EEXIST') throw new EnvFileExistsError(path);
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * What `swarm env gateway` says after writing the gateway's `.env` to `path` on Windows, where Node
 * applies only the read-only bit of a file's mode, so the file is readable by whoever its folder's
 * access control list lets in: the icacls command that removes the inherited entries and gives `user`
 * alone full control. Null on other systems, where writeEnvFile makes it readable by its owner only.
 */
export function aclNotice(path: string, platform: NodeJS.Platform, user: string): string | null {
  if (platform !== 'win32') return null;
  return (
    `${path} is protected only by its folder's access control list, since Windows ignores the file mode: ` +
    `to let ${user} alone use it, run icacls "${path}" /inheritance:r /grant:r "${user}:F"`
  );
}

/**
 * `swarm env gateway`: writes the gateway's `.env` to `path` with every key of the relayer's key
 * folder and a new credential key. Throws KeyFileError when the key folder is missing or holds a file
 * that is not a key, and EnvFileExistsError when `path` exists.
 */
export async function writeGatewayEnv(config: SwarmConfig, path: string): Promise<void> {
  const relayerKeys = await readKeyFolder(keyFolderPath(config.credentialsDir, config.network, config.relayer));
  await writeEnvFile(path, gatewayEnvText(config, relayerKeys, newCredentialJwk()));
}

/** `swarm env mcp`: writes the MCP server's `.env` to `path`. Throws EnvFileExistsError when `path` exists. */
export async function writeMcpEnv(config: SwarmConfig, path: string): Promise<void> {
  await writeEnvFile(path, mcpEnvText(config));
}

/** The variables every app reads alike from the buyer settings, in the gateway's order. */
function sharedEntries(config: SwarmConfig): EnvEntry[] {
  return [
    ['QUORUM_NETWORK', config.network],
    ['QUORUM_RPC_URL', config.rpcUrl],
    ['QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL', config.gatewayUrl],
    ['QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT', config.parent],
    ['QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT', config.token],
    ['QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT', config.poolsContract],
  ];
}

/**
 * An env file: `comments` as `#` lines, then one `NAME=value` line per entry. Throws RangeError for
 * an entry that Node's parser would not read back as it is, such as a value holding `#`.
 */
function envText(comments: readonly string[], entries: readonly EnvEntry[]): string {
  const lines = [...comments.map((comment) => `# ${comment}`), ...entries.map(([name, value]) => `${name}=${value}`)];
  const text = `${lines.join('\n')}\n`;
  const read = parseEnv(text);
  for (const [name, value] of entries) {
    if (read[name] !== value) throw new RangeError(`${name} has a value that an env file cannot hold as it is`);
  }
  return text;
}
```

### Task 9: The provider's pool opening

`openPool(config, { chain, log }, scenario)` opens the scenario's pool as the simulated provider
(section 7.3). It first reads every pool at optimistic finality, every page of `list_pools`, so that
a pool counts as soon as the pools contract's receipt that opened it has run, and refuses with
`PoolAlreadyOpenError` while one of the provider's pools is Open: each scripted buyer's budget
covers one pool. It then sends nothing and reads no key. Filled, Settled, Expired and Refunded pools
do not block it, nor does another seller's open pool. The refusal names every open pool, and says
that `swarm run <pool-id> <fills|fails>` resumes its buyers. Otherwise it reads the provider's key
file and the final block, and sends the bonus to the pools contract with `ft_transfer_call` and an
`open` message,
`{"open":{"seat_price":"<base units>","target":<seats>,"deadline_ms":<ms>,"max_seats_per_buyer":<seats>,"terms":"<text>"}}`
(the seat price as a decimal string, the others as numbers), whose deadline is the final block's
time plus the scenario's deadline, since the contract measures deadlines in block time, never by a
local clock. It returns the pool id that the `pool_opened` event of the pools contract's receipts
gives, the transaction and the deadline, and logs them in one line.

The bonus transfer is sent once and never signed again, since a second send could open a second
pool. When another transaction of the provider's key took its nonce (`NonceTakenError`), or the
transfer got no result (`OutcomeUnknownError`), the error names the transaction, says that a pool
may have opened, and advises waiting until that transaction is final before running `swarm open`
again, whose check then sees the pool. `OpenPoolError` names the transaction when the pools contract
logged no `pool_opened`, logged one without a valid pool id, or the token did not keep the whole
bonus; a failure of the transfer itself passes on the chain's `TransactionFailedError`.
`assertNoPoolOpen(config, chain)` makes the open-pool check alone, so that `swarm demo` (Task 12)
refuses before setup sends anything; it reads no pool while the pools account does not exist or
holds no contract.

```typescript
import { mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';

import { keyFilePath, KeyFileError, writeKeyFile } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';

import { scenario } from '../src/scenarios.ts';

const DEFAULTS = { deadlineSeconds: null, spreadSeconds: null };
const FILLS = scenario('fills', DEFAULTS);
const FAILS = scenario('fails', DEFAULTS);
const TX_HASH = '8bB1Ttk9c3kXe2RsE3oqgJ1ZBTVxfXJWQWfWcnPrw8bh';

let credentialsDir: string;

beforeEach(async () => {
  credentialsDir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'quorum-provider-'));
});

afterEach(async () => {
  await rm(credentialsDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

interface Setup {
  chain: FakeChain;
  keyPair: KeyPair;
  config: SwarmConfig;
  deps: OpenPoolDeps;
  /** The lines openPool logged. */
  lines: string[];
}

/**
 * A fake chain with the pools contract deployed and registered, and the provider holding 1 NEAR and
 * 10,000 base units, with its key in a key file under the test's credentials folder.
 */
async function setup(): Promise<Setup> {
  const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
  await writeKeyFile(keyFilePath(credentialsDir, 'near:testnet', PROVIDER), PROVIDER, keyPair);
  const chain = new FakeChain();
  chain.addAccount(PROVIDER, { balance: NEAR, publicKeys: [keyPair.getPublicKey()] });
  chain.addAccount(POOLS, { balance: 3n * NEAR, hasCode: true });
  chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_000n);
  chain.register(POOLS);
  const lines: string[] = [];
  return { chain, keyPair, config: testConfig({ credentialsDir }), deps: { chain, log: (line) => lines.push(line) }, lines };
}

/** A `pool_opened` event for pool `poolId` of FILLS, as the pools contract logs it. */
function opened(poolId: unknown): QuorumEvent {
  const data = { pool_id: poolId, seller: PROVIDER, seat_price: '180', target: 192, deadline_ms: NOW_MS + 600_000, bonus: '1728', terms: TERMS };
  return { event: 'pool_opened', data } as QuorumEvent;
}

/**
 * An `onTransferCall` script: transaction TX_HASH, in which the token kept `used`, and whose pools
 * contract receipt logs `logs` (or the token's receipt, when `loggedBy` is the token).
 */
function transferResult(used: bigint, logs: string[], loggedBy = POOLS) {
  return (call: FakeTransferCall) => ({
    outcome: {
      txHash: TX_HASH,
      receipts: [
        { executorId: call.signer, logs: [], failed: false, gasBurnt: 0n },
        { executorId: TOKEN, logs: loggedBy === TOKEN ? logs : [], failed: false, gasBurnt: 0n },
        { executorId: POOLS, logs: loggedBy === POOLS ? logs : [], failed: false, gasBurnt: 0n },
        { executorId: TOKEN, logs: [], failed: false, gasBurnt: 0n },
      ],
    },
    used,
  });
}

        "is final, then run `swarm open` again; it lists the provider's open pools.",

    await expect(failure).rejects.toThrow(PoolAlreadyOpenError);
    await expect(failure).rejects.toThrow(`the provider ${PROVIDER} has pool 4 open`);
    await expect(failure).rejects.toMatchObject({ poolIds: [4] });
    expect(chain.writes).toEqual([]);
    expect(lines).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('names every open pool of the provider', async () => {
    const { chain, config, deps } = await setup();
    for (const id of [2, 5]) chain.setPool(poolView({ id }));
    await expect(openPool(config, deps, FAILS)).rejects.toMatchObject({
      poolIds: [2, 5],
      message: expect.stringContaining(`the provider ${PROVIDER} has pools 2, 5 open`),
    });
  });

  it('names the command that resumes the open pool’s buyers', () => {
    expect(new PoolAlreadyOpenError(PROVIDER, [4]).message).toMatch(/nothing was sent; `swarm run 4 <fills\|fails>` resumes its buyers$/);
    expect(new PoolAlreadyOpenError(PROVIDER, [2, 5]).message).toMatch(/`swarm run <pool-id> <fills\|fails>` resumes a pool's buyers$/);
  });

  it('reads the pools at optimistic finality, so that a pool opened moments ago counts', async () => {
    const { chain, config, deps } = await setup();
    await openPool(config, deps, FILLS);
    const listed = chain.reads.filter((read) => read.method === 'listPools');
    expect(listed.map((read) => read.atHeight)).toEqual(['optimistic']);
  });

  it('finds an open pool past the first page of pools', async () => {
    const { chain, config, deps } = await setup();
    for (let id = 0; id < 150; id += 1) chain.setPool(poolView({ id, status: id === 120 ? 'open' : 'refunded' }));
    await expect(openPool(config, deps, FILLS)).rejects.toMatchObject({ poolIds: [120] });
    expect(chain.writes).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('refuses before reading the provider’s key file', async () => {
    const { chain, deps } = await setup();
    chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 4 }));
    const config = testConfig({ credentialsDir: join(credentialsDir, 'empty') });
    await expect(openPool(config, deps, FILLS)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(PoolAlreadyOpenError);
  });

  it.each(['filled', 'settled', 'expired', 'refunded'] as const)('opens a pool when the provider’s other pool is %s', async (status) => {
    const { chain, config, deps } = await setup();
    chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 0, status }));
    expect(await openPool(config, deps, FILLS)).toMatchObject({ poolId: 1 });
  });

  it('opens a pool while another seller’s pool is open', async () => {
    const { chain, config, deps } = await setup();
    chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 0, seller: 'provider.other.testnet' }));
    expect(await openPool(config, deps, FILLS)).toMatchObject({ poolId: 1 });
  });
});

describe('assertNoPoolOpen', () => {
  it('throws PoolAlreadyOpenError, naming the pool, when the provider has a pool open', async () => {
    const { chain, config } = await setup();
    chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 0, status: 'settled' }));
    chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 1 }));
    await expect(assertNoPoolOpen(config, chain)).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: 'PoolAlreadyOpenError', poolIds: [1] });
    expect(chain.writes).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('passes when none of the provider’s pools is open', async () => {
    const { chain, config } = await setup();
    chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 0, status: 'refunded' }));
    chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 1, seller: 'provider.other.testnet' }));
    await expect(assertNoPoolOpen(config, chain)).resolves.toBeUndefined();
  });

  it.each([
    ['does not exist', (chain: FakeChain) => chain.accounts.delete(POOLS)],
    ['holds no contract', (chain: FakeChain) => chain.addAccount(POOLS)],
  ])('passes without reading the pools when the pools account %s yet', async (_, prepare) => {
    const { chain, config } = await setup();
    prepare(chain);
    await expect(assertNoPoolOpen(config, chain)).resolves.toBeUndefined();
    expect(chain.reads).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

`apps/swarm/src/provider.ts`:

```typescript
import { keyFilePath, readKeyFile } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { poolsEvents } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { allPools, NonceTakenError, OutcomeUnknownError, type SwarmChain, type TransferCallResult } from './chain.ts';
import type { SwarmConfig } from './config.ts';
import type { Scenario } from './scenarios.ts';

/** A pool the provider opened. `deadlineMs` is in block time, milliseconds since the epoch. */
export interface OpenedPool {
  poolId: number;
  txHash: string;
  deadlineMs: number;
}

/** What openPool uses: the chain, and a logger for the line it writes once the pool is open. */
export interface OpenPoolDeps {
  chain: Pick<SwarmChain, 'finalBlock' | 'ftTransferCall' | 'listPools'>;
  log: (line: string) => void;
}

/**
 * The provider has a pool that is still Open, so openPool sent nothing: each scripted buyer's budget
 * covers one pool, so a second open pool would leave buyers unable to pay for their seats. A send
 * that timed out before its result was known may have opened that pool. `poolIds` lists the open
 * pools, in id order. The pools are read at optimistic finality, so a pool counts as soon as the
 * pools contract's receipt that opened it has run; a bonus transfer already in a block whose receipt
 * at the pools contract has not run yet, a block or two later, is not seen. Hence openPool's advice,
 * after a transfer that got no result, to wait until it is final before trying again.
 */
export class PoolAlreadyOpenError extends Error {
  override name = 'PoolAlreadyOpenError';
  readonly poolIds: number[];

  constructor(provider: string, poolIds: number[]) {
    const one = poolIds.length === 1;
    const pools = one ? `pool ${poolIds[0]}` : `pools ${poolIds.join(', ')}`;
    const resume = one ? `\`swarm run ${poolIds[0]} <fills|fails>\` resumes its buyers` : "`swarm run <pool-id> <fills|fails>` resumes a pool's buyers";
    super(
      `the provider ${provider} has ${pools} open, and each buyer's budget covers one pool: ` +
        `no other pool is opened until ${one ? 'it has' : 'they have'} ended, and nothing was sent; ${resume}`,
    );
    this.poolIds = poolIds;
  }
}

/**
 * The bonus transfer ran, but did not open the pool it was sent for. The token returns to the
 * provider whatever the pools contract did not keep. The message names the transaction.
 */
export class OpenPoolError extends Error {
  override name = 'OpenPoolError';
  readonly txHash: string;

  constructor(message: string, txHash: string) {
    super(message);
    this.txHash = txHash;
  }
}

/**
 * Throws PoolAlreadyOpenError, sending nothing, when one of the provider's pools is Open. A pools
 * account that does not exist or holds no contract yet has no pool, so nothing more is read; otherwise
 * every pool is read (the contract's views derive the status from block time, so a pool past its
 * deadline is not Open). `swarm demo` calls it before setup, so that it refuses before anything is
 * sent; openPool makes the same check just before its own send.
 */
export async function assertNoPoolOpen(
  config: Pick<SwarmConfig, 'provider' | 'poolsContract'>,
  chain: Pick<SwarmChain, 'account' | 'listPools'>,
): Promise<void> {
  const pools = await chain.account(config.poolsContract);
  if (pools === null || !pools.hasCode) return;
  await refuseWhileOpen(config, chain);
}

/**
 * Throws PoolAlreadyOpenError when one of the provider's pools, read with list_pools at optimistic
 * finality, is Open.
 */
async function refuseWhileOpen(config: Pick<SwarmConfig, 'provider'>, chain: Pick<SwarmChain, 'listPools'>): Promise<void> {
  const open = (await allPools(chain, 'optimistic')).filter((pool) => pool.seller === config.provider && pool.status === 'open');
  if (open.length > 0) throw new PoolAlreadyOpenError(config.provider, open.map((pool) => pool.id));
}

/** What `swarm open` advises once its bonus transfer may have opened a pool it could not learn of. */
const OPEN_AGAIN = "Wait until it is final, then run `swarm open` again; it lists the provider's open pools.";

/** The bonus transfer's error, reworded as `swarm open` says it when the transfer may have opened a pool. */
function mayHaveOpened(error: unknown): unknown {
  if (error instanceof NonceTakenError) {
    return new NonceTakenError(
      `the provider's key signed another transaction after its nonce was read (transaction ${error.txHash} was refused): ` +
        `an earlier \`swarm open\` may have opened a pool. ${OPEN_AGAIN}`,
      error.txHash,
      { cause: error },
    );
  }
  if (error instanceof OutcomeUnknownError) {
    const transfer = error.txHash === null ? 'the bonus transfer may have been sent' : `the bonus transfer ${error.txHash} was sent`;
    return new OutcomeUnknownError(
      `${transfer}, but the RPC gave no result (${error.reason}): a pool may have opened. ${OPEN_AGAIN}`,
      error.txHash,
      error.reason,
      { cause: error },
    );
  }
  return error;
}

/**
 * Opens the scenario's pool as the provider, signing with the key in its key file: sends the bonus to
 * the pools contract with `ft_transfer_call` and an `open` message. The deadline is the final block's
 * time plus the scenario's deadline, since the contract checks deadlines against block time, never
 * the local clock. Returns the id the contract gave the pool, read from its `pool_opened` event.
 * Before anything else, reads every pool and throws PoolAlreadyOpenError, sending nothing, when one
 * of the provider's is Open (the contract's views derive the status from block time, so a pool past
 * its deadline is not). Throws OpenPoolError when the pools contract logged no such event or the
 * token did not keep the whole bonus, KeyFileError (before sending anything) when the key file is
 * missing or unreadable, and passes on the chain's error when the transfer itself failed. The bonus
 * transfer is sent once: when another transaction of the provider's key took its nonce
 * (NonceTakenError), or it got no result (OutcomeUnknownError), the error names the transaction and
 * says that a pool may have opened, and to run `swarm open` again once that is final.
 */
export async function openPool(
  config: Pick<SwarmConfig, 'credentialsDir' | 'network' | 'provider' | 'poolsContract'>,
  deps: OpenPoolDeps,
  scenario: Scenario,
): Promise<OpenedPool> {
  await refuseWhileOpen(config, deps.chain);
  const keyPair = await readKeyFile(keyFilePath(config.credentialsDir, config.network, config.provider));
  const block = await deps.chain.finalBlock();
  const deadlineMs = block.timestampMs + scenario.deadlineSeconds * 1000;
  const msg = JSON.stringify({
    open: {
      seat_price: scenario.seatPrice.toString(),
      target: scenario.target,
      deadline_ms: deadlineMs,
      max_seats_per_buyer: scenario.maxSeatsPerBuyer,
      terms: scenario.terms,
    },
  });
  let sent: TransferCallResult;
  try {
    sent = await deps.chain.ftTransferCall({ accountId: config.provider, keyPair }, { receiverId: config.poolsContract, amount: scenario.bonus, msg });
  } catch (error) {
    throw mayHaveOpened(error);
  }
  const { outcome, used } = sent;
  const { txHash } = outcome;
  const kept = `the token kept ${used} of the ${scenario.bonus} bonus`;
  const event = poolsEvents(outcome, config.poolsContract).find((e) => e.event === 'pool_opened');
  if (event === undefined) {
    throw new OpenPoolError(`transaction ${txHash} opened no pool: the pools contract logged no pool_opened event, and ${kept}`, txHash);
  }
  const poolId: unknown = event.data.pool_id;
  if (typeof poolId !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(poolId) || poolId < 0) {
    throw new OpenPoolError(`transaction ${txHash} logged a pool_opened event without a valid pool id`, txHash);
  }
  if (used !== scenario.bonus) {
    throw new OpenPoolError(`transaction ${txHash} opened pool ${poolId}, but ${kept}`, txHash);
  }
  deps.log(
    `opened pool ${poolId} (${scenario.name}): ${scenario.target} seats at ${scenario.seatPrice}, bonus ${scenario.bonus}, ` +
      `deadline ${new Date(deadlineMs).toISOString()}  tx ${txHash}`,
  );
  return { poolId, txHash, deadlineMs };
}
```

### Task 10: The final check

`checkPool(config, deps, { poolId, scenario, baseline?, extraCommits? })` is the final check of a
pool (section 10), which `swarm check` makes alone and `swarm demo` makes last (Task 12). It first
waits:

- It polls the pool (`get_pool`, at final finality) and the gateway's activity feed every 2 seconds,
  until the pool is Settled or Refunded and the feed holds the keeper transaction that ended it: an
  `ok` `settle` record, or the `ok` `dust` record of `pool_refunded` (a failed `settle` record is no
  proof).
- It gives up 5 minutes after the pool's deadline. The time left until the deadline is read in block
  time, from the first successful read of the pool and of the final block, and the wait is measured
  on the local clock (`deps.now`); until that first read, the limit is 5 minutes from the start.
- A read that fails while it waits is logged once for each distinct failure, by what it read and
  its `transportReason`, and made again at the next poll. When the last poll before the limit
  failed, a `reads` check fails after the status, which is then the last one read. A pool never read
  ends the check with the last error; a pool the contract does not hold throws `UnknownPoolError` at
  once.

The contract marks a pool Settled, and Refunded, before its transfers have all run, so the check
then looks up every transaction of the feed with `txOutcome`, the relayer as its signer, which waits
for one not yet final, before it reads any balance. Each read after the wait is tried up to 3 times,
2 seconds apart. It then prints one line per check as it makes it, `ok    <name>: <figures>` or
`FAIL  <name>: <figures>`:

- `status`: the pool ended as the scenario expects (`expectedEnd`). This is the only check made
  against the scenario; the others follow the status the pool did end in.
- `buyers`, once the pool has ended: every row of `get_seats` is `committed` in a Settled pool,
  `refunded` in a Refunded one.
- `refunds and dust`, for a Refunded pool (invariant 4): the bonus shares, `taken × bonus_per_seat`,
  do not exceed the bonus, and the buyers' refunds, each `seats × (seat_price + bonus_per_seat)`,
  plus the dust, `bonus − taken × bonus_per_seat`, are `taken × seat_price + bonus`.
- `solvency` (invariant 1), across every pool: the pools contract's token balance covers what every
  pool still owes (Open or Filled, `taken × seat_price + bonus`; Settled, nothing; Expired or
  Refunded, the refunds of its buyers not yet `refunded` and the dust unless `dust_sent`). The
  balance and every `list_pools` and `get_seats` page are read at the height of one final block, so
  that a commit landing between two reads cannot make it fail falsely; a retried read takes a new
  final block.
- `provider balance`, `pools contract balance` and `buyer balances`, once the pool has ended and when
  a baseline is given (`snapshot`, read before the pool opened): the pool's seller changed by
  `+taken × seat_price` once Settled or `−(bonus − dust)` once Refunded, the pools contract by 0,
  and each buyer of the pool by `−seats × seat_price` or `+seats × bonus_per_seat`. Only accounts in
  the baseline are compared, and a buyer with no seats in the pool is not.
- `commit gas`: every commit of the feed, and every transaction of `extraCommits` that the feed lacks
  and whose outcome shows the pools contract's `seats_committed` for that buyer in this pool, burns
  at most `QUORUM_COMMIT_MIN_GAS` in the token and the pools contract (`commitGas`: the receipts after
  the buyer's delegate receipt that ran on either). A transaction unknown to the RPC, or with no
  receipt on its buyer, fails it. Once the pool has ended, each of the swarm's 21 buyers that holds
  seats with neither an `ok` commit record nor such a learned commit fails it too, and the message
  says that the gateway records no relay whose result was unknown and keeps its feed in its
  `QUORUM_DATA_DIR`; a holder the swarm does not know is named in a note and does not fail it.
- `payout gas`: each `ft_transfer`, a failed one included, and each callback of the feed's `settle`,
  `refund` and `dust` transactions burns under 5 Tgas, half the 10 Tgas the contract gives each
  (`payoutGas`: after the call's own receipt, the token's receipts are the transfers and the pools
  contract's the callbacks). The feed must hold the record that ended the pool. Once the pool is
  Refunded, each of the swarm's buyers refunded with no `ok` refund record fails it, and a refunded
  stranger is named in a note.

When the pool has not ended, `buyers`, `refunds and dust` and the balance lines are left out;
`solvency` and both gas checks still run. Gas is printed in Tgas with 2 decimals, truncated, so that
a figure never shows as the limit it is under (4.996 Tgas shows as 4.99). `checkPool` returns a
`CheckReport` of every line and whether any failed; the command line prints the verdict.
`snapshot(config, chain)` reads the token balance of the provider, the pools contract and every buyer
(`buyerIds`), and is called before the pool opens, since opening it moves the provider's bonus.

`test/check-outcomes.ts` builds, for the tests, the FINAL `tx` responses of relayed commits and of
keeper calls, with the gas of each step of the commit that the gateway captured on the sandbox.
`test/check.test.ts` also reads that capture, `apps/gateway/test/fixtures/relayed-commit.json`, in
which the token and the pools contract burn 5.70 Tgas.

```typescript
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { toTxOutcome, type TxOutcome } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { baseEncode } from 'near-api-js';

/** A hash as NEAR writes one: the base58 of a SHA-256, here of `label`. */
export function hashOf(label: string): string {
  return baseEncode(createHash('sha256').update(label).digest());
}

/**
 * The gas each step of a relayed commit burns in `apps/gateway/test/fixtures/relayed-commit.json`,
 * a commit captured on the sandbox: the relayer's transaction, the buyer's delegate receipt, the
 * token's `ft_transfer_call`, the pools contract's `ft_on_transfer`, the token's
 * `ft_resolve_transfer`, and each gas refund to the relayer.
 */
export const COMMIT_STEP_GAS = {
  transaction: 513_352_392_365n,
  delegate: 513_352_392_365n,
  transferCall: 2_464_838_848_012n,
  onTransfer: 1_959_738_779_630n,
  resolve: 1_275_586_760_213n,
  gasRefund: 223_182_562_500n,
};

/** What the token and the pools contract burn in that commit: 5.70 Tgas. */
export const FIXTURE_COMMIT_GAS = 5_700_164_387_855n;

/** One entry of a transaction's outcome: who executed it, the gas it burnt, whether it failed, and its logs. */
interface Step {
  executor: string;
  gas: bigint;
  failed?: boolean;
  logs?: string[];
}

/** The status the RPC gives a receipt whose contract call panicked. */
const PANICKED = { Failure: { ActionError: { index: 0, kind: { FunctionCallError: { ExecutionError: 'Smart contract panicked' } } } } };

/**
 * The FINAL `tx` response the RPC gives for a transaction whose outcome is `steps` (the
 * transaction first, then its receipts in the RPC's order), read with toTxOutcome as the chain seam
 * reads it.
 */
function outcomeOf(txHash: string, steps: Step[]): TxOutcome {
  const [transaction, ...receipts] = steps.map((step, i) => ({
    id: i === 0 ? txHash : hashOf(`${txHash} receipt ${i}`),
    outcome: {
      executor_id: step.executor,
      gas_burnt: Number(step.gas),
      logs: step.logs ?? [],
      status: step.failed === true ? PANICKED : { SuccessValue: '' },
    },
  }));
  return toTxOutcome({ final_execution_status: 'FINAL', transaction_outcome: transaction, receipts_outcome: receipts });
}

/**
 * A commit the relayer relayed, receipt by receipt as in the captured fixture: the relayer's
 * transaction, the buyer's delegate receipt, the token's `ft_transfer_call`, the pools contract's
 * `ft_on_transfer`, a gas refund, the token's `ft_resolve_transfer`, then three more gas refunds.
 * `gas` overrides the fixture's figures; `poolsLogs` are the logs of the pools contract's receipt.
 */
export function relayedCommit(opts: {
  txHash: string;
  relayer: string;
  buyer: string;
  token: string;
  pools: string;
  gas?: Partial<typeof COMMIT_STEP_GAS>;
  poolsLogs?: string[];
}): TxOutcome {
  const gas = { ...COMMIT_STEP_GAS, ...opts.gas };
  const refund = { executor: opts.relayer, gas: gas.gasRefund };
  return outcomeOf(opts.txHash, [
    { executor: opts.relayer, gas: gas.transaction },
    { executor: opts.buyer, gas: gas.delegate },
    { executor: opts.token, gas: gas.transferCall },
    { executor: opts.pools, gas: gas.onTransfer, logs: opts.poolsLogs ?? [] },
    refund,
    { executor: opts.token, gas: gas.resolve },
    refund,
    refund,
    refund,
  ]);
}

/**
 * A keeper call the relayer signed (`settle`, or a `refund` batch, whose last payout may be the
 * dust): the relayer's transaction, the call at the pools contract, then for each payout the
 * token's `ft_transfer`, the pools contract's callback and a gas refund to the relayer, then the
 * call's own gas refund.
 */
export function keeperCall(opts: {
  txHash: string;
  relayer: string;
  token: string;
  pools: string;
  callGas: bigint;
  payouts: ReadonlyArray<{ transfer: bigint; callback: bigint; failed?: boolean }>;
}): TxOutcome {
  const refund = { executor: opts.relayer, gas: COMMIT_STEP_GAS.gasRefund };
  return outcomeOf(opts.txHash, [
    { executor: opts.relayer, gas: 308_066_207_802n },
    { executor: opts.pools, gas: opts.callGas },
    ...opts.payouts.flatMap((payout) => [
      { executor: opts.token, gas: payout.transfer, failed: payout.failed ?? false },
      { executor: opts.pools, gas: payout.callback },
      refund,
    ]),
    refund,
  ]);
}
```

```typescript
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import type { ActivityRecord } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { toTxOutcome, type PoolView, type SeatView } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import {

  commitGas,
  payoutGas,
  snapshot,
  UnknownPoolError,
  type Baseline,
  type CheckDeps,
  type CheckReport,
} from '../src/check.ts';
import type { SwarmConfig } from '../src/config.ts';
import { scenario } from '../src/scenarios.ts';
import { COMMIT_STEP_GAS, FIXTURE_COMMIT_GAS, hashOf, keeperCall, relayedCommit } from './check-outcomes.ts';
import { eventLog, FakeChain, NOW_MS, PARENT, POOLS, poolView, PROVIDER, testConfig, TOKEN } from './fake-chain.ts';

const RELAYER = `relay.${PARENT}`;
const FILLS = scenario('fills', { deadlineSeconds: null, spreadSeconds: null });
const FAILS = scenario('fails', { deadlineSeconds: null, spreadSeconds: null });
const FIXTURE = new URL('../../gateway/test/fixtures/relayed-commit.json', import.meta.url);

/** The gas a payout's `ft_transfer` and its callback burn in these tests, shown as 1.72 and 1.49 Tgas. */
const TRANSFER_GAS = 1_723_456_789_012n;
const CALLBACK_GAS = 1_498_765_432_109n;
const PAYOUT = { transfer: TRANSFER_GAS, callback: CALLBACK_GAS };
/** What a `settle` or `refund` call burns at the pools contract itself: more than 5 Tgas, and not a payout. */
const CALL_GAS = 9_512_345_678_901n;

function buyer(n: number): string {
  return `buyer-${String(n).padStart(2, '0')}.${PARENT}`;
}

let chain: FakeChain;
let feed: ActivityRecord[];
/** The check's clock, which the fake sleep moves on. */
let clock: number;
let slept: number[];
/** Runs after each sleep, before the check polls again: lets a test change the chain or the feed. */
let afterSleep: (sleeps: number) => void;
let logs: string[];

beforeEach(() => {
  chain = new FakeChain();
  feed = [];
  clock = 50_000;
  slept = [];
  afterSleep = () => {};
  logs = [];
});

/** What the check reads and how it waits: the fake chain, the feed, and a clock that only the sleeps move on. */
function deps(): CheckDeps {
  return {
    chain,
    gateway: { activity: async (poolId) => feed.filter((record) => record.poolId === poolId) },
    now: () => clock,
    sleep: async (ms) => {
      slept.push(ms);
      clock += ms;
      afterSleep(slept.length);
    },
    log: (line) => logs.push(line),
  };
}

function run(
  check: { poolId: number; scenario?: typeof FILLS; baseline?: Baseline },
  config: SwarmConfig = testConfig(),
): Promise<CheckReport> {
  return checkPool(config, deps(), { poolId: check.poolId, scenario: check.scenario ?? FILLS, baseline: check.baseline });
}

function names(report: CheckReport): string[] {
  return report.lines.map((line) => line.name);
}

function lineOf(report: CheckReport, name: string): { ok: boolean; detail: string } {
  const line = report.lines.find((l) => l.name === name);
  if (line === undefined) throw new Error(`the report has no ${name} line`);
  return { ok: line.ok, detail: line.detail };
}

/** A relayed commit in the feed, whose outcome the relayer's transaction has. */
function commit(poolId: number, account: string, seats: number, seatPrice: number, gas?: Partial<typeof COMMIT_STEP_GAS>): string {
  const txHash = hashOf(`commit ${poolId} ${account}`);
  feed.push({ at: NOW_MS, poolId, kind: 'commit', account, seats, amount: BigInt(seats * seatPrice), txHash, ok: true });
  chain.addOutcome(RELAYER, relayedCommit({ txHash, relayer: RELAYER, buyer: account, token: TOKEN, pools: POOLS, gas }));
  return txHash;
}

/** A keeper transaction in the feed: its records, all with one hash, and its outcome with `payouts`. */
function keeperTx(
  poolId: number,
  records: Array<Pick<ActivityRecord, 'kind' | 'account' | 'seats' | 'amount'>>,
  payouts: Array<{ transfer: bigint; callback: bigint; failed?: boolean }>,
): string {
  const txHash = hashOf(`keeper ${poolId} ${feed.length}`);
  for (const record of records) feed.push({ at: NOW_MS, poolId, txHash, ok: true, ...record });
  chain.addOutcome(RELAYER, keeperCall({ txHash, relayer: RELAYER, token: TOKEN, pools: POOLS, callGas: CALL_GAS, payouts }));
  return txHash;
}

/**
 * Pool 0, a `fills` pool of 3 seats at 180 that buyer-01 (2 seats) and buyer-02 (1 seat) filled and
 * the keeper settled. Every account held 10,000 before it opened, the pools contract none.
 */
function settledFills(): Baseline {
  chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 0, target: 3, taken: 3, status: 'settled', buyer_count: 2 }));
  chain.seats.set(0, [
    { buyer: buyer(1), seats: 2, state: 'committed' },
    { buyer: buyer(2), seats: 1, state: 'committed' },
  ]);
  commit(0, buyer(1), 2, 180);
  commit(0, buyer(2), 1, 180);
  keeperTx(0, [{ kind: 'settle', account: PROVIDER, seats: 3, amount: 2268n }], [PAYOUT]);
  // The provider sent the 1,728 bonus and got back 3 × 180 + 1,728.
  chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_540n);
  chain.register(POOLS, 0n);
  chain.register(buyer(1), 9_640n);
  chain.register(buyer(2), 9_820n);
  return new Map([
    [PROVIDER, 10_000n],
    [POOLS, 0n],
    [buyer(1), 10_000n],
    [buyer(2), 10_000n],
  ]);
}

const FAILS_SEATS = [24, 20, 18, 16, 12, 10];

/**
 * Pool 1, a `fails` pool at 320 a seat with a 3,072 bonus, which expired with 100 seats taken by
 * buyer-01 to buyer-06 and was refunded in one keeper transaction: each seat gets back 320 and a
 * bonus share of 30, and the dust of 72 goes back to the provider. Every account held 10,000 before
 * it opened, the pools contract none.
 */
function refundedFails(overrides: Partial<PoolView> = {}): Baseline {
  chain.setPool(
    poolView({
      id: 1,
      seat_price: '320',
      bonus: '3072',
      deadline_ms: NOW_MS - 60_000,
      taken: 100,
      status: 'refunded',
      bonus_per_seat: '30',
      refund_cursor: 6,
      dust_sent: true,
      buyer_count: 6,
      ...overrides,
    }),
  );
  chain.seats.set(
    1,
    FAILS_SEATS.map((seats, i) => ({ buyer: buyer(i + 1), seats, state: 'refunded' as const })),
  );
  FAILS_SEATS.forEach((seats, i) => commit(1, buyer(i + 1), seats, 320));
  keeperTx(
    1,
    [
      ...FAILS_SEATS.map((seats, i) => ({ kind: 'refund' as const, account: buyer(i + 1), seats, amount: BigInt(seats * 350) })),
      { kind: 'dust', account: PROVIDER, seats: 0, amount: 72n },
    ],
    Array.from({ length: 7 }, () => PAYOUT),
  );
  chain.register(PROVIDER, 7_000n);
  chain.register(POOLS, 0n);
  FAILS_SEATS.forEach((seats, i) => chain.register(buyer(i + 1), 10_000n + BigInt(seats * 30)));
  return new Map([[PROVIDER, 10_000n], [POOLS, 0n], ...FAILS_SEATS.map((_, i) => [buyer(i + 1), 10_000n] as const)]);
}

      method: K,

      error: () => Error = () => new Error('Bad Gateway', { cause: 502 }),
    ): void {

      // 150 buyers of one seat: a bonus share of floor(3072 / 150) = 20 each and a dust of 72.
      const seats: SeatView[] = Array.from({ length: 150 }, (_, i) => ({ buyer: `b${i}.testnet`, seats: 1, state: 'refunded' }));
      seats[120]!.state = 'claimable';
      refundedFails({ taken: 150, buyer_count: 150, refund_cursor: 150, bonus_per_seat: '20' });
      chain.seats.set(1, seats);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 1, scenario: FAILS });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'buyers')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: '1 of 150 buyers not refunded: b120.testnet claimable' });
      expect(lineOf(report, 'refunds and dust').ok).toBe(true);
    });
  });

  describe('refunds and dust (invariant 4)', () => {
    it('fails when the buyers’ seats do not add up to the seats the pool took', async () => {
      // 101 seats at a share of 30 leave a dust of 3072 − 3030 = 42.
      refundedFails({ taken: 101 });

      const report = await run({ poolId: 1, scenario: FAILS });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'refunds and dust')).toEqual({
        ok: false,
        detail: 'refunds 35000 + dust 42 = 35042, not 101 × 320 + bonus 3072 = 35392',
      });
    });

    it('fails when the bonus shares come to more than the bonus', async () => {
      refundedFails({ bonus_per_seat: '31' });

      const report = await run({ poolId: 1, scenario: FAILS });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'refunds and dust')).toEqual({
        ok: false,
        detail: 'a bonus share of 31 for each of 100 seats comes to more than the bonus 3072',
      });
    });

    it('accepts a dust of 0, when the bonus shares come to the whole bonus', async () => {
      refundedFails({ bonus: '3000' });

      const report = await run({ poolId: 1, scenario: FAILS });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'refunds and dust')).toEqual({ ok: true, detail: 'refunds 35000 + dust 0 = 100 × 320 + bonus 3000 = 35000' });
    });

    it('is not checked for a settled pool', async () => {
      settledFills();

      expect(names(await run({ poolId: 0 }))).not.toContain('refunds and dust');
    });
  });

  describe('solvency', () => {
    /**
     * Pools 5 to 9 beside the settled pool 0, owing by status: open 10 × 180 + 1728 = 3528; filled
     * 3 × 100 + 50 = 350; settled 0; expired, a committed and a claimable buyer at 100 + 3 each and a
     * dust of 1 not sent yet = 207; refunded, a claimable buyer of 2 seats at 100 + 5 = 210 with its
     * dust sent. 4295 in all.
     */
    function otherPools(): void {
      chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 5, taken: 10 }));
      chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 6, seat_price: '100', target: 3, taken: 3, bonus: '50', status: 'filled' }));
      chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 7, taken: 192, status: 'settled' }));
      chain.setPool(
        poolView({ id: 8, seat_price: '100', taken: 3, bonus: '10', status: 'expired', bonus_per_seat: '3', refund_cursor: 1, buyer_count: 3 }),
      );
      chain.seats.set(8, [
        { buyer: 'a.testnet', seats: 1, state: 'refunded' },
        { buyer: 'b.testnet', seats: 1, state: 'committed' },
        { buyer: 'c.testnet', seats: 1, state: 'claimable' },
      ]);
      chain.setPool(
        poolView({ id: 9, seat_price: '100', taken: 2, bonus: '11', status: 'refunded', bonus_per_seat: '5', dust_sent: true, buyer_count: 1 }),
      );
      chain.seats.set(9, [{ buyer: 'd.testnet', seats: 2, state: 'claimable' }]);
    }

    it('passes when the pools contract holds what every pool still owes', async () => {
      settledFills();
      otherPools();
      chain.register(POOLS, 4_295n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'solvency')).toEqual({ ok: true, detail: 'the pools contract holds 4295 and owes 4295 across 6 pools' });
    });

    it('fails when the pools contract holds less than every pool still owes', async () => {
      settledFills();
      otherPools();
      chain.register(POOLS, 4_294n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'solvency')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: 'the pools contract holds 4294 but owes 4295 across 6 pools' });
    });

    it('reads the pools contract’s balance and every view it sums at one final block', async () => {
      settledFills();
      otherPools();
      chain.register(POOLS, 4_295n);
      // The final block moves on at each read of it, as it does while the check runs.
      const finalBlock = chain.finalBlock.bind(chain);
      chain.finalBlock = async () => {
        chain.block = { ...chain.block, height: chain.block.height + 1n };
        return finalBlock();
      };

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'solvency').ok).toBe(true);
      const pinned = chain.reads.filter((read) => read.atHeight !== null);
      expect(pinned.map(({ method, args }) => [method, args])).toEqual([
        ['ftBalanceOf', [POOLS]],
        ['listPools', [0, 100]],
        ['getSeats', [8, 0, 100]],
        ['getSeats', [9, 0, 100]],
      ]);
      expect(pinned.map((read) => read.atHeight)).toEqual(Array(4).fill(chain.block.height));
    });

    it('reads every page of pools', async () => {
      settledFills();
      for (let id = 1; id <= 100; id++) chain.setPool(poolView({ id, status: 'settled' }));
      chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 101 }));
      chain.register(POOLS, 1_728n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'solvency')).toEqual({ ok: true, detail: 'the pools contract holds 1728 and owes 1728 across 102 pools' });
    });
  });

  describe('balances', () => {
    it('fails a buyer whose balance did not change by its seats’ price', async () => {
      const baseline = settledFills();
      chain.register(buyer(1), 9_650n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0, baseline });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'buyer balances')).toEqual({
        ok: false,
        detail: `1 of 2 buyers off: ${buyer(1)} changed by -350, expected -360`,
      });
    });

    it('fails a provider whose balance did not change by the seats taken', async () => {
      const baseline = settledFills();
      chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_500n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0, baseline });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'provider balance')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `${PROVIDER} changed by +500, expected +540` });
    });

    it('fails a pools contract whose balance changed', async () => {
      const baseline = settledFills();
      chain.register(POOLS, 1n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0, baseline });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'pools contract balance')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `${POOLS} changed by +1, expected 0` });
    });

    it('fails a refunded pool’s buyer that did not get its bonus share', async () => {
      const baseline = refundedFails();
      chain.register(buyer(2), 10_000n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 1, scenario: FAILS, baseline });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'buyer balances')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `1 of 6 buyers off: ${buyer(2)} changed by 0, expected +600` });
    });

    it('fails a refunded pool’s provider that did not get the dust back', async () => {
      const baseline = refundedFails();
      chain.register(PROVIDER, 6_928n);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 1, scenario: FAILS, baseline });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'provider balance')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `${PROVIDER} changed by -3072, expected -3000` });
    });

    it('compares only the accounts in the baseline, and only the pool’s buyers', async () => {
      settledFills();
      // buyer-03 holds no seat of this pool, so what it spent elsewhere during the run is not checked.
      chain.register(buyer(3), 1n);
      const baseline = new Map([
        [buyer(1), 10_000n],
        [buyer(3), 10_000n],
      ]);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0, baseline });

      expect(names(report)).not.toContain('provider balance');
      expect(names(report)).not.toContain('pools contract balance');
      expect(lineOf(report, 'buyer balances')).toEqual({ ok: true, detail: '1 buyer changed as expected' });
    });

    it('checks no balance without a baseline', async () => {
      settledFills();

      expect(names(await run({ poolId: 0 }))).toEqual(['status', 'buyers', 'solvency', 'commit gas', 'payout gas']);
    });
  });

  describe('commit gas', () => {
    it('fails each commit that burnt more than QUORUM_COMMIT_MIN_GAS', async () => {
      settledFills();
      const heavy = commit(0, buyer(3), 1, 180, { onTransfer: 50n * TGAS });

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 }, testConfig({ commitMinGas: 52n * TGAS }));

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `3 commits, limit 52.00 Tgas: ${heavy} burnt 53.74 Tgas` });
    });

    it('accepts a commit that burnt exactly QUORUM_COMMIT_MIN_GAS', async () => {
      settledFills();

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 }, testConfig({ commitMinGas: FIXTURE_COMMIT_GAS }));

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas').ok).toBe(true);
    });

    it('fails a commit whose transaction the RPC does not know as one the relayer signed', async () => {
      settledFills();
      const txHash = hashOf('a commit signed by the buyer');
      feed.push({ at: NOW_MS, poolId: 0, kind: 'commit', account: buyer(3), seats: 1, amount: 180n, txHash, ok: true });
      chain.addOutcome(buyer(3), relayedCommit({ txHash, relayer: RELAYER, buyer: buyer(3), token: TOKEN, pools: POOLS }));

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `3 commits, limit 50.00 Tgas: ${txHash} is unknown to the RPC` });
    });

    it('fails a commit whose outcome has no receipt on its buyer', async () => {
      settledFills();
      const txHash = hashOf('a commit of another buyer');
      feed.push({ at: NOW_MS, poolId: 0, kind: 'commit', account: buyer(3), seats: 1, amount: 180n, txHash, ok: true });
      chain.addOutcome(RELAYER, relayedCommit({ txHash, relayer: RELAYER, buyer: buyer(4), token: TOKEN, pools: POOLS }));

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

    it("fails when one of the swarm's buyers holds seats but the feed has no commit of it, saying why that can be", async () => {

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas')).toEqual({

          `1 commit, limit 50.00 Tgas: not measured: ${buyer(2)} (1 seat) holds seats, but the activity feed has no commit of it ` +
          "(the gateway records no relay whose result was unknown; its feed is in its QUORUM_DATA_DIR)",
      });
      expect(report.lines).toHaveLength(5);

    it('fails, naming each of them, when the feed holds no commit at all of a pool whose seats were taken', async () => {
      settledFills();
      feed = feed.filter((record) => record.kind !== 'commit');

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas')).toEqual({
        ok: false,
        detail:
          `no commits, limit 50.00 Tgas: not measured: ${buyer(1)} (2 seats), ${buyer(2)} (1 seat) hold seats, but the activity feed ` +
          "has no commit of theirs (the gateway records no relay whose result was unknown; its feed is in its QUORUM_DATA_DIR)",
      });
    });

    it('takes no failed commit record for the commit of a buyer holding seats', async () => {
      settledFills();
      for (const record of feed) if (record.kind === 'commit' && record.account === buyer(2)) record.ok = false;

    });

    it('measures a commit a buyer learned the transaction of, which the feed lacks, once its outcome shows the seats it took', async () => {

      chain.addOutcome(RELAYER, relayedCommit({ txHash, relayer: RELAYER, buyer: buyer(2), token: TOKEN, pools: POOLS, poolsLogs: [committed] }));

      const report = await checkPool(testConfig(), deps(), { poolId: 0, scenario: FILLS, extraCommits: [{ account: buyer(2), txHash }] });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas')).toEqual({ ok: true, detail: '2 commits, at most 5.70 Tgas each (limit 50.00 Tgas)' });
    });

    it('measures nothing from a learned transaction the RPC does not know, or whose outcome took no seats for its buyer in the pool', async () => {
      settledFills();
      feed = feed.filter((record) => !(record.kind === 'commit' && record.account === buyer(2)));
      const elsewhere = hashOf('a commit to another pool');
      const otherPool = eventLog({ event: 'seats_committed', data: { pool_id: 5, buyer: buyer(2), seats: 1, amount: '180', taken: 1, target: 3 } });
      chain.addOutcome(RELAYER, relayedCommit({ txHash: elsewhere, relayer: RELAYER, buyer: buyer(2), token: TOKEN, pools: POOLS, poolsLogs: [otherPool] }));
      const extraCommits = [
        { account: buyer(2), txHash: hashOf('never relayed') },
        { account: buyer(2), txHash: elsewhere },
      ];

      const report = await checkPool(testConfig(), deps(), { poolId: 0, scenario: FILLS, extraCommits });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas').ok).toBe(false);
      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas').detail).toMatch(/^1 commit, limit 50\.00 Tgas: not measured: /);
    });

    it('passes a pool no one committed to', async () => {
      chain.setPool(poolView({ id: 2, deadline_ms: NOW_MS - 60_000, status: 'refunded', dust_sent: true }));
      keeperTx(2, [{ kind: 'dust', account: PROVIDER, seats: 0, amount: 1728n }], [PAYOUT]);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 2, scenario: FAILS });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'commit gas')).toEqual({ ok: true, detail: 'no commits' });
      expect(report.failed).toBe(false);
    });

  describe('payout gas', () => {
    it('shows gas truncated to 2 decimals, so that a transfer that passes at 4.996 Tgas shows as 4.99, not 5.00', async () => {
      settledFills();

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'payout gas')).toEqual({
        ok: true,
        detail: '2 transactions, 2 ft_transfers at most 4.99 Tgas, 2 callbacks at most 1.49 Tgas (each under 5.00 Tgas)',

    it('fails an ft_transfer that burnt 5 Tgas', async () => {

      const txHash = keeperTx(0, [{ kind: 'settle', account: PROVIDER, seats: 3, amount: 2268n }], [{ transfer: 5n * TGAS, callback: CALLBACK_GAS }]);

      const report = await run({ poolId: 0 });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'payout gas')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `2 transactions: ${txHash} ft_transfer burnt 5.00 Tgas` });

      const report = await run({ poolId: 1, scenario: FAILS });

      expect(lineOf(report, 'payout gas')).toEqual({ ok: false, detail: `2 transactions: ${txHash} callback burnt 5.00 Tgas` });

    it('measures an ft_transfer that failed, as a refund the token refused does', async () => {
      refundedFails();
      const txHash = keeperTx(
        1,

    });

    it("fails a refunded pool when one of the swarm's refunded buyers has no refund in the feed, saying why that can be", async () => {
      refundedFails();
```
