```typescript
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util';
import { ConfigError, type Env } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { loadMcpConfig, type McpConfig } from '../src/config.ts';

const EXAMPLE = fileURLToPath(new URL('../.env.example', import.meta.url));
/** The repository root. */
const REPO_ROOT = resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../..', import.meta.url)));
const PARENT = 'parent.testnet';
const ABSOLUTE = resolve('/var/lib/quorum');

/** The one required variable, plus `overrides` (`undefined` unsets one). */
function env(overrides: Env = {}): Env {
  return { QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT, ...overrides };
}

/** The problem lines of the ConfigError that loadMcpConfig throws for `vars`. */
function problems(vars: Env): readonly string[] {
  try {
    loadMcpConfig(vars);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ConfigError) return error.problems;
    throw error;
  }
  throw new Error('loadMcpConfig accepted the configuration');
}

describe('loadMcpConfig', () => {
  it('applies every default when only the parent account is set', () => {
    expect(loadMcpConfig(env())).toEqual<McpConfig>({
      network: 'near:testnet',
      rpcUrl: 'https://test.rpc.fastnear.com',
      gatewayUrl: 'http://localhost:8402',
      parent: PARENT,
      token: '3e2210e1184b45b64c8a434c0a7e7b23cc04ea7eb7a6c3c32520d03d4afcb8af',
      poolsContract: 'pools.parent.testnet',
      blockTimeMs: 1000,
      maxTimeoutSeconds: 120,
      mcpAccount: 'buyer-llm.parent.testnet',
      credentialsDir: join(homedir(), '.near-credentials'),
      spendCap: 10_000n,
      spendFile: join(REPO_ROOT, 'data', 'mcp-spend.json'),
    });
  });

  it('reads its own variables when they are set', () => {
    const config = loadMcpConfig(
      env({
        QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT: 'agent.example.testnet',
        QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR: join(ABSOLUTE, 'keys'),
        QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP: '2500',
        QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE: join(ABSOLUTE, 'spend.json'),
      }),
    );
    expect(config).toMatchObject({
      mcpAccount: 'agent.example.testnet',
      credentialsDir: join(ABSOLUTE, 'keys'),
      spendCap: 2500n,
      spendFile: join(ABSOLUTE, 'spend.json'),
    });
  });

  it('reads the buyer settings it shares with the gateway', () => {
    const config = loadMcpConfig(
      env({
        QUORUM_NETWORK: 'near:sandbox',
        QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:9000/',
        QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS: '600',
        QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '240',
      }),
    );
    expect(config).toMatchObject({ network: 'near:sandbox', gatewayUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:9000', blockTimeMs: 600, maxTimeoutSeconds: 240 });
  });

  it('accepts a spend cap of 0, which refuses every payment', () => {
    expect(loadMcpConfig(env({ QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP: '0' })).spendCap).toBe(0n);
  });

  it('lists every invalid variable at once, the shared ones first', () => {
    expect(
      problems({
        QUORUM_NETWORK: 'near:mainnet',
        QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT: 'Buyer LLM',
        QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR: '~/.near-credentials',
        QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP: '0.01',
        QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE: 'data/mcp-spend.json',
      }),
    ).toEqual([
      'QUORUM_NETWORK must be near:testnet or near:sandbox, got "near:mainnet"',
      'QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT is required',
      'QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT must be a NEAR account id, got "Buyer LLM"',
      'QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR must be an absolute path, got "~/.near-credentials"',
      'QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE must be an absolute path, got "data/mcp-spend.json"',
      'QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP must be an amount in base units (decimal digits, such as 10000), got "0.01"',
    ]);
  });

  it('ships an example file whose values, once the parent is filled in, are the defaults', async () => {
    const example = parseEnv(await readFile(EXAMPLE, 'utf8'));
    expect(loadMcpConfig({ ...example, ...env() })).toEqual(loadMcpConfig(env()));
  });

  it('ships an example file that lists exactly the variables loadMcpConfig reads', async () => {
    const read = new Set<string>();
    const tracked = new Proxy(env(), {
      get: (target, name) => {
        if (typeof name === 'string') read.add(name);
        return Reflect.get(target, name);
      },
    });
    loadMcpConfig(tracked);
    const listed = [...(await readFile(EXAMPLE, 'utf8')).matchAll(/^#?(QUORUM_[A-Z_]+)=/gm)].map((m) => m[1]);
    expect(listed.sort()).toEqual([...read].sort());
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { mkdtemp, readdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { PaymentNotSentError, readSpendFile, SpendFileError, writeSpendFile, type BuyerPaymentAnswer } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { PaymentOutcomeUnknownError, SpendLedger } from '../src/spend.ts';
import { BUYER, filled, offerFor, pending, signed, TX_HASH } from './fixtures.ts';

/** The offer for 2 seats at 180: a payment of 360. */
const OFFER = offerFor(2);
const CAP = 1000n;

let dir: string;
let path: string;

beforeEach(async () => {
  dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'quorum-mcp-spend-'));
  path = join(dir, 'state', 'mcp-spend.json');
});

afterEach(async () => {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

function ledger(cap = CAP, log?: (line: string) => void): SpendLedger {
  return new SpendLedger({ path, account: BUYER, cap, ...(log === undefined ? {} : { log }) });
}

/** A send that records each call and answers `answer`. */
function sender(answer: BuyerPaymentAnswer) {
  const calls: bigint[] = [];
  const send = async (maxAmount: bigint): Promise<BuyerPaymentAnswer> => {
    calls.push(maxAmount);
    return answer;
  };
  return { send, calls };
}

describe('SpendLedger.left', () => {
  it('is the whole cap when nothing was spent, with no spend file yet', async () => {
    expect(await ledger().left()).toBe(1000n);
  });

  it('is the cap less the total in the spend file', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 640n);
    expect(await ledger().left()).toBe(360n);
  });

  it('is 0 when the total is above the cap', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 1500n);
    expect(await ledger().left()).toBe(0n);
  });

  it("refuses a spend file that holds another account's total", async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, `buyer-01.parent.testnet`, 0n);
    await expect(ledger().left()).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: 'SpendFileError', problem: 'other_account' });
  });
});

describe('SpendLedger.pay', () => {
  it('reserves the price in the spend file before sending, and passes it as the most to pay', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
    let reserved: bigint | undefined;
    const result = await ledger().pay(OFFER, async (maxAmount) => {
      reserved = await readSpendFile(path, BUYER);
      expect(maxAmount).toBe(360n);
      return pending(2);
    });
    expect(reserved).toBe(460n);
    expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'answered', answer: pending(2), spent: 360n, left: 540n });
  });

  const NO_SEATS: BuyerPaymentAnswer[] = [
    { kind: 'declined', refusal: { code: 'wrong_pay_to', detail: 'payTo is not pools.parent.testnet' } },
    signed({ kind: 'refused', error: 'insufficient_balance', offer: OFFER }),
    signed({ kind: 'no_seats_taken' }),
    signed({ kind: 'pool_expired', txHash: TX_HASH }),
    signed({ kind: 'unknown_pool' }),
    signed({ kind: 'unavailable' }),
  ];

  it.each(NO_SEATS)('releases the reserved price when the answer is $kind: nothing was spent', async (answer) => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
    const result = await ledger().pay(OFFER, sender(answer).send);
    expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'answered', answer, spent: 0n, left: 900n });
    expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(100n);
  });

  it.each([
    ['a 202 for every seat paid', pending(2), 360n],
    ['a 202 for fewer seats than paid', pending(1), 180n],
    ['a 200 for every seat paid', filled(2), 360n],
    ['a 200 for fewer seats than paid', filled(1), 180n],
    ['a 200 that also counts seats held before', filled(5), 360n],
    ['a relay_failed 502', signed({ kind: 'relay_failed', txHash: TX_HASH }), 360n],
    ['a result_unknown 502', signed({ kind: 'result_unknown', txHash: TX_HASH }), 360n],
  ])('keeps the seats taken at the seat price, at most the reserved price, for %s', async (_, answer, spent) => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
    const result = await ledger().pay(OFFER, sender(answer).send);
    expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'answered', answer, spent, left: 900n - spent });
    expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(100n + spent);
  });

  it('refuses a payment above what is left, and sends nothing', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 700n);
    const { send, calls } = sender(pending(2));
    expect(await ledger().pay(OFFER, send)).toEqual({ kind: 'over_spend_cap', amount: 360n, left: 300n });
    expect(calls).toEqual([]);
    expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(700n);
  });

  it('pays exactly what is left', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 640n);
    expect(await ledger().pay(OFFER, sender(pending(2)).send)).toMatchObject({ kind: 'answered', spent: 360n, left: 0n });
  });

  it('keeps the price reserved and throws PaymentOutcomeUnknownError when sending fails', async () => {
    const cause = new TypeError('fetch failed');
    const error = await ledger()
      .pay(OFFER, async () => {
        throw cause;
      })
      .catch((e: unknown) => e);
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(PaymentOutcomeUnknownError);
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ amount: 360n, cause, message: 'the payment of 360 may have been sent' });
    expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(360n);
  });

  it('releases the reserved price when the payment was never sent, and answers not_sent', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
    const error = new PaymentNotSentError('chain_read', 'could not read the final block: nothing was sent', new Error('502'));
    const result = await ledger().pay(OFFER, async () => {
      expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(460n);
      throw error;
    });
    expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'not_sent', error, left: 900n });
    expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(100n);
  });

  it('keeps what another writer added when it releases a payment that was never sent', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
    const result = await ledger().pay(OFFER, async () => {
      await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n + 360n + 50n);
      throw new PaymentNotSentError('signing', 'could not sign the payment: nothing was sent', new Error('bad key'));
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'not_sent', left: CAP - 150n });
    expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(150n);
  });

  describe('when the total cannot be settled once the payment is answered', () => {
    /** A send that leaves the spend file unreadable as a total, then answers `answer` or throws it. */
    const breaking = (answer: BuyerPaymentAnswer | Error) => async (): Promise<BuyerPaymentAnswer> => {
      await writeFile(path, 'not a spend file');
      if (answer instanceof Error) throw answer;
      return answer;
    };

    it('still returns the answer, counting its whole price, and logs why', async () => {
      await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
      const logs: string[] = [];
      const result = await ledger(CAP, (line) => logs.push(line)).pay(OFFER, breaking(pending(1)));
      // The reservation, 100 + 360, is what the file was last written with.
      expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'answered', answer: pending(1), spent: 360n, left: 540n });
      expect(logs).toEqual([expect.stringMatching(/^the spend total could not be settled .*360.* stays counted/)]);
      expect(logs[0]).toContain('does not hold an account and a decimal total');
      expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toBe('not a spend file');
    });

    it('still answers not_sent for a payment that was never sent, its price still counted', async () => {
      await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
      const logs: string[] = [];
      const error = new PaymentNotSentError('signing', 'could not sign the payment: nothing was sent', new Error('bad key'));
      const result = await ledger(CAP, (line) => logs.push(line)).pay(OFFER, breaking(error));
      expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'not_sent', error, left: 540n });
      expect(logs).toHaveLength(1);
    });
  });

  it("refuses to count from another account's spend file, and sends nothing", async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, 'buyer-01.parent.testnet', 0n);
    const { send, calls } = sender(pending(2));
    await expect(ledger().pay(OFFER, send)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(SpendFileError);
    expect(calls).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('continues the total of an earlier run: a restart does not reset it', async () => {
    await ledger().pay(OFFER, sender(pending(2)).send);
    expect(await ledger().left()).toBe(640n);
  });

  it('reads the total each time, so a total cleared by setup since the last payment counts from 0', async () => {
    const theLedger = ledger();
    await theLedger.pay(OFFER, sender(pending(2)).send);
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 0n);
    expect(await theLedger.pay(OFFER, sender(pending(2)).send)).toMatchObject({ spent: 360n, left: 640n });
  });

  it.each([
    ['every seat paid', pending(2), 360n],
    ['fewer seats than paid', pending(1), 180n],
    ['no seats', signed({ kind: 'no_seats_taken' }), 0n],
  ])(
    'counts only its own spend once setup clears the total while the payment is in flight: %s',
    async (_, answer: BuyerPaymentAnswer, spent) => {
      await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
      const result = await ledger().pay(OFFER, async () => {
        await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 0n);
        return answer;
      });
      expect(result).toEqual({ kind: 'answered', answer, spent, left: CAP - spent });
      expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(spent);
    },
  );

  it('keeps what another writer added to the total while the payment was in flight', async () => {
    await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n);
    const result = await ledger().pay(OFFER, async () => {
      // Another server sharing the file reserves 360 on top of this payment's reservation.
      await writeSpendFile(path, BUYER, 100n + 360n + 360n);
      return pending(1);
    });
    expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(100n + 360n + 180n);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ spent: 180n, left: CAP - 640n });
  });

  it('sends one payment at a time, each reserved after the one before is counted', async () => {
    const theLedger = ledger();
    let answerFirst: ((answer: BuyerPaymentAnswer) => void) | undefined;
    let firstAnswered = false;
    const first = theLedger.pay(OFFER, () => new Promise((resolve) => (answerFirst = resolve)));
    const second = theLedger.pay(OFFER, async () => {
      expect(firstAnswered).toBe(true);
      expect(await readSpendFile(path, BUYER)).toBe(720n);
      return pending(2);
    });
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(answerFirst).toBeDefined());
    firstAnswered = true;
    answerFirst?.(pending(2));
    expect(await first).toMatchObject({ spent: 360n, left: 640n });
    expect(await second).toMatchObject({ spent: 360n, left: 280n });
  });

  it('still sends the next payment after one fails', async () => {
    const theLedger = ledger();
    const failed = theLedger.pay(OFFER, async () => {
      throw new TypeError('fetch failed');
    });
    const next = theLedger.pay(OFFER, sender(pending(2)).send);
    await expect(failed).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(PaymentOutcomeUnknownError);
    expect(await next).toMatchObject({ spent: 360n, left: 280n });
  });

  it('writes the total atomically, leaving no temporary file beside it', async () => {
    await ledger().pay(OFFER, sender(signed({ kind: 'no_seats_taken' })).send);
    expect(await readdir(dirname(path))).toEqual(['mcp-spend.json']);
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { formatUnits, readTokenUnits, TokenMetadataError, tokenUnits } from '../src/token.ts';

const USDC_METADATA = {
  spec: 'ft-1.0.0',
  name: 'USDC',
  symbol: 'USDC',
  icon: null,
  reference: null,
  reference_hash: null,
  decimals: 6,
};

describe('formatUnits', () => {
  it.each([
    [180n, 6, '0.000180'],
    [10_000n, 6, '0.010000'],
    [1_234_567n, 6, '1.234567'],
    [36_288_000_000n, 6, '36288.000000'],
    [0n, 6, '0.000000'],
    [180n, 0, '180'],
    [5n, 24, '0.000000000000000000000005'],
  ])('writes %s base units with %i decimals as %s', (amount, decimals, text) => {
    expect(formatUnits(amount, decimals)).toBe(text);
  });

  it('refuses a negative amount', () => {
    expect(() => formatUnits(-1n, 6)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe('tokenUnits', () => {
  it("reads the decimals and the symbol of a token's ft_metadata", () => {
    expect(tokenUnits(USDC_METADATA)).toEqual({ decimals: 6, symbol: 'USDC' });
  });

  it.each([
    ['is not an object', null],
    ['has no decimals', { symbol: 'USDC' }],
    ['has fractional decimals', { ...USDC_METADATA, decimals: 6.5 }],
    ['has decimals above 255, a u8', { ...USDC_METADATA, decimals: 256 }],
    ['has decimals as a string', { ...USDC_METADATA, decimals: '6' }],
    ['has an empty symbol', { ...USDC_METADATA, symbol: '' }],
    ['has a symbol with spaces', { ...USDC_METADATA, symbol: 'USD Coin' }],
    ['has a symbol over 16 characters', { ...USDC_METADATA, symbol: 'U'.repeat(17) }],
  ])('throws TokenMetadataError for metadata that %s', (_, metadata) => {
    expect(() => tokenUnits(metadata)).toThrow(TokenMetadataError);
  });

  it('accepts the symbols of bridged tokens, with a dot or a hyphen', () => {
    expect(tokenUnits({ ...USDC_METADATA, symbol: 'USDC.e' }).symbol).toBe('USDC.e');
  });
});

describe('readTokenUnits', () => {
  it("calls the token's ft_metadata view at final finality", async () => {
    const calls: unknown[] = [];
    const provider = {
      async callFunction<T>(params: unknown): Promise<T | undefined> {
        calls.push(params);
        return USDC_METADATA as T;
      },
    };
    expect(await readTokenUnits(provider, 'usdc.testnet')).toEqual({ decimals: 6, symbol: 'USDC' });
    expect(calls).toEqual([{ contractId: 'usdc.testnet', method: 'ft_metadata', args: {}, blockQuery: { finality: 'final' } }]);
  });
});
```

The swarm's two test files, in full: `config.test.ts` gains the `GATEWAY_EXAMPLE`, `MCP_EXAMPLE` and
`VARIABLE` constants and the test that heads each section with its readers; `env-files.test.ts`
gains the import of `loadMcpConfig` and `McpConfig`, `mcpEnvText` and `writeMcpEnv` in the
env-files import list, and the `mcpEnvText` and `writeMcpEnv` blocks.

```typescript
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

import { loadSwarmConfig, type SwarmConfig } from '../src/config.ts';

const EXAMPLE = fileURLToPath(new URL('../.env.example', import.meta.url));
const GATEWAY_EXAMPLE = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../gateway/.env.example', import.meta.url));
const MCP_EXAMPLE = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../mcp/.env.example', import.meta.url));
/** A variable line of an example file, set or commented out: its name is the first group. */
const VARIABLE = /^#?(QUORUM_[A-Z_]+)=/gm;
const PARENT = 'parent.testnet';

/** The one required variable, plus `overrides` (`undefined` unsets one). */
function env(overrides: Env = {}): Env {
  return { QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT, ...overrides };
}

/** The problems loadSwarmConfig lists for `values`, one per line of its ConfigError. */
function problems(values: Env): readonly string[] {
  try {
    loadSwarmConfig(values);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ConfigError) return error.problems;
    throw error;
  }
  return [];
}

  it('ships an example file whose values, once the parent account is filled in, are the defaults', async () => {
    const example = parseEnv(await readFile(EXAMPLE, 'utf8'));
    expect(loadSwarmConfig({ ...example, ...env() })).toEqual(loadSwarmConfig(env()));
  });

  it('says in its example file that every command but env and help checks the chain QUORUM_RPC_URL serves', async () => {
    const text = (await readFile(EXAMPLE, 'utf8')).replace(/\n# /g, ' ');
    expect(text).toContain('Every swarm command but env and help stops unless it serves that chain');
  });

  it('heads each section of its example file with the other apps that read its variables, and only those', async () => {
    const text = await readFile(EXAMPLE, 'utf8');
    const gateway = new Set([...(await readFile(GATEWAY_EXAMPLE, 'utf8')).matchAll(VARIABLE)].map((m) => m[1]));
    const mcp = new Set([...(await readFile(MCP_EXAMPLE, 'utf8')).matchAll(VARIABLE)].map((m) => m[1]));
    const sections = text.split(/^# --- /m).slice(1);
    expect(sections.length).toBeGreaterThan(1);
    for (const section of sections) {
      const heading = section.slice(0, section.indexOf('\n'));
      const readers = { gateway: heading.includes('the gateway'), mcp: heading.includes('the MCP server') };
      for (const [, name] of section.matchAll(VARIABLE)) {
        expect({ name, gateway: gateway.has(name), mcp: mcp.has(name) }).toEqual({ name, ...readers });
      }
    }
  });

  it('ships an example file that lists exactly the variables loadSwarmConfig reads', async () => {
    const read = new Set<string>();
    const tracked = new Proxy(env(), {
      get: (target, name) => {
        if (typeof name === 'string') read.add(name);
        return Reflect.get(target, name);
      },
    });
    loadSwarmConfig(tracked);
    const listed = [...(await readFile(EXAMPLE, 'utf8')).matchAll(/^#?(QUORUM_[A-Z_]+)=/gm)].map((m) => m[1]);
    expect(listed.sort()).toEqual([...read].sort());
  });
});
```

`apps/swarm/test/env-files.test.ts`:

```typescript
import { createPrivateKey, createPublicKey } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdtemp, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util';
import { folderKeyPath, KeyFileError, keyFolderPath, writeKeyFile } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { KeyPair } from 'near-api-js';
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
// The apps' own loaders, from their sources: the swarm itself never imports another app.
import { loadConfig, type GatewayConfig } from '../../gateway/src/config.ts';
import { loadMcpConfig, type McpConfig } from '../../mcp/src/config.ts';
import { loadSwarmConfig, type SwarmConfig } from '../src/config.ts';
import {
  aclNotice,
  EnvFileExistsError,
  envFilePath,
  gatewayEnvText,
  mcpEnvText,
  newCredentialJwk,
  writeEnvFile,
  writeGatewayEnv,
  writeMcpEnv,
} from '../src/env-files.ts';

const RELAYER = 'gas.test.near';

let dir: string;

beforeEach(async () => {
  dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'quorum-env-files-'));
});

afterEach(async () => {
  await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

/** A swarm configuration in which no shared value is the apps' default, with its files in the temp folder. */
function sandboxConfig(overrides: Partial<SwarmConfig> = {}): SwarmConfig {
  return {
    ...loadSwarmConfig({
      QUORUM_NETWORK: 'near:sandbox',
      QUORUM_RPC_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:3030',
      QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:9000',
      QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: 'test.near',
      QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT: 'musd.test.near',
      QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT: 'escrow.test.near',
      QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS: '600',
      QUORUM_RELAYER_ACCOUNT: RELAYER,
      QUORUM_PROVIDER_ACCOUNT: 'seller.test.near',
      QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT: 'agent.test.near',
      QUORUM_COMMIT_MIN_GAS: '40000000000000',
      QUORUM_COMMIT_MAX_GAS: '60000000000000',
      QUORUM_BUYER_BUDGET: '20000',
      QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR: join(dir, 'keys'),
      QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE: join(dir, 'spend.json'),
      QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '90',
    }),
    ...overrides,
  };
}

/** The error `promise` rejects with; fails the test if it resolves. */
async function rejection(promise: Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
  try {
    await promise;
  } catch (error) {
    return error;
  }
  throw new Error('the promise resolved');
}

/** Writes `count` new keys to the relayer's key folder and returns them. */
async function relayerKeys(config: SwarmConfig, count: number): Promise<KeyPair[]> {
  const folder = keyFolderPath(config.credentialsDir, config.network, config.relayer);
  const keys = Array.from({ length: count }, () => KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'));
  for (const key of keys) await writeKeyFile(folderKeyPath(folder, key.getPublicKey()), config.relayer, key);
  return keys;
}

describe('gatewayEnvText', () => {
  it("is read by the gateway's own loader as the swarm is configured, with every relayer key and the credential key", () => {
    const keys = [KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'), KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519'), KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')];
    const jwk = newCredentialJwk();
    const gateway = loadConfig(parseEnv(gatewayEnvText(sandboxConfig(), keys, jwk)));
    expect(gateway).toMatchObject<Partial<GatewayConfig>>({
      network: 'near:sandbox',
      rpcUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:3030',
      publicUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:9000',
      parent: 'test.near',
      token: 'musd.test.near',
      poolsContract: 'escrow.test.near',
      relayer: RELAYER,
      provider: 'seller.test.near',
      relayerKeys: keys.map((key) => key.toString()),
      credentialJwk: { ...jwk },
      minGas: 40_000_000_000_000n,
      maxGas: 60_000_000_000_000n,
      blockTimeMs: 600,
    });
  });

  it('sets only the variables the gateway shares with the swarm, and its two secrets', () => {
    const text = gatewayEnvText(sandboxConfig(), [KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')], newCredentialJwk());
    expect(Object.keys(parseEnv(text)).sort()).toEqual([
      'QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS',
      'QUORUM_COMMIT_MAX_GAS',
      'QUORUM_COMMIT_MIN_GAS',
      'QUORUM_CREDENTIAL_JWK',
      'QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL',
      'QUORUM_NETWORK',
      'QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT',
      'QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT',
      'QUORUM_PROVIDER_ACCOUNT',
      'QUORUM_RELAYER_ACCOUNT',
      'QUORUM_RELAYER_KEYS',
      'QUORUM_RPC_URL',
      'QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT',
    ]);
  });

  it('refuses a value that would not read back as it is, naming the variable and not the value', () => {
    const config = sandboxConfig({ rpcUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:3030/#fragment' });
    expect(() => gatewayEnvText(config, [KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')], newCredentialJwk())).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => gatewayEnvText(config, [KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')], newCredentialJwk())).toThrow(/QUORUM_RPC_URL/);
    expect(() => gatewayEnvText(config, [KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519')], newCredentialJwk())).not.toThrow(/fragment/);
  });

  it('needs at least one relayer key', () => {
    expect(() => gatewayEnvText(sandboxConfig(), [], newCredentialJwk())).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe('mcpEnvText', () => {
  it("is read by the MCP server's own loader as the swarm is configured, with the spend cap at the buyer budget", () => {

    const jwk = newCredentialJwk();
    expect(Object.keys(jwk).sort()).toEqual(['crv', 'd', 'kty', 'x']);
    expect([jwk.kty, jwk.crv]).toEqual(['OKP', 'Ed25519']);
    expect(createPublicKey(createPrivateKey({ key: { ...jwk }, format: 'jwk' })).export({ format: 'jwk' }).x).toBe(jwk.x);
  });

  it('is a new key each time', () => {
    expect(newCredentialJwk().d).not.toBe(newCredentialJwk().d);
  });

  it('writes the text to a new file', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, '.env');
    await writeEnvFile(path, 'QUORUM_NETWORK=near:sandbox\n');
    expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toBe('QUORUM_NETWORK=near:sandbox\n');
  });

  it('refuses to write over a file that exists, and says where it is', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, '.env');
    await writeFile(path, 'KEPT=1\n');
    const error = await rejection(writeEnvFile(path, 'QUORUM_NETWORK=near:sandbox\n'));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(EnvFileExistsError);
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ path });
    expect((error as Error).message).toContain(path);
    expect(await readFile(path, 'utf8')).toBe('KEPT=1\n');
  });

  it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')('makes the file readable by its owner only', async () => {
    const path = join(dir, '.env');
    await writeEnvFile(path, 'QUORUM_NETWORK=near:sandbox\n');

    const config = sandboxConfig();

    const path = join(dir, 'gateway.env');

    const error = await rejection(writeGatewayEnv(sandboxConfig(), join(dir, 'gateway.env')));
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(KeyFileError);
    expect(error).toMatchObject({ problem: 'missing' });
  });
});

describe('writeMcpEnv', () => {

    expect(await rejection(writeMcpEnv(config, path))).toBeInstanceOf(EnvFileExistsError);
```

```bash
# MCP server configuration. Copy to .env, next to this file, and fill in the required value (left empty
# here); the server reads it wherever it is started from, and a variable set in its environment wins.
# Every other line shows its default, which applies when the variable is unset.
# `swarm env mcp` writes that .env from the swarm's configuration.

# NEAR network, in CAIP-2 form: near:testnet, or near:sandbox for a local test chain. No other is accepted.
# The server exits at startup unless QUORUM_RPC_URL serves that chain (testnet, or any non-public chain).
QUORUM_NETWORK=near:testnet
# NEAR RPC endpoint, read for the buyer's key nonce, the final block height, the token's metadata, and
# each pool the agent is offered (get_pool), which the server checks the gateway's offer against.
# It may carry an API key: the server never writes it, in its log or to the agent.
QUORUM_RPC_URL=https://test.rpc.fastnear.com
# The gateway's base URL, written exactly as the gateway's own QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: its host is the
# recipient that redemption proofs name.
QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8402
# Required. The parent account the system's accounts are created under.
QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT=
# Token the pools contract was initialised with (Circle's USDC on testnet). Offers in another token are refused.
QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT=3e2210e1184b45b64c8a434c0a7e7b23cc04ea7eb7a6c3c32520d03d4afcb8af
# Pools contract account, the only one the buyer pays. Unset means pools.<parent>.
#QUORUM_POOLS_ACCOUNT=
# Block time used to turn an offer's timeout into blocks, in milliseconds. Must equal the gateway's.
QUORUM_BLOCK_TIME_MS=1000
# The longest a payment the buyer signs stays valid, in seconds, from 30 to 3600; shared with the
# swarm. The buyer signs an expiry of the offer's timeout or this, whichever is shorter. Not the
# gateway's QUORUM_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
QUORUM_BUYER_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120
# The buyer the server acts for. Unset means buyer-llm.<parent>.
#QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT=
# Absolute path of the folder that holds the buyer's key file, <folder>/testnet/<account>.json
# (sandbox/ for near:sandbox), in near-cli's layout. Unset means ~/.near-credentials.
#QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR=
# The most the buyer may spend between two runs of `swarm setup`, in the token's base units.
# A payment that would take the running total past it is refused before anything is signed.
QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP=10000
# Absolute path of the file that keeps the running total, so that a restart does not reset it.
# `swarm setup` clears it on every run whose token top-ups go through, also when none was needed;
# a run stopped before then, by a token shortfall for one, leaves it. Unset means
# data/mcp-spend.json at the repository root.
#QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE=
```

`apps/mcp/src/config.ts`:

```typescript
import {
  asAmount,
  completeConfig,
  EnvReader,
  readBuyerSettings,
  readMcpBuyerSettings,
  type BuyerSettings,
  type Env,
  type McpBuyerSettings,
} from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';

/**
 * The MCP server's configuration: the settings a buyer shares with the gateway, its buyer as the
 * swarm also reads it (QUORUM_MCP_ACCOUNT, QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR, QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE), and its own.
 */
export interface McpConfig extends BuyerSettings, McpBuyerSettings {
  /** QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP: the most the buyer may spend between two setups, in the token's base units. */
  spendCap: bigint;
}

/**
 * Reads the configuration from `env`. Throws ConfigError listing every missing or invalid variable,
 * the shared ones first.
 */
export function loadMcpConfig(env: Env): McpConfig {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const base = readBuyerSettings(env, problems);
  const buyer = readMcpBuyerSettings(env, problems, base.parent);
  const read = new EnvReader(env, problems);
  return completeConfig<McpConfig>(
    { ...base, ...buyer, spendCap: read.optional('QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_CAP', '10000', asAmount) },
    problems,
  );
}
```

`apps/mcp/src/spend.ts`:

```typescript
import {
  describeError,
  PaymentNotSentError,
  readSpendFile,
  writeSpendFile,
  type BuyerPaymentAnswer,
} from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import type { Offer } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';

/** What a SpendLedger counts against. */
export interface SpendLedgerOptions {
  /** The spend file that keeps the running total (see readSpendFile). */
  path: string;
  /** The buyer whose payments are counted. */
  account: string;
  /** The most the buyer may spend, in the token's base units. */
  cap: bigint;
  /** Writes one line to the operator's log; standard error by default. */
  log?: (line: string) => void;
}

/** Signs and sends a payment that costs at most `maxAmount`, and returns the answer. */
export type Send = (maxAmount: bigint) => Promise<BuyerPaymentAnswer>;

/** The result of SpendLedger.pay. */
export type LedgerPayment =
  /** The payment would take the total past the cap: nothing was sent. `left` is what the cap leaves. */
  | { kind: 'over_spend_cap'; amount: bigint; left: bigint }
  /** The payment's answer, `spent` the part of its price counted against the cap, `left` what the cap leaves now. */
  | { kind: 'answered'; answer: BuyerPaymentAnswer; spent: bigint; left: bigint }
  /** The payment never left the buyer (`error` says why), so its price was released; `left` is what the cap leaves. */
  | { kind: 'not_sent'; error: PaymentNotSentError; left: bigint };

/**
 * The payment was handed to its sender, which rejected: whether it reached the gateway is unknown,
 * so the ledger keeps its whole price counted. `cause` is the sender's error; the message never
 * quotes it, since a library's message may hold the RPC URL.
 */
export class PaymentOutcomeUnknownError extends Error {
  override name = 'PaymentOutcomeUnknownError';
  readonly amount: bigint;

  constructor(amount: bigint, cause: unknown) {
    super(`the payment of ${amount} may have been sent`, { cause });
    this.amount = amount;
  }
}

/**
 * The spend cap: a running total of what the buyer has paid, kept in the spend file, that no payment
 * may take past the cap. Payments go through the ledger one at a time. Each one is refused before it
 * is sent if its price is above what the cap leaves; otherwise its price is reserved in the file
 * before it is sent, and once it is answered, the part of the price the answer did not spend is
 * released. The total is read from the file for each payment, so a total cleared by `swarm setup`
 * counts from 0 at the next one, and read again when the payment is answered, so a total cleared
 * while the payment was in flight then counts only that payment's spend (see settledTotal).
 *
 * The answers are the gateway's word: a gateway that misreports what it relayed can make the cap count
 * less than was spent. The buyer's token balance is the bound that does not depend on the gateway.
 */
export class SpendLedger {
  readonly cap: bigint;
  readonly #path: string;
  readonly #account: string;
  readonly #log: (line: string) => void;
  /** Settles once the payment in progress, if any, has been counted. */
  #idle: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();

  constructor(opts: SpendLedgerOptions) {
    this.cap = opts.cap;
    this.#path = opts.path;
    this.#account = opts.account;
    this.#log = opts.log ?? ((line) => console.error(line));
  }

  /** What the buyer may still spend: the cap less the total, or 0 once the total has reached the cap. */
  async left(): Promise<bigint> {
    return this.#leftAfter(await readSpendFile(this.#path, this.#account));
  }

  /**
   * Pays `offer` through `send`, once the payments before it are counted. Its price is
   * `offer.maxAmountRequired`, and `send` receives it as the most the payment may cost. What the
   * answer spent:
   * - nothing for an answer that relayed nothing or whose transfer the token returned: `declined`,
   *   `refused` (402), `unavailable` (503), `unknown_pool` (404), `no_seats_taken` (409), `pool_expired`
   *   (410);
   * - the seats taken at the offer's seat price, at most the price, for `pending` (202) and `filled`
   *   (200; its seats include those the buyer held before, hence the bound);
   * - the whole price for `relay_failed` and `result_unknown` (502), since a relayed transaction may
   *   have moved the tokens.
   * When `send` rejects with PaymentNotSentError, the payment never left the buyer: its price is
   * released and the result is `not_sent`. When `send` rejects with any other error, whether the
   * payment reached the gateway is unknown: the price stays counted and PaymentOutcomeUnknownError is
   * thrown. The offer's amounts are decimal strings, as GatewayClient returns them.
   *
   * Once `send` has settled, the result is always returned, so that a payment's receipt is never lost:
   * if the spend file cannot then be read or written, the whole price stays counted (`spent` is the
   * price, `left` what the reservation leaves), and the error goes to the log.
   *
   * Releasing the price on `unavailable` relies on the gateway's guarantee: it answers a payment 503
   * `{error: "chain_unavailable"}` only when a chain read failed before the relay, or its relayer
   * threw before sending the transaction (no relayer key free in time, the final block or the key's
   * nonce unreadable). Once a transaction is sent, the relayer no longer throws, and the answer is a
   * 202, 200, 409, 410 or 502. GatewayClient reads a 503 as `unavailable` only with that body; any
   * other 503 is a GatewayResponseError, so `send` rejects and the price stays counted.
   */
  pay(offer: Offer, send: Send): Promise<LedgerPayment> {
    const payment = this.#idle.then(() => this.#pay(offer, send));
    this.#idle = payment.then(
      () => undefined,
      () => undefined,
    );
    return payment;
  }

  async #pay(offer: Offer, send: Send): Promise<LedgerPayment> {
    const amount = BigInt(offer.maxAmountRequired);
    const seatPrice = BigInt(offer.extra.seatPrice);
    const total = await readSpendFile(this.#path, this.#account);
    const left = this.#leftAfter(total);
    if (amount > left) return { kind: 'over_spend_cap', amount, left };
    const reservation = { total: total + amount, amount };
    await writeSpendFile(this.#path, this.#account, reservation.total);
    let answer: BuyerPaymentAnswer;
    try {
      answer = await send(amount);
    } catch (error) {
      if (!(error instanceof PaymentNotSentError)) throw new PaymentOutcomeUnknownError(amount, error);
      return { kind: 'not_sent', error, left: (await this.#settle(reservation, 0n)).left };
    }
    return { kind: 'answered', answer, ...(await this.#settle(reservation, spentBy(answer, amount, seatPrice))) };
  }

  /**
   * Settles a payment whose reservation of `amount` took the total to `total`, once its answer says
   * it spent `spent` (see settledTotal): returns the part of the price that stays counted, and what the
   * cap leaves. The total is read again: `swarm setup` may have cleared it while the payment was in
   * flight, and a total computed from the first read would bring the cleared amount back. If the file
   * cannot be read or written, the reservation stays as it was written, and the error is logged.
   */
  async #settle(reservation: { total: bigint; amount: bigint }, spent: bigint): Promise<{ spent: bigint; left: bigint }> {
    try {
      const current = await readSpendFile(this.#path, this.#account);
      const settled = settledTotal(current, reservation.amount, spent);
      if (settled !== current) await writeSpendFile(this.#path, this.#account, settled);
      return { spent, left: this.#leftAfter(settled) };
    } catch (error) {
      this.#log(
        `the spend total could not be settled once the payment was answered, so its whole price, ` +
          `${reservation.amount}, stays counted in ${this.#path}: ${describeError(error, undefined)}`,
      );
      return { spent: reservation.amount, left: this.#leftAfter(reservation.total) };
    }
  }

  #leftAfter(total: bigint): bigint {
    return total < this.cap ? this.cap - total : 0n;
  }
}

/**
 * The total once a payment that reserved `reserved` and spent `spent` is settled, from the total
 * `current` read after its answer: `current − reserved + spent`, which is the total before the
 * payment plus its spend when nothing else wrote the file, and keeps what another writer added; but
 * never below `spent`, since a total cleared while the payment was in flight no longer holds its
 * reservation, and then counts only this payment's spend.
 */
function settledTotal(current: bigint, reserved: bigint, spent: bigint): bigint {
  const total = current - reserved + spent;
  return total > spent ? total : spent;
}

/** The part of a payment of `amount` that `answer` spent (see SpendLedger.pay). */
function spentBy(answer: BuyerPaymentAnswer, amount: bigint, seatPrice: bigint): bigint {
  switch (answer.kind) {
    case 'pending':
    case 'filled': {
      const taken = BigInt(answer.seats) * seatPrice;
      return taken < amount ? taken : amount;
    }
    case 'relay_failed':
    case 'result_unknown':
      return amount;
    case 'declined':
    case 'refused':
    case 'unavailable':
    case 'unknown_pool':
    case 'no_seats_taken':
    case 'pool_expired':
      return 0n;
  }
}
```

`apps/mcp/src/token.ts`:

```typescript
import type { Provider } from 'near-api-js';

/** How the token's amounts are written for people: its decimals and its symbol, from its NEP-148 ft_metadata. */
export interface TokenUnits {
  decimals: number;
  symbol: string;
}

/** The token's ft_metadata cannot be used to write its amounts. The message never quotes the metadata. */
export class TokenMetadataError extends Error {
  override name = 'TokenMetadataError';
}

/** A symbol that reads as one word: letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, up to 16 of them. */
const SYMBOL = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,16}$/;
/** NEP-148 decimals are a u8. */
const MAX_DECIMALS = 255;

/**
 * `amount` base units in whole tokens, with every decimal: 180 at 6 decimals is `0.000180`. Throws
 * RangeError for a negative amount.
 */
export function formatUnits(amount: bigint, decimals: number): string {
  if (amount < 0n) throw new RangeError(`not an amount: ${amount}`);
  if (decimals === 0) return amount.toString();
  const digits = amount.toString().padStart(decimals + 1, '0');
  return `${digits.slice(0, -decimals)}.${digits.slice(-decimals)}`;
}

/**
 * The decimals and the symbol of an ft_metadata result. Throws TokenMetadataError unless the decimals
 * are an integer from 0 to 255 and the symbol is 1 to 16 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`; a symbol is
 * shown to the agent next to every amount, so it is never free text.
 */
export function tokenUnits(metadata: unknown): TokenUnits {
  if (typeof metadata !== 'object' || metadata === null) throw new TokenMetadataError('ft_metadata is not an object');
  const { decimals, symbol } = metadata as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof decimals !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(decimals) || decimals < 0 || decimals > MAX_DECIMALS) {
    throw new TokenMetadataError(`ft_metadata.decimals is not an integer from 0 to ${MAX_DECIMALS}`);
  }
  if (typeof symbol !== 'string' || !SYMBOL.test(symbol)) {
    throw new TokenMetadataError('ft_metadata.symbol is not 1 to 16 letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"');
  }
  return { decimals, symbol };
}

/** Reads the token's units from its `ft_metadata` view, at final finality (see tokenUnits). */
export async function readTokenUnits(provider: Pick<Provider, 'callFunction'>, token: string): Promise<TokenUnits> {
  const metadata = await provider.callFunction({
    contractId: token,
    method: 'ft_metadata',
    args: {},
    blockQuery: { finality: 'final' },
  });
  return tokenUnits(metadata);
}
```

### Task 14: The MCP server's tools and its stdio process

The server gives an agent four tools, all acting as the one configured buyer (section 7.5):

| Tool | Input | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `quorum_pools` | none | The gateway's open pools: for each, its id, the seller's terms, the seat price, `target`, the seats taken and left, the deadline (ISO 8601, milliseconds, and seconds left), the bonus and the least bonus per seat. This is the gateway's listing, not checked, and the description says so. At most the first 50 pools by id (`MAX_POOLS_LISTED`), with `omitted` counting the others |
| `quorum_offer` | `pool`, `seats` | The gateway's offer for that many seats (or fewer, when fewer are left or the pool caps seats per buyer), with the pool's facts read from the pools contract, never from the offer; `minRefundIfFails`, the least paid back if the pool fails: the seats offered times the seat price plus the least bonus per seat; whether `quorum_commit` would pay it now (`payable`, else a `refusal` with the first code `quorum_commit` would answer); and `spendCapLeft`. It signs nothing |
| `quorum_commit` | `pool`, `seats` | Asks for a fresh offer, never reusing one `quorum_offer` returned, checks it, then pays through the spend cap. Answers `pending` (the `202` receipt) or `filled` (the `200` credential, whose access is simulated), with `paid`, what the payment counts against the cap, and `spendCapLeft` |
| `quorum_status` | `pool` | Redeems with a fresh proof of the account, which pays nothing: `pending`; `filled` with the credential; a refund, `refunded`, `refund_pending` or `claimable`, with its amount, bonus share and transaction (null until the gateway has recorded one); or `no_seats`, an answer, not a failure |

`pool` is an integer of at least 0 and `seats` an integer from 1 to 1000 (`MAX_SEATS_PER_REQUEST`).
Amounts are `{base, display}` (Task 13). A pool's `terms` is free text written by its seller: the
server returns it as quoted data in its own field, and the tool descriptions and the server's
instructions say it is never an instruction. The instructions also name the account the server acts
for, the threshold rule, the refund floor, the order in which to use the tools and the spend cap, and
say to check a pool with `quorum_offer` before `quorum_commit`.

- **The chain check** (`src/offer-check.ts`). What an offer says of the pool is the gateway's word,
  and the gateway is the seller's. Before anything is signed, `quorum_offer` and `quorum_commit` read
  the pool with `get_pool` on the configured pools contract at optimistic finality, and refuse the
  offer with `offer_mismatch` unless its seat price, target, deadline, bonus, terms and least bonus
  per seat are the pool's on chain. Seats taken and status move between two reads, so they are never
  compared. The offer is refused with `pool_closed` if the pool is not Open on chain or has no seat
  left there. A pool the contract does not hold is `offer_mismatch`, and a failed read
  `chain_unavailable`; nothing is signed after either.
- **Holds** (`src/commits.ts`). After a `quorum_commit` whose payment result is unknown (the buyer's
  `PaymentUnknownError`, answered `payment_unknown`), or that the gateway answers `502 result_unknown`,
  the server holds that pool until it has read a final block above the payment's `max_block_height`
  plus 20 (`SETTLE_MARGIN_BLOCKS`), since the payment may land until then. Meanwhile `quorum_commit`
  for the pool answers `payment_unsettled` and signs nothing, and `quorum_offer` says it would not
  pay. The answer gives the wait in seconds at the configured block time, and says that a `no_seats`
  from `quorum_status` is final only after it. If the final height cannot be read while a pool is
  held, the answer is `chain_unavailable`. Holds are kept in memory and are lost on a restart
  (section 12).
- **One commit at a time.** `Commits.serial` runs one `quorum_commit` at a time, even when the client
  calls tools concurrently, so that each sees the hold the one before it left.
- **Refusal order.** `quorum_commit` refuses `payment_unsettled` first; then, on its fresh offer,
  `offer_mismatch` or `pool_closed`; then `over_spend_cap`; then the buyer's own checks of section 6.3
  (`checkOffer`). `quorum_offer` makes the same checks in the same order.
- **Failures** (`src/server.ts`). Every failure is an MCP `isError` result whose text is JSON
  `{error, message}`. The codes are the server's own (`over_spend_cap`, `offer_mismatch`,
  `pool_closed`, `payment_unsettled`, `payment_not_sent`, `payment_unknown`, `chain_unavailable`,
  `gateway_unavailable`, `request_failed`), the gateway's (`unknown_pool`, `pool_expired`,
  `no_seats_taken`, `relay_failed`, `result_unknown`, and each `402` and `401` code), and the buyer's
  own refusals. A failure whose price stays counted says so, names the transaction when there is one,
  and points to `quorum_status`. An error a tool throws, such as an unreachable gateway or an answer
  the gateway does not document, becomes `request_failed`, in fixed words of the server's own with at
  most an HTTP status or a socket code (`transportReason`); for `quorum_commit` those words say that a
  payment may have been sent, and to call `quorum_status` before committing again. Only input that
  fails its schema gets the MCP SDK's own text. No text the agent receives holds a library's or the
  RPC's message: the operator's log, on standard error, gets the full error (`describeError`), with
  the RPC URL written as `QUORUM_RPC_URL`.
- **Schemas** (`src/schemas.ts`). Every input and output has a zod schema, which the SDK advertises as
  JSON Schema and checks each result against; each result carries its output both as structured
  content and as JSON text, for clients that read only text.
- **The process** (`src/main.ts`, the `start` script). `node apps/mcp/src/main.ts` (at the
  repository's root, or by its absolute path from any folder) loads `apps/mcp/.env`, next to itself,
  whatever the current folder, when it exists (a variable already set in the environment wins), and
  reads the configuration, exiting 1 with every problem on standard error if
  it is invalid. At startup it checks that the RPC serves the configured network (`checkChainId`),
  reads the token's `ft_metadata`, the buyer's key file (`<QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR>/testnet/<account>.json`,
  `sandbox/` on a local chain) and the spend total, and exits 1 with a message naming what failed if
  any of them does. It then serves the tools over stdio and writes one line on standard error naming
  the buyer, the gateway and what the spend cap leaves.
- **Standard output carries only the MCP stream.** Every message the process writes goes to standard
  error. `test/stdout.test.ts` scans `apps/mcp/src`, `packages/buyer/src` and `packages/protocol/src`
  for any use of `process.stdout` or of a console method that prints to standard output. It passes
  before this task's sources exist, since the folders it scans already do, and keeps the rule for
  every later change.

**Connecting a client.** `apps/mcp/mcp.example.json` is an MCP client's entry for the server, named
`quorum-buyer`: the command `node` with the argument `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/apps/mcp/src/main.ts`.
The server needs no variable from the client, since it reads its own `.env`. Claude Code expands
`${VAR:-default}` in `.mcp.json` but sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` only in the server's own environment,
so the argument expands to `./apps/mcp/src/main.ts` and resolves only when Claude Code is started at
this repository's root. There are two ways to add it:
- from another project: copy the `quorum-buyer` entry into that project's `.mcp.json` (inside its
  `mcpServers` object), and replace `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` with the absolute path of this
  repository; as it stands, the argument resolves only when the project is this repository;
- in this repository: leave its committed `.mcp.json` as it is, and add the same command in your own
  local scope, from the repository's root: `claude mcp add --scope local quorum-buyer -- node "$PWD/apps/mcp/src/main.ts"`.

Either way, `/mcp` in Claude Code then lists `quorum-buyer` with its four tools. Task 17 does this
against testnet. `test/main.test.ts` starts the command of `mcp.example.json`, with the repository as
the project folder, to check that it reaches `main.ts`.

`test/fixtures.ts` is final here: it gains `toolDeps(spendFile, answers?)`, which returns the tools'
dependencies over a stubbed buyer, gateway and chain and a real `SpendLedger` on a temporary spend
file, with the `Answers` it is given, the `Calls` it records and the log lines it collects.
`package.json` gains the `start` script; `test:sandbox` comes in Task 15.

`apps/mcp/test/fixtures.ts`:

```typescript
import type {
  BuyerPaymentAnswer,
  OfferAnswer,
  PaymentAnswer,
  PaymentRequest,
  PoolListing,
  PoolsAnswer,
  RedeemAnswer,
  SignedPayment,
} from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { buildOffer, type Offer, type OfferContext, type PoolView } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { baseEncode } from 'near-api-js';
import { Commits } from '../src/commits.ts';
import { SpendLedger } from '../src/spend.ts';
import type { ToolDeps } from '../src/tools.ts';

/** The accounts, the pool, the gateway answers and the stubbed buyer the MCP tests share. */

export const PARENT = 'parent.testnet';
export const BUYER = `buyer-llm.${PARENT}`;
export const POOLS = `pools.${PARENT}`;
export const TOKEN = 'usdc.testnet';
export const POOL_ID = 7;
/** 2027-01-15T08:00:00.000Z. */
export const DEADLINE_MS = 1_800_000_000_000;
export const TERMS = '8×GPU × 24 h; 1 seat = 1 GPU-hour; prices at 1/10,000 scale';

/** A pool of the gateway's provider: 180 per seat, 148 of 192 seats taken, a bonus of 1728, at most 24 per buyer. */
export const POOL: PoolView = {
  id: POOL_ID,
  seller: `provider.${PARENT}`,
  seat_price: '180',
  target: 192,
  taken: 148,
  deadline_ms: DEADLINE_MS,
  bonus: '1728',
  max_seats_per_buyer: 24,
  terms: TERMS,
  status: 'open',
  bonus_per_seat: '0',
  refund_cursor: 0,
  dust_sent: false,
  buyer_count: 30,
};

/** POOL as GatewayClient lists it: the least bonus per seat is floor(1728 / 191) = 9. */
export const LISTING: PoolListing = {
  id: POOL_ID,
  terms: TERMS,
  seat_price: 180n,
  target: 192,
  taken: 148,
  deadline_ms: DEADLINE_MS,
  bonus: 1728n,
  min_bonus_per_seat: 9n,
};

/** What the stubbed gateway is configured with. */
export const CONTEXT: OfferContext = {
  network: 'near:testnet',
  gatewayUrl: 'http://localhost:8402',
  poolsContract: POOLS,
  token: TOKEN,
  relayer: `relay.${PARENT}`,
  minGas: 50_000_000_000_000n,
  maxGas: 100_000_000_000_000n,
  maxTimeoutSeconds: 120,
};

/** The gateway's offer for `seats` seats of `pool`, built as the gateway builds it. */
export function offerFor(seats: number, pool: PoolView = POOL, context: OfferContext = CONTEXT): Offer {
  return buildOffer(pool, seats, context);
}

/** A transaction hash: base58 of 32 bytes. */
export const TX_HASH = baseEncode(new Uint8Array(32).fill(7));

/** A compact JWS, as the gateway's credentials are. */
export const CREDENTIAL = 'eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJidXllci1sbG0ifQ.c2lnbmF0dXJl';

/** What the stubbed buyer signed for each payment: 120 blocks of expiry past the final height. */
export const SIGNED: SignedPayment = { nonce: 1_001n, finalHeight: 245_000_100n, maxBlockHeight: 245_000_220n };

/** The gateway's `answer` as Buyer.pay returns it, with the payment it answers. */
export function signed(answer: PaymentAnswer): BuyerPaymentAnswer {
  return { ...answer, signed: SIGNED };
}

/** The 202 answer to a payment that took `seats` seats of POOL. */
export function pending(seats: number): BuyerPaymentAnswer {
  return signed({
    kind: 'pending',
    txHash: TX_HASH,
    poolId: POOL_ID,
    buyer: BUYER,
    seats,
    taken: 148 + seats,
    target: 192,
    deadlineMs: DEADLINE_MS,
  });
}

/** The 200 answer to a payment that filled POOL, the buyer then holding `seats` seats. */
export function filled(seats: number): BuyerPaymentAnswer {
  return signed({ kind: 'filled', txHash: TX_HASH, credential: CREDENTIAL, poolId: POOL_ID, seats, terms: TERMS });
}

/** 90.5 seconds before the pool's deadline. */
export const NOW_MS = DEADLINE_MS - 90_500;
export const CAP = 10_000n;

/** The RPC URL the tools are configured with: it carries an API key, so no text may quote it. */
export const RPC_URL = 'https://rpc.example.org/?apiKey=TEST-RPC-KEY';

/** The stubbed gateway's answers; each defaults to the happy path for POOL, and an Error is thrown. */
export interface Answers {
  pools?: PoolsAnswer | Error;
  /** Defaults to the offer for the seats requested. */
  offer?: OfferAnswer | Error;
  /** Defaults to a 202 for every seat of the offer. */
  pay?: BuyerPaymentAnswer | Error;
  /** Runs while the payment is in flight, before its answer. */
  duringPay?: () => Promise<void>;
  redeem?: RedeemAnswer | Error;
  /** The latest final height, read at each call; SIGNED's final height by default. */
  finalHeight?: () => bigint;
  /** The pool's view on chain, for any pool id; POOL with that id by default. */
  pool?: PoolView | null | Error;
}

/** What the stubbed buyer and gateway were asked. */
export interface Calls {
  pools: number;
  offer: [pool: number, seats: number][];
  pay: [offer: Offer, request: PaymentRequest][];
  redeem: number[];
  finalHeight: number;
  getPool: number[];
}

/** `answer`, or a throw when it is an Error. */
function answerOrThrow<T>(answer: T | Error): T {
  if (answer instanceof Error) throw answer;
  return answer;
}

/**
 * The tools' dependencies: a buyer and a gateway stubbed with `answers`, and a real spend ledger over
 * the file at `spendFile` with a cap of CAP, at the time NOW_MS, writing amounts as USDC does. `logs`
 * holds every line written to the operator's log.
 */
export function toolDeps(spendFile: string, answers: Answers = {}): { deps: ToolDeps; calls: Calls; logs: string[] } {
  const calls: Calls = { pools: 0, offer: [], pay: [], redeem: [], finalHeight: 0, getPool: [] };
  const logs: string[] = [];
  const deps: ToolDeps = {
    buyer: {
      accountId: BUYER,
      async offer(pool, seats) {
        calls.offer.push([pool, seats]);
        return answerOrThrow(answers.offer ?? { kind: 'offer', offer: offerFor(seats) });
      },
      async pay(offer, request) {
        calls.pay.push([offer, request]);
        await answers.duringPay?.();
        return answerOrThrow(answers.pay ?? pending(offer.extra.seats));
      },
      async redeem(pool) {
        calls.redeem.push(pool);
        return answerOrThrow(answers.redeem ?? { kind: 'no_seats' });
      },
      async finalHeight() {
        calls.finalHeight += 1;
        return answers.finalHeight?.() ?? SIGNED.finalHeight;
      },
    },
    gateway: {
      async pools() {
        calls.pools += 1;
        return answerOrThrow(answers.pools ?? { kind: 'pools', pools: [LISTING] });
      },
    },
    chain: {
      async getPool(id) {
        calls.getPool.push(id);
        return answerOrThrow(answers.pool === undefined ? { ...POOL, id } : answers.pool);
      },
    },
    ledger: new SpendLedger({ path: spendFile, account: BUYER, cap: CAP, log: (line) => logs.push(line) }),
    settings: { network: 'near:testnet', token: TOKEN, poolsContract: POOLS, rpcUrl: RPC_URL, blockTimeMs: 1000 },
    units: { decimals: 6, symbol: 'USDC' },
    now: () => NOW_MS,
    log: (line) => logs.push(line),
    commits: new Commits(),
  };
  return { deps, calls, logs };
}
```

```typescript
import type { Offer, PoolView } from '@quorum-on-near/protocol';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { offerMismatch, poolRefusal } from '../src/offer-check.ts';
import { offerFor, POOL } from './fixtures.ts';

/** The offer for 2 seats of POOL, with `extra` changed by `change`. */
function offerWith(change: Partial<Offer['extra']>): Offer {
  const offer = offerFor(2);
  return { ...offer, extra: { ...offer.extra, ...change } };
}

describe('offerMismatch', () => {
  it('finds nothing in the offer the gateway builds from the pool it reads', () => {
    expect(offerMismatch(offerFor(2), POOL)).toBeNull();
  });

  it.each<[string, Partial<Offer['extra']>]>([
    ['seat price', { seatPrice: '181' }],
    ['target', { target: 191 }],
    ['deadline', { deadlineMs: POOL.deadline_ms + 1 }],
    ['bonus', { bonus: '1000000' }],
    ['terms', { terms: `${POOL.terms} ` }],
    // floor(1,728 / 191) = 9.
    ['minimum bonus per seat', { minBonusPerSeat: '5000' }],
  ])("names the %s when the offer's differs from the chain's", (field, change) => {
    expect(offerMismatch(offerWith(change), POOL)).toBe(`the offer's ${field} is not the pool's on chain`);
  });

  it('names the first fact that differs, in the order seat price, target, deadline, bonus, terms', () => {
    expect(offerMismatch(offerWith({ bonus: '1', terms: 'other' }), POOL)).toBe("the offer's bonus is not the pool's on chain");
  });

  it.each<[string, Partial<PoolView>]>([
    ['taken', { taken: 191 }],
    ['status', { status: 'filled' }],
    ['the buyer count', { buyer_count: 31 }],
  ])('never compares what moves after the pool opened: %s', (_, change) => {
    expect(offerMismatch(offerFor(2), { ...POOL, ...change })).toBeNull();
  });

  it('compares amounts by value, and refuses one that is not a decimal amount', () => {
    const offer = offerWith({ seatPrice: 'one hundred' });
    expect(offerMismatch(offer, POOL)).toBe("the offer's seat price is not the pool's on chain");
  });

  it('never throws for an offer without its pool facts', () => {
    const offer = { ...offerFor(2), extra: null } as unknown as Offer;
    expect(offerMismatch(offer, POOL)).toBe('the offer carries no pool facts');
  });
});

describe('poolRefusal', () => {
  it('refuses nothing for an open pool with seats left whose facts the offer states', () => {
    expect(poolRefusal(offerFor(2), POOL)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('refuses an offer that misstates the pool as offer_mismatch, before anything else', () => {
    expect(poolRefusal(offerWith({ bonus: '1' }), { ...POOL, status: 'filled' })).toEqual({
      code: 'offer_mismatch',
      detail: "the offer's bonus is not the pool's on chain",
    });
  });

  it.each<[PoolView['status']]>([['filled'], ['settled'], ['expired'], ['refunded']])(
    'refuses a pool that is %s on chain as pool_closed',
    (status) => {
      const refusal = { code: 'pool_closed', detail: `pool 7 is ${status} on chain` };
      expect(poolRefusal(offerFor(2), { ...POOL, status })).toEqual(refusal);
    },
  );

  it('refuses an open pool with no seat left on chain as pool_closed', () => {
    expect(poolRefusal(offerFor(2), { ...POOL, taken: 192 })).toEqual({
      code: 'pool_closed',
      detail: 'pool 7 has no seat left on chain',
    });
  });
});
```
