`apps/swarm/test/sandbox/teardown.ts`:

```typescript
// Stops a near-sandbox Sandbox within a bounded time and leaves nothing of it behind. near-sandbox
// 0.3.5's tearDown() sends neard SIGTERM and waits for its exit with no time limit, and a neard that
// has run for a while can catch SIGTERM and go on producing blocks; a neard that exited earlier
// never sends the exit event tearDown waits for. tearDown also leaves, in the system's temporary
// folder, the two empty port lock files it created, once it has released the locks.
import type { ChildProcess } from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { rm } from 'node:fs/promises';

/** What stopSandbox uses of a near-sandbox Sandbox. */
export interface SandboxToStop {
  readonly homeDir: string;
  readonly rpcPortLockPath: string;
  readonly netPortLockPath: string;
  tearDown(): Promise<void>;
}

/** What stopSandbox uses of the sandbox's neard process. */
export type NeardProcess = Pick<ChildProcess, 'exitCode' | 'signalCode' | 'kill'>;

export interface StopSandboxOptions {
  /** How long tearDown gets, from its SIGTERM, before neard is killed; SANDBOX_GRACE_MS by default. */
  graceMs?: number;
  /** How long tearDown then gets to release the ports once neard is killed; SANDBOX_KILL_WAIT_MS by default. */
  killWaitMs?: number;
}

/** How stopSandbox stopped a sandbox. */
export interface SandboxStopped {
  /** neard was still running when the grace period ended, and was sent SIGKILL. */
  killed: boolean;
  /** tearDown ended, so the port locks are released; false when it was still waiting for neard's exit. */
  tornDown: boolean;
}

/** A neard that stops on SIGTERM does so in well under a second. */
export const SANDBOX_GRACE_MS = 10_000;
/** After SIGKILL, tearDown only releases two locks and removes the home folder. */
export const SANDBOX_KILL_WAIT_MS = 10_000;

/**
 * Tears `sandbox` down and gives it `graceMs`. If tearDown has not ended by then, sends neard SIGKILL
 * (unless it has already exited) and gives tearDown `killWaitMs` more: neard's exit lets it release
 * the port locks and remove the home folder. Then removes the home folder (again, when tearDown did)
 * and each port lock file whose lock is released. A lock still held stays: proper-lockfile, which
 * near-sandbox locks the ports with, holds a lock as a `<file>.lock` folder that it keeps fresh and
 * reports as compromised (by throwing) once it is removed, and it removes the folder itself when the
 * process exits. A held lock is this process's when tearDown never ended, or another sandbox's that
 * took the same port since. Resolves in at most `graceMs + killWaitMs` plus the removals; rejects only
 * when the home folder cannot be removed.
 */
export async function stopSandbox(
  sandbox: SandboxToStop,
  neard: NeardProcess,
  options: StopSandboxOptions = {},
): Promise<SandboxStopped> {
  const { graceMs = SANDBOX_GRACE_MS, killWaitMs = SANDBOX_KILL_WAIT_MS } = options;
  // tearDown's only failure is removing the home folder, which is done again below.
  const tearDown = sandbox.tearDown().then(
    () => true,
    () => true,
  );
  let tornDown = await settledWithin(tearDown, graceMs);
  let killed = false;
  if (!tornDown) {
    if (neard.exitCode === null && neard.signalCode === null) killed = neard.kill('SIGKILL');
    tornDown = await settledWithin(tearDown, killWaitMs);
  }
  await rm(sandbox.homeDir, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 3 });
  for (const lockFile of [sandbox.rpcPortLockPath, sandbox.netPortLockPath]) {
    if (!existsSync(`${lockFile}.lock`)) await rm(lockFile, { force: true });
  }
  return { killed, tornDown };
}

/** Resolves with what `promise` resolves with, or false once `ms` have passed. */
async function settledWithin(promise: Promise<boolean>, ms: number): Promise<boolean> {
  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
  const timeout = new Promise<false>((resolve) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), ms);
  });
  try {
    return await Promise.race([promise, timeout]);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}
```

```typescript
// A whole local system for the sandbox tests: a NEAR sandbox holding the mock token, every account
// of the swarm prepared by runSetup, and the real gateway running as a child process. Needs Linux or
// macOS (near-sandbox ships no Windows binary) and the wasm files from `cargo near build`, named by
// QUORUM_POOLS_WASM and QUORUM_MOCK_USD_WASM. Everything it writes (key files, the spend file, the
// gateway's data and logs) goes to one temporary folder, which stop() removes; nothing is written
// into the repository. The sandbox keeps about 15 minutes of history (SANDBOX_GC_EPOCHS), and stop()
// ends it within a bounded time (stopSandbox).
import { ChildProcess, spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { closeSync, openSync } from 'node:fs';
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { createServer } from 'node:net';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util';
import {
  GatewayClient,
  keyFilePath,
  keyFolderPath,
  readKeyFolder,
  RpcBuyerChain,
  writeKeyFile,
  type Env,
} from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { Account, actions, JsonRpcProvider, KeyPair, KeyPairSigner, teraToGas, type KeyPairString } from 'near-api-js';
import { DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID, DEFAULT_PRIVATE_KEY, Sandbox } from 'near-sandbox';
import type {
  AccountKey,
  AccountState,
  BlockInfo,
  NewAccount,
  ReadAt,
  SwarmChain,
  TokenTransfer,
  TransferCall,
  TransferCallResult,
  TxOutcome,
} from '../../src/chain.ts';
import { loadSwarmConfig, type SwarmConfig } from '../../src/config.ts';
import { gatewayEnvText, mcpEnvText, newCredentialJwk } from '../../src/env-files.ts';
import { createRpcSwarmChain } from '../../src/rpc-chain.ts';
import { runSetup, type SetupReport } from '../../src/setup.ts';
import { stopSandbox } from './teardown.ts';

/** The repository's root folder, the working folder of the child processes. */
const REPO_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../', import.meta.url));
const SWARM_MAIN = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../src/main.ts', import.meta.url));
const GATEWAY_MAIN = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../gateway/src/main.ts', import.meta.url));
const WEB_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../web/', import.meta.url));

/**
 * The mock token minted to the funding account between the two setup runs, in base units: 10 mUSD.
 * A first setup's top-ups take 220,000 (21 buyers and the provider at 10,000 each); the rest covers
 * the top-ups of every later setup in a test run. One `mint` call creates at most 1,000 mUSD.
 */
export const DEFAULT_MINT = 10_000_000n;

/**
 * The deadline every scenario gets, in seconds, unless a test sets QUORUM_SCENARIO_DEADLINE_SECONDS.
 * The sandbox makes a block about every 125 ms and the gateway relays a commit in under a second, so
 * even when all 14 buyers that accept `fills` arrive at once, its 4 relayer keys have answered them
 * all within about 3 s. 30 s covers the spread, those 3 s and a buyer's retries (2 s, then 4 s) more
 * than twice over, on a slower machine too. A pool that fills settles at once, so only a pool that
 * fails waits for its deadline.
 */
const SANDBOX_DEADLINE_SECONDS = '30';
/**
 * The arrival spread every scenario gets, in seconds, unless a test sets QUORUM_SWARM_SPREAD_SECONDS:
 * long enough that the buyers arrive one after another, as they would over the scenarios' own spread.
 */
const SANDBOX_SPREAD_SECONDS = '5';
/** How often a scripted buyer polls its redemption: 1 s, since sandbox blocks come faster than testnet's. */
const SANDBOX_REDEEM_INTERVAL_MS = '1000';
/**
 * How many epochs of blocks, transactions and state the sandbox keeps: neard's gc_num_epochs_to_keep,
 * 5 by default. A sandbox epoch is 60 blocks of about 125 ms, 7.5 s, so the default keeps about 37 s,
 * and the RPC knows no older transaction: `swarm check` could not measure a run that lasts longer.
 * 120 epochs keep about 15 minutes.
 */
export const SANDBOX_GC_EPOCHS = 120;

/** NEAR given to the mock token's account: its code locks about 1.5 NEAR, and each registration pays its own storage. */
const TOKEN_NEAR = 5_000_000_000_000_000_000_000_000n;
const INIT_GAS = teraToGas(30);
const MINT_GAS = teraToGas(20);
/** How long the gateway gets to answer its first request once started. */
const GATEWAY_START_MS = 30_000;
/** How long a stopped gateway gets to finish its running work before it is killed. */
const GATEWAY_STOP_MS = 15_000;

/** What startSwarmWorld can be asked to do differently. */
export interface SwarmWorldOptions {
  /**
   * Serve apps/web at the gateway's `/` and turn its RPC pass-through on, as a browser looking at the
   * live page needs. Off by default: QUORUM_WEB_DIR is empty and the pass-through off.
   */
  page?: boolean;
  /** Swarm variables set over the world's own, such as QUORUM_SCENARIO_DEADLINE_SECONDS. */
  swarmEnv?: Env;
  /** Gateway variables set over those its env file holds, such as QUORUM_KEEPER_INTERVAL_MS. */
  gatewayEnv?: Env;
  /** The mock token minted to the funding account between the two setup runs; DEFAULT_MINT by default. */
  mint?: bigint;
}

/** One write a CountingChain passed on: the SwarmChain method and the account that signed it. */
export interface WriteRecord {
  method: 'createAccount' | 'transferNear' | 'deployPools' | 'storageDeposits' | 'ftTransfers' | 'ftTransferCall';
  signer: string;
}

/** What one recordSetup run did. */
export interface SetupRun {
  /** The lines runSetup logged, in order. */
  lines: string[];
  /** What runSetup returned; null when it threw. */
  report: SetupReport | null;
  /** What runSetup threw; null when it returned. */
  error: unknown;
  /** The writes it sent through the chain, failed ones included. */
  writes: number;
  /** The parent's NEAR balance before and after the run, at the latest final block, in yoctoNEAR. */
  parentBefore: bigint;
  parentAfter: bigint;
  /** How long the run took, in milliseconds. */
  ms: number;
}

/** The gateway running as a child process. */
export interface GatewayProcess {
  /** Its base URL, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`: QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL for it and for every buyer. */
  url: string;
  port: number;
  /** The files its standard output and standard error go to, inside the world's temporary folder. */
  stdoutPath: string;
  stderrPath: string;
}

/** A running world, as startSwarmWorld returns it. */
export interface SwarmWorld {
  sandbox: Sandbox;
  /**
   * The swarm's variables in this world: the sandbox network and RPC, the sandbox's root account as
   * the parent, the mock token, the gateway's URL, QUORUM_POOLS_WASM, the temporary key folder and
   * spend file, a shortened deadline, spread and redemption interval, and the options' swarmEnv. It
   * holds paths and account ids, no key. Spawn the real command line with it (runSwarmCli).
   */
  swarmEnv: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  /** loadSwarmConfig(swarmEnv). */
  config: SwarmConfig;
  /** The swarm's RPC chain, counting the writes sent through it. */
  chain: CountingChain;
  /** A client of the running gateway. */
  gatewayClient: GatewayClient;
  /** The chain reads a buyer signs its payments with, on the sandbox's RPC. */
  buyerChain: RpcBuyerChain;
  /** The two setup runs of the start: the first stops on the token shortfall, the second completes. */
  setupRuns: readonly [SetupRun, SetupRun];
  /** What was minted to the funding account between them, in base units. */
  minted: bigint;
  gateway: GatewayProcess;
  /**
   * The MCP server's variables for the buyer `buyer-llm.<root>`, as `swarm env mcp` writes them
   * (mcpEnvText, parsed): no key, the server reads its buyer's key file in the temporary key folder.
   */
  mcpEnv: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  /** How long each step of the start took, in order, in milliseconds. */
  timings: ReadonlyArray<{ step: string; ms: number }>;
  /**
   * Stops the gateway, stops the sandbox with stopSandbox (killing neard if it has not stopped within
   * SANDBOX_GRACE_MS) and removes the temporary folder. Runs once; later calls wait for it.
   */
  stop(): Promise<void>;
}

/** How a child process ended, with everything it printed. */
export interface ProcessResult {
  /** Its exit code; null when a signal ended it. */
  code: number | null;
  signal: NodeJS.Signals | null;
  stdout: string;
  stderr: string;
}

/**
 * A SwarmChain that passes every call on to another one and records each write before passing it on,
 * so that a test can assert that a command sent nothing.
 */
export class CountingChain implements SwarmChain {
  readonly #inner: SwarmChain;
  readonly #writes: WriteRecord[] = [];

  constructor(inner: SwarmChain) {
    this.#inner = inner;
  }

  /** Every write passed on so far, in order; one that then failed is counted. */
  get writes(): readonly WriteRecord[] {
    return this.#writes;
  }

  chainId(): Promise<string> {
    return this.#inner.chainId();
  }

  account(accountId: string): Promise<AccountState | null> {
    return this.#inner.account(accountId);
  }

  getToken(): Promise<string> {
    return this.#inner.getToken();
  }

  registrationDeposit(): Promise<bigint> {
    return this.#inner.registrationDeposit();
  }

  isRegistered(accountId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.#inner.isRegistered(accountId);
  }

  ftBalanceOf(accountId: string, atHeight?: bigint): Promise<bigint> {
    return this.#inner.ftBalanceOf(accountId, atHeight);
  }

  getPool(poolId: number): ReturnType<SwarmChain['getPool']> {
    return this.#inner.getPool(poolId);
  }

  listPools(from: number, limit: number, at?: ReadAt): ReturnType<SwarmChain['listPools']> {
    return this.#inner.listPools(from, limit, at);
  }

  getSeats(poolId: number, from: number, limit: number, atHeight?: bigint): ReturnType<SwarmChain['getSeats']> {
    return this.#inner.getSeats(poolId, from, limit, atHeight);
  }

  finalBlock(): Promise<BlockInfo> {
    return this.#inner.finalBlock();
  }

  txOutcome(txHash: string, signerId: string): Promise<TxOutcome | null> {
    return this.#inner.txOutcome(txHash, signerId);
  }

  createAccount(signer: AccountKey, account: NewAccount): Promise<TxOutcome> {
    this.#count('createAccount', signer);
    return this.#inner.createAccount(signer, account);
  }

  transferNear(signer: AccountKey, receiverId: string, amount: bigint): Promise<TxOutcome> {
    this.#count('transferNear', signer);
    return this.#inner.transferNear(signer, receiverId, amount);
  }

  deployPools(signer: AccountKey, code: Uint8Array): Promise<TxOutcome> {
    this.#count('deployPools', signer);
    return this.#inner.deployPools(signer, code);
  }

  storageDeposits(signer: AccountKey, accountIds: readonly string[], deposit: bigint): Promise<TxOutcome> {
    this.#count('storageDeposits', signer);
    return this.#inner.storageDeposits(signer, accountIds, deposit);
  }

  ftTransfers(signer: AccountKey, transfers: readonly TokenTransfer[]): Promise<TxOutcome> {
    this.#count('ftTransfers', signer);
    return this.#inner.ftTransfers(signer, transfers);
  }

  ftTransferCall(signer: AccountKey, call: TransferCall): Promise<TransferCallResult> {
    this.#count('ftTransferCall', signer);
    return this.#inner.ftTransferCall(signer, call);
  }

  #count(method: WriteRecord['method'], signer: AccountKey): void {
    this.#writes.push({ method, signer: signer.accountId });
  }
}

/** The wasm files QUORUM_POOLS_WASM and QUORUM_MOCK_USD_WASM name. Throws, naming both, unless both are set. */
export function wasmFromEnv(): { pools: string; mockUsd: string } {
  const { QUORUM_POOLS_WASM: pools, QUORUM_MOCK_USD_WASM: mockUsd } = process.env;
  if (!pools || !mockUsd) {
    throw new Error(
      'set QUORUM_POOLS_WASM and QUORUM_MOCK_USD_WASM to the absolute paths of the pools and mock-usd wasm files that `cargo near build` writes',
    );
  }
  return { pools, mockUsd };
}

/**
 * Stands up a whole world, up to a running gateway:
 * 1. starts a sandbox and deploys the mock token, initialised, at `musd.<root>`;
 * 2. writes the root account's key file into a temporary key folder: the root is the swarm's parent;
 * 3. builds the swarm's configuration (see SwarmWorld.swarmEnv);
 * 4. runs setup, which stops on the token shortfall once it has created and registered every
 *    account; mints `options.mint` to the funding account, as a faucet would; runs setup again;
 * 5. starts the gateway (`node apps/gateway/src/main.ts`) with the variables `swarm env gateway`
 *    writes (gatewayEnvText, never written to a file), on a free port, with a temporary data folder,
 *    and waits until it answers `GET /pools`.
 * The QUORUM_* variables of this process are not passed on: the world's own are. Throws if a step
 * fails, the second setup included, after stopping whatever it had started.
 */
export async function startSwarmWorld(options: SwarmWorldOptions = {}): Promise<SwarmWorld> {
  const wasm = wasmFromEnv();
  const timings: Array<{ step: string; ms: number }> = [];
  const timed = async <T>(step: string, work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> => {
    const start = performance.now();
    const result = await work();
    timings.push({ step, ms: Math.round(performance.now() - start) });
    return result;
  };

  const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'quorum-swarm-sandbox-'));
  let sandbox: Sandbox | undefined;
  let gatewayChild: ChildProcess | undefined;
  const stopAll = async (): Promise<void> => {
    try {
      if (gatewayChild !== undefined) await stopChild(gatewayChild);
    } finally {
      try {
        if (sandbox !== undefined) {
          const { killed } = await stopSandbox(sandbox, neardProcess(sandbox));
          if (killed) console.log('the sandbox did not stop on SIGTERM: neard was killed');
        }
      } finally {
        await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
      }
    }
  };

  try {
    const credentialsDir = join(root, 'keys');
    const gatewayData = join(root, 'gateway-data');
    await mkdir(gatewayData);
    const port = await freePort();
    const gatewayUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;

    const started = await timed('start the sandbox', startSandbox);
    sandbox = started;
    const provider = new JsonRpcProvider({ url: started.rpcUrl });
    const rootAccount = new Account(DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID, provider, DEFAULT_PRIVATE_KEY);
    const rootKey = KeyPair.fromString(DEFAULT_PRIVATE_KEY as KeyPairString);
    await writeKeyFile(keyFilePath(credentialsDir, 'near:sandbox', DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID), DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID, rootKey);
    const token = await timed('deploy the mock token', () => deployToken(rootAccount, wasm.mockUsd));

    const swarmEnv: Record<string, string> = {
      QUORUM_NETWORK: 'near:sandbox',
      QUORUM_RPC_URL: started.rpcUrl,
      QUORUM_GATEWAY_URL: gatewayUrl,
      QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID,
      QUORUM_TOKEN_ACCOUNT: token,
      QUORUM_POOLS_WASM: wasm.pools,
      QUORUM_CREDENTIALS_DIR: credentialsDir,
      QUORUM_MCP_SPEND_FILE: join(root, 'mcp-spend.json'),
      QUORUM_SCENARIO_DEADLINE_SECONDS: SANDBOX_DEADLINE_SECONDS,
      QUORUM_SWARM_SPREAD_SECONDS: SANDBOX_SPREAD_SECONDS,
      QUORUM_REDEEM_INTERVAL_MS: SANDBOX_REDEEM_INTERVAL_MS,
      ...definedOnly(options.swarmEnv),
    };
    const config = loadSwarmConfig(swarmEnv);
    const chain = new CountingChain(createRpcSwarmChain(config));

    const first = await timed('first setup', () => recordSetup(config, chain));
    const minted = options.mint ?? DEFAULT_MINT;
    await timed('mint to the funding account', () => mint(rootAccount, token, config.funding, minted));
    const second = await timed('second setup', () => recordSetup(config, chain));
    if (second.error !== null) {
      throw new Error(
        `the second setup failed; the first logged:\n${first.lines.join('\n')}\nand ended with: ${errorText(first.error)}`,
        { cause: second.error },
      );
    }

    const relayerKeys = await readKeyFolder(keyFolderPath(credentialsDir, config.network, config.relayer));
    const gatewayEnv: Record<string, string> = {
      ...definedOnly(parseEnv(gatewayEnvText(config, relayerKeys, newCredentialJwk()))),
      QUORUM_GATEWAY_PORT: String(port),
      QUORUM_DATA_DIR: gatewayData,
      QUORUM_WEB_DIR: options.page === true ? WEB_DIR : '',
      QUORUM_RPC_PASSTHROUGH: options.page === true ? 'true' : 'false',
      ...definedOnly(options.gatewayEnv),
    };
    const gateway: GatewayProcess = {
      url: gatewayUrl,
      port,
      stdoutPath: join(root, 'gateway.stdout.txt'),
      stderrPath: join(root, 'gateway.stderr.txt'),
    };
    await timed('start the gateway', async () => {
      gatewayChild = spawnLogged(GATEWAY_MAIN, [], childEnv(gatewayEnv), gateway);
      await untilAnswers(gatewayChild, gateway);
    });

    let stopping: Promise<void> | undefined;
    return {
      sandbox: started,
      swarmEnv,
      config,
      chain,
      gatewayClient: new GatewayClient({ gatewayUrl }),
      buyerChain: new RpcBuyerChain(new JsonRpcProvider({ url: started.rpcUrl })),
      setupRuns: [first, second],
      minted,
      gateway,
      mcpEnv: definedOnly(parseEnv(mcpEnvText(config))),
      timings,
      stop: () => (stopping ??= stopAll()),
    };
  } catch (error) {
    await stopAll();
    throw error;
  }
}

/** Starts a sandbox that keeps SANDBOX_GC_EPOCHS epochs of history. Stop it with stopSandbox. */
export async function startSandbox(): Promise<Sandbox> {
  return Sandbox.start({ config: { additionalConfig: { gc_num_epochs_to_keep: SANDBOX_GC_EPOCHS } } });
}

/** The neard process a sandbox runs, which near-sandbox keeps in a private field. */
export function neardProcess(sandbox: Sandbox): ChildProcess {
  const child: unknown = sandbox['childProcess'];
  if (!(child instanceof ChildProcess)) throw new TypeError('the sandbox keeps no neard process in childProcess');
  return child;
}

/**
 * Runs setup once through `chain` and records what it did: the lines it logged (also passed to
 * `log`, when given), what it returned or threw, the writes it sent, the parent's NEAR before and
 * after, and how long it took. Never throws for setup's own error: it is in `error`.
 */
export async function recordSetup(config: SwarmConfig, chain: CountingChain, log?: (line: string) => void): Promise<SetupRun> {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  const writesBefore = chain.writes.length;
  const parentBefore = await parentBalance(config, chain);
  const start = performance.now();
  let report: SetupReport | null = null;
  let error: unknown = null;
  try {
    report = await runSetup(config, {
      chain,
      log: (line) => {
        lines.push(line);
        log?.(line);
      },
    });
  } catch (thrown) {
    error = thrown;
  }
  const ms = Math.round(performance.now() - start);
  const parentAfter = await parentBalance(config, chain);
  return { lines, report, error, writes: chain.writes.length - writesBefore, parentBefore, parentAfter, ms };
}

/**
 * Runs the swarm's real command line, `node apps/swarm/src/main.ts <args>`, from the repository's
 * root, with the world's swarmEnv and then `env` as its only QUORUM_* variables. Resolves once it
 * exits, with what it printed; a run longer than `timeoutMs` is killed and resolves with its signal.
 */
export async function runSwarmCli(
  world: Pick<SwarmWorld, 'swarmEnv'>,
  args: readonly string[],
  options: { env?: Env; timeoutMs?: number } = {},
): Promise<ProcessResult> {
  const child = spawn(process.execPath, [SWARM_MAIN, ...args], {
    cwd: REPO_ROOT,
    env: childEnv({ ...world.swarmEnv, ...definedOnly(options.env) }),
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  });
  let stdout = '';
  let stderr = '';
  child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8').on('data', (chunk: string) => (stdout += chunk));
  child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8').on('data', (chunk: string) => (stderr += chunk));
  const timer = options.timeoutMs === undefined ? undefined : setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGKILL'), options.timeoutMs);
  try {
    const [code, signal] = await onceExited(child);
    return { code, signal, stdout, stderr };
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

/**
 * The environment of a child process: this process's variables except every QUORUM_* one, then
 * `vars`. A child configured this way reads only the variables it is given, whatever the shell that
 * started the tests exports.
 */
export function childEnv(vars: Env): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
  const env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(process.env)) {
    if (!name.startsWith('QUORUM_')) env[name] = value;
  }
  return { ...env, ...definedOnly(vars) };
}

/** Creates `musd.<root>`, deploys the mock token's code to it and initialises it, in one transaction after the creation. */
async function deployToken(root: Account, wasmFile: string): Promise<string> {
  const id = `musd.${root.accountId}`;
  const keyPair = KeyPair.fromRandom('ed25519');
  await root.signAndSendTransaction({
    receiverId: id,
    actions: [actions.createAccount(), actions.transfer(TOKEN_NEAR), actions.addFullAccessKey(keyPair.getPublicKey())],
    waitUntil: 'FINAL',
  });
  const token = new Account(id, root.provider, new KeyPairSigner(keyPair));
  await token.signAndSendTransaction({
    receiverId: id,
    actions: [actions.deployContract(await readFile(wasmFile)), actions.functionCall('new', {}, INIT_GAS, 0n)],
    waitUntil: 'FINAL',
  });
  return id;
}

/** Mints `amount` of the mock token to `accountId`, which must be registered on it, signed by the root. */
async function mint(root: Account, token: string, accountId: string, amount: bigint): Promise<void> {
  await root.signAndSendTransaction({
    receiverId: token,
    actions: [actions.functionCall('mint', { account_id: accountId, amount: amount.toString() }, MINT_GAS, 0n)],
    waitUntil: 'FINAL',
  });
}

async function parentBalance(config: SwarmConfig, chain: SwarmChain): Promise<bigint> {
  const state = await chain.account(config.parent);
  if (state === null) throw new Error(`the parent account ${config.parent} does not exist`);
  return state.balance;
}

/** A TCP port on 127.0.0.1 that was free a moment ago. */
async function freePort(): Promise<number> {
  const server = createServer();
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve);
  });
  const address = server.address();
  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve()));
  if (address === null || typeof address === 'string') throw new Error('the free port probe got no TCP address');
  return address.port;
}

/** Starts `node <script> <args>` from the repository's root, its output going to the gateway's log files. */
function spawnLogged(script: string, args: readonly string[], env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, logs: GatewayProcess): ChildProcess {
  const out = openSync(logs.stdoutPath, 'w');
  const err = openSync(logs.stderrPath, 'w');
  try {
    return spawn(process.execPath, [script, ...args], { cwd: REPO_ROOT, env, stdio: ['ignore', out, err] });
  } finally {
    // The child holds its own copies of the two descriptors.
    closeSync(out);
    closeSync(err);
  }
}

/**
 * Waits until the gateway answers `GET /pools` with 200, which it does once it has read the chain id
 * and the pools contract's token and listens. Throws, with what it wrote on standard error, if it
 * exits first or does not answer within GATEWAY_START_MS.
 */
async function untilAnswers(child: ChildProcess, gateway: GatewayProcess): Promise<void> {
  let exited = false;
  const exit = onceExited(child).then(() => {
    exited = true;
  });
  const giveUpAt = Date.now() + GATEWAY_START_MS;
  while (!exited && Date.now() < giveUpAt) {
    try {
      const response = await fetch(`${gateway.url}/pools`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2_000) });
      await response.body?.cancel();
      if (response.status === 200) return;
    } catch {
      // Not listening yet.
    }
    await Promise.race([exit, new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 200))]);
  }
  const stderr = await readFile(gateway.stderrPath, 'utf8');
  const why = exited ? `exited with code ${child.exitCode}` : `did not answer within ${GATEWAY_START_MS} ms`;
  throw new Error(`the gateway ${why}; its standard error:\n${stderr}`);
}

/** Asks a child to stop (SIGTERM), kills it if it is still running after GATEWAY_STOP_MS, and waits until it has exited. */
async function stopChild(child: ChildProcess): Promise<void> {
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) return;
  const exited = onceExited(child);
  child.kill('SIGTERM');
  const timer = setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGKILL'), GATEWAY_STOP_MS);
  try {
    await exited;
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

/** Resolves with `[code, signal]` once the child has exited, at once if it already has. */
function onceExited(child: ChildProcess): Promise<[number | null, NodeJS.Signals | null]> {
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) return Promise.resolve([child.exitCode, child.signalCode]);
  return new Promise((resolve) => child.once('exit', (code, signal) => resolve([code, signal])));
}

/** `vars` without its undefined values. */
function definedOnly(vars: Env | undefined): Record<string, string> {
  const result: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(vars ?? {})) {
    if (value !== undefined) result[name] = value;
  }
  return result;
}

function errorText(error: unknown): string {
  return error instanceof Error ? `${error.name}: ${error.message}` : String(error);
}
```

### Task 16: `swarm reset`

After the scenarios, the provider holds the `fills` pool's sales and the refunded buyers hold their
bonus shares. `swarm reset` returns those surpluses to the funding account (section 7.2), so that the
next setup tops nothing up for them and the funding account holds the rest. Repeat runs do not need
it: without a reset, setup keeps refilling the buyers from the funding account while the provider's
balance grows.

`runReset(config, { chain, log })` first checks the RPC's chain against `QUORUM_NETWORK`
(`checkChain`). Then, for the provider and each buyer in turn (`swarmAccounts`, those with a token
amount), it reads the account's token balance; an account above its configured amount
(`QUORUM_PROVIDER_BONUS_FUNDS`, `QUORUM_BUYER_BUDGET`) reads its own key file only then and sends its
whole surplus to the funding account in one `ft_transfer`, logging
`<account>  returned <amount> to <funding account>  tx <hash>`. An account at or below its amount
sends nothing and needs no key file, so a second reset in a row transfers nothing and logs
`nothing to do`. Reset moves balances only: it never calls `claim_refund`, and money still held by an
unresolved pool is not counted. It stops at the first error (a `KeyFileError` for a missing key file,
or the chain's): the transfers made before it stand, and after a transfer that got no result the
error says (`rerunAdvice`) that running reset again once that transaction is final sends only what
is still above the amounts. The command line gains `swarm reset`, which takes no argument and checks
the chain first like every other chain command. The swarm's sandbox suite gains the test that reset,
then setup, bring every buyer and the provider back to its amount, and that a second reset sends
nothing.

```typescript
    const returned = await reset();

    expect(chain.writes).toMatchObject([
      { kind: 'ftTransfers', signer: PROVIDER, transfers: [{ receiverId: FUNDING, amount: 540n }] },
      { kind: 'ftTransfers', signer: buyer(3), transfers: [{ receiverId: FUNDING, amount: 30n }] },
      { kind: 'ftTransfers', signer: LLM, transfers: [{ receiverId: FUNDING, amount: 200n }] },
    ]);
    const [provider, third, llm] = chain.writes.map((write) => write.txHash);
    expect(returned).toEqual([
      { accountId: PROVIDER, amount: 540n, txHash: provider },
      { accountId: buyer(3), amount: 30n, txHash: third },
      { accountId: LLM, amount: 200n, txHash: llm },
    ]);
    expect([PROVIDER, buyer(3), LLM, buyer(5)].map((id) => chain.tokenBalances.get(id))).toEqual([10_000n, 10_000n, 10_000n, 9_000n]);
    expect(chain.tokenBalances.get(FUNDING)).toBe(1_000_770n);
  });

  it('logs one line for each transfer, with its transaction', async () => {
    await setUp();
    chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_540n);

    await reset();

    expect(lines).toEqual([`${PROVIDER}  returned 540 to ${FUNDING}  tx ${chain.writes[0]!.txHash}`]);
  });

  it('transfers nothing the second time in a row', async () => {
    await setUp();
    chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_540n);
    chain.register(buyer(12), 10_090n);
    await reset();
    const writes = chain.writes.length;
    lines = [];

    const returned = await reset();

    expect(returned).toEqual([]);
    expect(chain.writes).toHaveLength(writes);
    expect(lines).toEqual(['nothing to do']);
  });

  it('brings each account back to its own configured amount', async () => {
    config = testConfig({ credentialsDir: dir, buyerBudget: 5_000n, providerBonusFunds: 20_000n });
    await setUp();
    chain.register(PROVIDER, 20_500n);
    chain.register(buyer(1), 5_001n);
    chain.register(buyer(2), 10_000n);

    await reset();

    expect([PROVIDER, buyer(1), buyer(2)].map((id) => chain.tokenBalances.get(id))).toEqual([20_000n, 5_000n, 5_000n]);
  });

  it('leaves the funding account, the pools contract and the relayer as they are', async () => {
    await setUp();
    // Money an unresolved pool still holds, and tokens sent to the relayer.
    chain.register(POOLS, 50_000n);
    await account(RELAYER, 7n);

    expect(await reset()).toEqual([]);
    expect(chain.writes).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('reads no key file for an account that holds no more than its amount', async () => {
    await setUp();
    await rm(keyFilePath(dir, config.network, buyer(7)));
    chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_001n);

    expect(await reset()).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('stops with KeyFileError when an account to send from has no key file', async () => {
    await setUp();
    await rm(keyFilePath(dir, config.network, buyer(4)));
    chain.register(buyer(4), 10_400n);

    await expect(reset()).rejects.toMatchObject({ constructor: KeyFileError, problem: 'missing' });
    expect(chain.writes).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('says, when a transfer got no result, that reset can be run again once that transaction is final', async () => {
    await setUp();
    chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_540n);
    const unknown = new OutcomeUnknownError('a transaction from provider to token may have been sent, but the RPC gave no result (timeout): it may still run', null, 'timeout');
    chain.failWrite(() => true, unknown);

    const rejected = await reset().catch((e: unknown) => e);

    expect(rejected).toBeInstanceOf(OutcomeUnknownError);
    expect(rejected).toMatchObject({ txHash: null, cause: unknown });
    expect((rejected as Error).message).toBe(
      `${unknown.message}. Reset is idempotent: run it again once that transaction is final, and it sends only what is still above the amounts.`,
    );
  });

  it('checks the RPC’s chain against QUORUM_NETWORK before sending anything', async () => {
    await setUp();
    chain.register(PROVIDER, 10_540n);
    chain.nodeChainId = 'mainnet';

    await expect(reset()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ConfigError);
    expect(chain.writes).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

The command line's tests, in full: they gain the `runReset` stub of `stubModules`, the rows
`[['reset'], { name: 'reset' }]`, `[['reset', 'all'], 'swarm reset']` and `['reset']` of three
`it.each` tables, `reset` in the `USAGE` name list, and the test
`reset runs runReset on the chain, its lines on stdout`.

`apps/swarm/test/main.test.ts`:

```typescript
import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { keyFilePath, writeKeyFile, type BuyerChainReads, type Env, type PoolReads } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { KeyPair } from 'near-api-js';
import { describe, expect, it, vi, type Mock } from 'vitest';
import type { AgentRuntime, BuyerOutcome } from '../src/buyer-agent.ts';
import type { Baseline, CheckReport } from '../src/check.ts';
import { aclNotice, EnvFileExistsError } from '../src/env-files.ts';
import { parseCommand, runCli, USAGE, UsageError, type Cli, type Connections, type SwarmModules } from '../src/main.ts';
import { PROFILES, profileAccount } from '../src/profiles.ts';
import { openPool, PoolAlreadyOpenError } from '../src/provider.ts';
import { runSwarm, SeatPriceMismatchError } from '../src/run.ts';
import { ShortfallError } from '../src/setup.ts';
import { FakeChain, PARENT, POOLS, poolView, PROVIDER } from './fake-chain.ts';

const MAIN = fileURLToPath(new URL('../src/main.ts', import.meta.url));
const GATEWAY_ENV = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../gateway/.env', import.meta.url));
const MCP_ENV = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../mcp/.env', import.meta.url));
/** A valid configuration whose scenario overrides show in the scenario each command is given. */
const ENV: Env = { QUORUM_PARENT_ACCOUNT: PARENT, QUORUM_SCENARIO_DEADLINE_SECONDS: '45', QUORUM_SWARM_SPREAD_SECONDS: '9' };
const BASELINE: Baseline = new Map([[PROVIDER, 10_000n]]);
const OPENED_POOL = 7;

function report(oks: readonly boolean[]): CheckReport {
  const lines = oks.map((ok, i) => ({ name: `check ${i}`, ok, detail: '' }));
  return { poolId: OPENED_POOL, status: 'settled', lines, failed: oks.includes(false) };
}

type StubModules = { [K in keyof SwarmModules]: Mock<SwarmModules[K]> };

/** Modules that record the order they are called in and answer as a successful run would. */
function stubModules(order: string[]): StubModules {
  return {
    runSetup: vi.fn<SwarmModules['runSetup']>(async () => {
      order.push('setup');
      return { actions: [] };
    }),
    snapshot: vi.fn<SwarmModules['snapshot']>(async () => {
      order.push('snapshot');
      return BASELINE;
    }),
    openPool: vi.fn<SwarmModules['openPool']>(async () => {
      order.push('open');
      return { poolId: OPENED_POOL, txHash: 'OpenTxHash', deadlineMs: 1_800_000_000_000 };
    }),
    runSwarm: vi.fn<SwarmModules['runSwarm']>(async () => {
      order.push('run');
      return [];
    }),
    checkPool: vi.fn<SwarmModules['checkPool']>(async () => {
      order.push('check');
      return report([true, true]);
    }),
    runReset: vi.fn<SwarmModules['runReset']>(async () => {
      order.push('reset');
      return [];
    }),
    writeGatewayEnv: vi.fn<SwarmModules['writeGatewayEnv']>(async () => {
      order.push('env gateway');
    }),
    writeMcpEnv: vi.fn<SwarmModules['writeMcpEnv']>(async () => {
      order.push('env mcp');
    }),
  };
}

const unused = (): never => {
  throw new Error('not used by the CLI itself');
};

function harness(env: Env = ENV) {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const err: string[] = [];
  const order: string[] = [];
  const chain = new FakeChain();
  const gateway: Connections['gateway'] = { pools: unused, offer: unused, pay: unused, redeem: unused, activity: unused };
  const buyerChain: BuyerChainReads = { nextNonce: unused, finalHeight: unused };
  const pools: PoolReads = { getPool: unused };
  const runtime: AgentRuntime = { now: () => 1_234, sleep: vi.fn(async () => {}), random: () => 0.5 };
  const modules = stubModules(order);
  const connect = vi.fn<Cli['connect']>(() => ({ chain, gateway, buyerChain, pools }));
  const cli: Cli = {
    env,
    out: (line) => out.push(line),
    err: (line) => err.push(line),
    connect,
    runtime,
    modules,
    platform: 'linux',
    userName: () => 'ada',
  };
  return { cli, out, err, order, chain, gateway, buyerChain, pools, runtime, modules, connect };
}

describe('parseCommand', () => {
  it.each([
    [['setup'], { name: 'setup' }],
    [['open', 'fills'], { name: 'open', scenario: 'fills' }],
    [['open', 'fails'], { name: 'open', scenario: 'fails' }],
    [['run', '0', 'fills'], { name: 'run', poolId: 0, scenario: 'fills' }],
    [['run', '9007199254740991', 'fails'], { name: 'run', poolId: 9_007_199_254_740_991, scenario: 'fails' }],
    [['check', '12', 'fails'], { name: 'check', poolId: 12, scenario: 'fails' }],
    [['demo', 'fills'], { name: 'demo', scenario: 'fills' }],
    [['env', 'gateway'], { name: 'env', app: 'gateway' }],
    [['env', 'mcp'], { name: 'env', app: 'mcp' }],
    [['reset'], { name: 'reset' }],
    [['help'], { name: 'help' }],
    [['--help'], { name: 'help' }],
    [['-h'], { name: 'help' }],
  ])('reads %j', (argv, command) => {
    expect(parseCommand(argv)).toEqual(command);
  });

  it.each([
    [[], 'no command'],
    [['deploy'], '"deploy"'],
    [['Setup'], '"Setup"'],
    [['setup', 'now'], 'swarm setup'],
    [['reset', 'all'], 'swarm reset'],
    [['help', 'open'], 'swarm help'],
    [['open'], 'swarm open <fills|fails>'],
    [['open', 'fills', 'fails'], 'swarm open <fills|fails>'],
    [['run', 'fills'], 'swarm run <pool-id> <fills|fails>'],
    [['check', '1'], 'swarm check <pool-id> <fills|fails>'],
    [['demo'], 'swarm demo <fills|fails>'],
    [['env'], 'swarm env <gateway|mcp>'],
  ])('refuses %j, naming what is wrong', (argv, named) => {
    expect(() => parseCommand(argv)).toThrow(UsageError);
    expect(() => parseCommand(argv)).toThrow(named);
  });

  it.each(['both', 'Fills', 'toString', ''])('refuses the scenario %j', (name) => {
    expect(() => parseCommand(['open', name])).toThrow(UsageError);
    expect(() => parseCommand(['demo', name])).toThrow(JSON.stringify(name));
  });

  it.each(['-1', '01', '1.5', '1e3', ' 1', '0x1', '', '9007199254740992'])('refuses the pool id %j', (id) => {
    expect(() => parseCommand(['run', id, 'fills'])).toThrow(UsageError);
    expect(() => parseCommand(['check', id, 'fills'])).toThrow(JSON.stringify(id));
  });

  it.each(['web', 'swarm', 'constructor'])('refuses the app %j', (app) => {
    expect(() => parseCommand(['env', app])).toThrow(UsageError);
    expect(() => parseCommand(['env', app])).toThrow(JSON.stringify(app));
  });

  it('is what USAGE lists, command by command', () => {
    for (const name of ['setup', 'open', 'run', 'check', 'demo', 'env', 'reset', 'help']) {
      expect(USAGE).toMatch(new RegExp(`^  ${name}\\b`, 'm'));
    }
  });

  it('says in USAGE that run resumes a pool, buying nothing more for a buyer that holds seats', () => {
    expect(USAGE).toMatch(/^ {2}run <pool-id> <fills\|fails> +run the 20 scripted buyers against the pool, or resume them on it$/m);
    expect(USAGE).toMatch(/^swarm run on a pool that buyers have paid in resumes them: .*\s+.*a buyer that holds seats in the pool follows them and never buys again\.$/m);
  });
});

describe('runCli: usage', () => {

    expect(h.out).toEqual([]);

    expect(h.order).toEqual([]);

  it('exits 2 with no command at all', async () => {

    expect(await runCli([], h.cli)).toBe(2);

});

    expect(written).toBe(path);
    expect(h.order).toEqual([`env ${app}`]);
    expect(h.out).toEqual([`wrote ${path}`]);
    expect(h.connect).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("env gateway on Windows adds a line giving the icacls command that restricts the file to the user", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.cli.platform = 'win32';
    h.cli.userName = () => 'Ada Lovelace';
    expect(await runCli(['env', 'gateway'], h.cli)).toBe(0);
    expect(h.out).toEqual([`wrote ${GATEWAY_ENV}`, aclNotice(GATEWAY_ENV, 'win32', 'Ada Lovelace')]);
    expect(h.out[1]).toContain(`icacls "${GATEWAY_ENV}" /inheritance:r /grant:r "Ada Lovelace:F"`);
  });

  it('env mcp on Windows writes no such line: the file holds no key', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.cli.platform = 'win32';
    expect(await runCli(['env', 'mcp'], h.cli)).toBe(0);
    expect(h.out).toEqual([`wrote ${MCP_ENV}`]);
  });

  it('env exits 1 with the refusal when the file exists', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.writeMcpEnv.mockRejectedValue(new EnvFileExistsError(MCP_ENV));
    expect(await runCli(['env', 'mcp'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual([new EnvFileExistsError(MCP_ENV).message]);
    expect(h.out).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/**
 * The outcomes of a run of `name` that went as it expects (each buyer at or above its seat price
 * holds its seats with a credential in fills or its refund in fails; the others declined), with
 * `changes` applied to the outcome at each index.
 */
function runOutcomes(name: 'fills' | 'fails', changes: Record<number, Partial<BuyerOutcome>> = {}): BuyerOutcome[] {
  const seatPrice = name === 'fills' ? 180n : 320n;
  return PROFILES.map((profile, i) => {
    const buyer = profileAccount(profile, PARENT);
    const accepts = profile.topPrice >= seatPrice;
    const outcome: BuyerOutcome = accepts
      ? { buyer, kind: name === 'fills' ? 'credential' : 'refunded', seats: profile.seats, paid: 0n, detail: 'as expected', txHashes: [] }
      : { buyer, kind: 'declined', seats: 0, paid: 0n, detail: 'seat price above top price', txHashes: [] };
    return { ...outcome, ...changes[i] };
  });
}

describe("runCli: the buyers' outcomes", () => {
  it('demo exits 1 when a buyer that accepts the price did not end as the scenario expects, naming it on stderr after the verdict', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(runOutcomes('fails', { 2: { kind: 'failed', seats: 0, detail: 'relay failed' } }));
    expect(await runCli(['demo', 'fails'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.out.at(-1)).toBe('pool 7: 2 checks passed');
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['buyer-03 ended failed with 0 seats (relay failed); fails expects refunded']);
  });

  it('demo exits 1 when a buyer that accepts the price declined the offer', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(runOutcomes('fills', { 0: { kind: 'declined', seats: 0, detail: 'offer refused: wrong_pay_to' } }));
    expect(await runCli(['demo', 'fills'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['buyer-01 ended declined with 0 seats (offer refused: wrong_pay_to); fills expects credential or missed']);
  });

  it('demo exits 1 when a buyer whose top price is below the seat price holds seats', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(runOutcomes('fails', { 6: { kind: 'refunded', seats: 18, detail: '6300 back, bonus 540' } }));
    expect(await runCli(['demo', 'fails'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual([
      'buyer-07 ended refunded with 18 seats (6300 back, bonus 540); fails expects no seats, its top price 250 being below the seat price 320',
    ]);
  });

  it('demo exits 0 when a buyer of fills missed the pool and every other buyer ended as expected', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(runOutcomes('fills', { 13: { kind: 'missed', seats: 0 }, 16: { kind: 'missed' } }));
    expect(await runCli(['demo', 'fills'], h.cli)).toBe(0);
    expect(h.err).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('demo prints both a failed check and each unexpected outcome, and exits 1', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.checkPool.mockResolvedValue(report([true, false]));
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(runOutcomes('fills', { 3: { kind: 'timed_out' }, 4: { kind: 'refused', seats: 0, detail: 'payment refused: expired' } }));
    expect(await runCli(['demo', 'fills'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual([
      'pool 7: 1 of 2 checks failed',
      'buyer-04 ended timed_out with 16 seats (as expected); fills expects credential or missed',
      'buyer-05 ended refused with 0 seats (payment refused: expired); fills expects credential or missed',
    ]);
  });

  it('demo gives the check every transaction its buyers learned, as commits the feed may lack', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const outcomes = runOutcomes('fills', { 0: { txHashes: ['Commit1'] }, 3: { txHashes: ['Unknown4', 'Commit4'] } });
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(outcomes);
    await runCli(['demo', 'fills'], h.cli);
    const [, , request] = h.modules.checkPool.mock.calls[0] ?? [];
    expect(request?.extraCommits).toEqual([
      { account: outcomes[0]?.buyer, txHash: 'Commit1' },
      { account: outcomes[3]?.buyer, txHash: 'Unknown4' },
      { account: outcomes[3]?.buyer, txHash: 'Commit4' },
    ]);
  });

  it('run exits 1 when a buyer did not end as the scenario expects, naming it on stderr', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(runOutcomes('fails', { 5: { kind: 'claimable', detail: '3500 to claim, bonus 300' } }));
    expect(await runCli(['run', '3', 'fails'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['buyer-06 ended claimable with 10 seats (3500 to claim, bonus 300); fails expects refunded']);
  });

  it('run exits 0 when every buyer ended as the scenario expects', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.runSwarm.mockResolvedValue(runOutcomes('fills'));
    expect(await runCli(['run', '3', 'fills'], h.cli)).toBe(0);
    expect(h.err).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('says in USAGE which buyer outcomes make run and demo exit 1', () => {
    expect(USAGE).toContain('run and demo also exit with 1 when a buyer did not end as the scenario expects');
  });
});

describe('runCli: errors', () => {
  it("prints an error's message and its cause's, never a stack", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const error = new Error('fetch failed', { cause: new Error('connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8402') });
    h.modules.runSetup.mockRejectedValue(error);
    expect(await runCli(['setup'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['fetch failed (connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8402)']);
  });

  it('names every address of a refused connection whose cause has no message of its own', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const refused = new AggregateError([new Error('connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:8402'), new Error('connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8402')], '');
    h.modules.runSetup.mockRejectedValue(new Error('fetch failed', { cause: refused }));
    expect(await runCli(['setup'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['fetch failed (connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:8402; connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8402)']);
  });

  it('gives the message of a cause that groups errors, then what each of its errors says', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const grouped = new AggregateError([new Error('first try'), new Error('second try')], 'every try failed');
    h.modules.runSetup.mockRejectedValue(new Error('cannot set up', { cause: grouped }));
    expect(await runCli(['setup'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['cannot set up (every try failed (first try; second try))']);
  });

  it('follows every cause of the chain, not only the first', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const error = new Error('cannot read the pool', { cause: new Error('fetch failed', { cause: new Error('connect ECONNRESET') }) });
    h.modules.runSetup.mockRejectedValue(error);
    expect(await runCli(['setup'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['cannot read the pool (fetch failed (connect ECONNRESET))']);
  });

  it('writes QUORUM_RPC_URL in place of the RPC URL, which may hold an API key, in an error and its causes', async () => {
    const rpcUrl = 'https://rpc.example.org/v1?apiKey=SECRET';
    const h = harness({ ...ENV, QUORUM_RPC_URL: rpcUrl });
    const cause = new Error(`${rpcUrl} answered 502 Bad Gateway`);
    h.modules.runSetup.mockRejectedValue(new Error(`could not read from ${rpcUrl}`, { cause }));
    expect(await runCli(['setup'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['could not read from QUORUM_RPC_URL (QUORUM_RPC_URL answered 502 Bad Gateway)']);
    expect(h.err.join('\n')).not.toContain('SECRET');
  });

  it('prints a thrown value that is not an Error as it is', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.modules.runSetup.mockImplementation(() => Promise.reject('stopped'));
    expect(await runCli(['setup'], h.cli)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.err).toEqual(['stopped']);
  });
});

interface Run {
  code: number | null;
  stdout: string;
  stderr: string;
}

/** Runs `node src/main.ts <args>` with `env` added to this process's environment. */
function runMain(args: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<Run> {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = execFile(process.execPath, [MAIN, ...args], { env: { ...process.env, ...env }, timeout: 30_000 }, (_, stdout, stderr) =>
      resolve({ code: child.exitCode, stdout, stderr }),
    );
  });
}

describe('main, as a process', () => {
  it('exits 2 with the usage on stderr for an unknown command', async () => {
    const { code, stdout, stderr } = await runMain(['deploy']);
    expect(code).toBe(2);
    expect(stdout).toBe('');
    expect(stderr).toContain(USAGE);
  });

  it('exits 0 with the usage on stdout for help', async () => {
    const { code, stdout } = await runMain(['help']);
    expect(code).toBe(0);
    expect(stdout).toBe(`${USAGE}\n`);
  });

  it('exits 1 on an invalid configuration, which the environment sets over apps/swarm/.env', async () => {
    const { code, stdout, stderr } = await runMain(['setup'], { QUORUM_NETWORK: 'near:mainnet' });
    expect(code).toBe(1);
    expect(stdout).toBe('');
    expect(stderr).toContain('QUORUM_NETWORK must be near:testnet or near:sandbox, got "near:mainnet"');
  });
});
```

The swarm's sandbox suite, in full: it gains the `runReset` import and the test
`brings every buyer and the provider back to its token amount with reset then setup, and a second reset sends nothing`,
which runs between the second setup in a row and the last test.

`apps/swarm/test/sandbox/demo.test.ts`:

```typescript
// The swarm end to end, against a local sandbox and the real gateway running as a child process:
// setup stopping on the token shortfall and then completing, the `fills` scenario run in this
// process, the `fails` scenario run through the command line, a second setup in a row that sends
// nothing, and reset. Needs Linux or macOS (near-sandbox ships no Windows binary, so on Windows the
// suite is skipped) and the wasm files from `cargo near build`, named by QUORUM_POOLS_WASM and
// QUORUM_MOCK_USD_WASM; without them the suite fails. The tests run in order, each on the state the
// previous ones left; the last one checks that the sandbox still holds the first setup's transactions.
// Figures worth comparing between runs (durations, NEAR spent, gas) are printed.
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { setTimeout as delay } from 'node:timers/promises';
import { RpcPoolReads } from '@quorum-on-near/buyer';
import { JsonRpcProvider, yoctoToNear } from 'near-api-js';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { buyerIds } from '../../src/accounts.ts';
import type { BuyerOutcome, BuyerOutcomeKind } from '../../src/buyer-agent.ts';
import { TGAS } from '../../src/chain.ts';
import { checkPool, commitGas, payoutGas, snapshot } from '../../src/check.ts';
import { PROFILES } from '../../src/profiles.ts';
import { openPool } from '../../src/provider.ts';
import { runReset } from '../../src/reset.ts';
import { runSwarm } from '../../src/run.ts';
import { scenario } from '../../src/scenarios.ts';
import { ShortfallError } from '../../src/setup.ts';
import { recordSetup, runSwarmCli, startSwarmWorld, type SetupRun, type SwarmWorld } from './harness.ts';

const TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000;
/** The start's limit: a sandbox, the token, two setups that create and fund 25 accounts, and the gateway. */
const START_TIMEOUT_MS = 900_000;
/** `swarm demo fails` waits for the pool's deadline, then for the keeper's refund; the check gives up 5 minutes after the deadline. */
const CLI_TIMEOUT_MS = 540_000;
/** The scripted buyers that accept the `fills` price, 180 (their top price is 400 or 250): buyer-01 to buyer-14. */
const FILLS_ACCEPTING = 14;

/** How many outcomes there are of each kind, in the order the kinds first appear. */
function kinds(outcomes: readonly BuyerOutcome[]): Record<string, number> {
  const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const { kind } of outcomes) counts[kind] = (counts[kind] ?? 0) + 1;
  return counts;
}

function near(yocto: bigint): string {
  return `${yoctoToNear(yocto)} NEAR`;
}

function tgas(gas: bigint): string {
  return (Number(gas) / Number(TGAS)).toFixed(2);
}

/** The least, the most and the mean of some gas figures, in Tgas. */
function gasRange(figures: readonly bigint[]): string {
  if (figures.length === 0) return 'none';
  const sorted = [...figures].sort((a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));
  const total = figures.reduce((sum, gas) => sum + gas, 0n);
  const least = sorted[0] ?? 0n;
  const most = sorted.at(-1) ?? 0n;
  return `${figures.length}, ${tgas(least)} to ${tgas(most)}, mean ${tgas(total / BigInt(figures.length))}`;
}

/** Prints what a setup run did and logged, and what it cost the parent. */
function logSetup(name: string, run: SetupRun): void {
  const ended = run.error === null ? 'completed' : `stopped: ${(run.error as Error).message}`;
  console.log(
    `${name}: ${run.writes} writes in ${run.ms} ms, the parent spent ${near(run.parentBefore - run.parentAfter)}; ${ended}`,
  );
  for (const line of run.lines) console.log(`  ${line}`);
}

// near-sandbox ships no Windows binary.
describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')('the swarm against a local sandbox and the real gateway', { timeout: TIMEOUT_MS }, () => {
  // Set by beforeAll; afterAll may find it unset if the start failed.
  let world: SwarmWorld | undefined;

  /** The world, which beforeAll started. */
  const started = (): SwarmWorld => {
    if (world === undefined) throw new Error('the world did not start');
    return world;
  };

  /**
   * Prints the gas each transaction of the pool's activity feed burnt, read with the relayer as
   * signer: each relayed commit's own receipts (commitGas) and its whole transaction, and each payout
   * `ft_transfer` and callback of the keeper's calls (payoutGas).
   */
  const logGas = async (poolId: number): Promise<void> => {
    const { config, chain, gatewayClient } = started();
    const commits: bigint[] = [];
    const relayed: bigint[] = [];
    const transfers: bigint[] = [];
    const callbacks: bigint[] = [];
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    for (const record of await gatewayClient.activity(poolId)) {
      if (seen.has(record.txHash)) continue;
      seen.add(record.txHash);
      const outcome = await chain.txOutcome(record.txHash, config.relayer);
      if (outcome === null) continue;
      if (record.kind === 'commit') {
        const gas = commitGas(outcome, record.account, [config.token, config.poolsContract]);
        if (gas !== null) commits.push(gas);
        relayed.push(outcome.receipts.reduce((sum, receipt) => sum + receipt.gasBurnt, 0n));
      } else {
        const gas = payoutGas(outcome, config.poolsContract, config.token);
        transfers.push(...gas.transfers);
        callbacks.push(...gas.callbacks);
      }
    }
    console.log(`pool ${poolId} gas in Tgas (count, least to most, mean):`);
    console.log(`  commit receipts:        ${gasRange(commits)}`);
    console.log(`  whole relayed commit:   ${gasRange(relayed)}`);
    console.log(`  payout ft_transfer:     ${gasRange(transfers)}`);
    console.log(`  payout callback:        ${gasRange(callbacks)}`);
  };

  beforeAll(async () => {
    world = await startSwarmWorld();
    for (const { step, ms } of world.timings) console.log(`start: ${step} took ${ms} ms`);
    const [first, second] = world.setupRuns;
    logSetup('first setup', first);
    logSetup('second setup', second);
  }, START_TIMEOUT_MS);

  afterAll(async () => {
    if (world === undefined) return;
    const stderr = await readFile(world.gateway.stderrPath, 'utf8');
    console.log(`the gateway's standard error:${stderr === '' ? ' empty' : `\n${stderr}`}`);
    await world.stop();
  }, TIMEOUT_MS);

  it('stops the first setup on the token shortfall once it has created and registered the funding account, and completes the second once the funding account holds the token', async () => {
    const { config, chain, setupRuns } = started();
    const [first, second] = setupRuns;
    const { funding } = config;

    expect(first.error).toBeInstanceOf(ShortfallError);
    expect(first.error).toMatchObject({
      problem: 'token_shortfall',
      account: funding,
      // Nothing held yet: the whole amount of each of the 21 buyers and the provider.
      shortfall: 21n * config.buyerBudget + config.providerBonusFunds,
    });
    expect((first.error as Error).message).toContain(funding);
    expect(first.lines).toContainEqual(expect.stringMatching(new RegExp(`^created {2}${funding.replaceAll('.', '\\.')} {2}`)));
    expect(first.lines.some((line) => line.startsWith('registered on the token') && line.includes(funding))).toBe(true);
    expect(first.lines.some((line) => line.startsWith('sent tokens'))).toBe(false);

    expect(second.error).toBeNull();
    expect(second.lines.some((line) => line.startsWith('sent tokens'))).toBe(true);
    expect(await chain.isRegistered(funding)).toBe(true);
    for (const id of buyerIds(config)) expect(await chain.ftBalanceOf(id)).toBe(config.buyerBudget);
    expect(await chain.ftBalanceOf(config.provider)).toBe(config.providerBonusFunds);
  });

  it('fills the fills pool: buyers 15 to 20 decline it or find it full, the others take its 192 seats, it settles, and every check passes', async () => {
    const { config, chain, gatewayClient, buyerChain } = started();
    const fills = scenario('fills', config);
    const log = (line: string): void => console.log(line);
    const relayerBefore = (await chain.account(config.relayer))?.balance ?? 0n;
    const blockBefore = await chain.finalBlock();

    let start = performance.now();
    const baseline = await snapshot(config, chain);
    const { poolId } = await openPool(config, { chain, log }, fills);
    const opened = performance.now() - start;
    start = performance.now();
    const pools = new RpcPoolReads(new JsonRpcProvider({ url: config.rpcUrl }), config.poolsContract);
    const outcomes = await runSwarm(config, { gateway: gatewayClient, chain: buyerChain, pools, log }, poolId, fills);
    const ran = performance.now() - start;
    start = performance.now();
    const checkDeps = { chain, gateway: gatewayClient, now: Date.now, sleep: (ms: number) => delay(ms), log };
    // As swarm demo does: a commit whose result was unknown is missing from the feed, but its buyer may have learned it.
    const extraCommits = outcomes.flatMap(({ buyer, txHashes }) => txHashes.map((txHash) => ({ account: buyer, txHash })));
    const report = await checkPool(config, checkDeps, { poolId, scenario: fills, baseline, extraCommits });
    const checked = performance.now() - start;

    const relayerAfter = (await chain.account(config.relayer))?.balance ?? 0n;
    const blockAfter = await chain.finalBlock();
    const blocks = Number(blockAfter.height - blockBefore.height);
    const blockMs = blocks === 0 ? 0 : Math.round((blockAfter.timestampMs - blockBefore.timestampMs) / blocks);
    console.log(`fills: open ${Math.round(opened)} ms, run ${Math.round(ran)} ms, check ${Math.round(checked)} ms`);
    console.log(`fills: ${blocks} blocks went by, one every ${blockMs} ms of block time`);
    console.log(`fills outcomes: ${JSON.stringify(kinds(outcomes))}`);
    console.log(`fills: the relayer spent ${near(relayerBefore - relayerAfter)}`);
    await logGas(poolId);

    expect(report.failed).toBe(false);
    expect(report.status).toBe('settled');
    // A buyer arriving once the pool is full no longer finds it listed, so it learns it missed the
    // pool without seeing its price; one arriving as it fills takes what is left.
    const missedFull = /^no seat left \(pool (filled|settled)\)$/;
    for (const outcome of outcomes.slice(FILLS_ACCEPTING)) {
      if (outcome.kind !== 'declined') expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ kind: 'missed', detail: expect.stringMatching(missedFull) });
      expect(outcome.seats).toBe(0);
    }
    const accepting = outcomes.slice(0, FILLS_ACCEPTING);
    for (const [i, outcome] of accepting.entries()) {
      const wanted = PROFILES[i]?.seats ?? 0;
      expect<BuyerOutcomeKind[]>(['credential', 'missed']).toContain(outcome.kind);
      if (outcome.kind === 'credential') {
        expect(outcome.seats).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        expect(outcome.seats).toBeLessThanOrEqual(wanted);
      } else {
        expect(outcome.seats).toBe(0);
      }
    }
    // They want 200 seats between them, so 8 go unsold to the last to arrive.
    expect(accepting.reduce((sum, outcome) => sum + outcome.seats, 0)).toBe(fills.target);
  });

  it('fails the fails pool through the command line: `swarm demo fails` exits 0, every check is ok and the pool is refunded', async () => {
    const run = started();
    const start = performance.now();

    const result = await runSwarmCli(run, ['demo', 'fails'], { timeoutMs: CLI_TIMEOUT_MS });

    console.log(`swarm demo fails: exit ${result.code} after ${Math.round(performance.now() - start)} ms`);
    console.log(`its standard output:\n${result.stdout}`);
    console.log(`its standard error:${result.stderr === '' ? ' empty' : `\n${result.stderr}`}`);
    const opened = /^opened pool (\d+) \(fails\)/m.exec(result.stdout);
    if (opened?.[1] !== undefined) await logGas(Number(opened[1]));

    expect(result.code).toBe(0);
    const checks = result.stdout.split('\n').filter((line) => /^(ok {2}|FAIL) {2}/.test(line));
    expect(checks.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(checks.filter((line) => line.startsWith('FAIL'))).toEqual([]);
    expect(result.stdout).toMatch(/^ok {4}status: refunded, as fails expects$/m);
    // Buyers 01 to 06 accept 320 a seat and take 100 seats; the others' top prices are below it.
    expect(result.stdout).toMatch(/^100 seats, 32000 paid: refunded 6, declined 14$/m);
    // Each names the keeper's refund transaction, which the gateway records once the call has finished.
    const refunds = result.stdout.split('\n').filter((line) => /^buyer-\d\d {2}refunded: /.test(line));
    expect(refunds).toHaveLength(6);
    for (const line of refunds) expect(line).toMatch(/ {2}tx [1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/);
  });

  it('sends nothing on the second of two setups in a row', async () => {
    const { config, chain } = started();
    const log = (line: string): void => console.log(line);

    const first = await recordSetup(config, chain, log);
    const second = await recordSetup(config, chain, log);

    logSetup('setup after the scenarios', first);
    logSetup('setup again', second);
    expect(first.error).toBeNull();
    expect(second.error).toBeNull();
    expect(second.writes).toBe(0);
    expect(second.report?.actions).toEqual([]);
    expect(second.lines).toEqual(['nothing to do']);
  });

  it('brings every buyer and the provider back to its token amount with reset then setup, and a second reset sends nothing', async () => {
    const { config, chain } = started();
    const log = (line: string): void => console.log(line);

    const returned = await runReset(config, { chain, log });
    const setup = await recordSetup(config, chain, log);
    const writes = chain.writes.length;
    const again = await runReset(config, { chain, log });

    logSetup('setup after reset', setup);
    // The provider earned the fills pool's sales; buyers 01 to 06 earned the fails pool's bonus.
    const buyers = buyerIds(config);
    expect(returned.map((surplus) => surplus.accountId)).toEqual([config.provider, ...buyers.slice(0, 6)]);
    expect(setup.error).toBeNull();
    for (const id of buyers) expect(await chain.ftBalanceOf(id)).toBe(config.buyerBudget);
    expect(await chain.ftBalanceOf(config.provider)).toBe(config.providerBonusFunds);
    expect(again).toEqual([]);
    expect(chain.writes.length).toBe(writes);
  });

  it("still knows the first setup's first transaction once every scenario has run, minutes later", async () => {
    const { config, chain, setupRuns } = started();
    const created = setupRuns[0].lines.find((line) => line.startsWith('created  '));
    const txHash = created?.match(/ tx (\S+)$/)?.[1];
    if (txHash === undefined) throw new Error('the first setup logged no account it created');

    expect(await chain.txOutcome(txHash, config.parent)).not.toBeNull();
  });
});
```
